They are not queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations Optional.

Number of seconds allowed for this object to gracefully terminate before it will be removed from the system. Only set when deletionTimestamp is also set. May only be shortened. Read-only. Optional.

Must be empty before the object is deleted from the registry. Each entry is an identifier for the responsible component that will remove the entry from the list. If the deletionTimestamp of the object is non-nil, entries in this list can only be removed. Finalizers may be processed and removed in any order. Order is NOT enforced because it introduces significant risk of stuck finalizers. finalizers is a shared field, any actor with permission can reorder it. If the finalizer list is processed in order, then this can lead to a situation in which the component responsible for the first finalizer in the list is waiting for a signal (field value, external system, or other) produced by a component responsible for a finalizer later in the list, resulting in a deadlock. Without enforced ordering finalizers are free to order amongst themselves and are not vulnerable to ordering changes in the list. Optional.

GenerateName is an optional prefix, used by the server, to generate a unique name ONLY IF the Name field has not been provided. If this field is used, the name returned to the client will be different than the name passed. This value will also be combined with a unique suffix. The provided value has the same validation rules as the Name field, and may be truncated by the length of the suffix required to make the value unique on the server. If this field is specified and the generated name exists, the server will return a 409. Applied only if Name is not specified. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#idempotency Optional.
A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state. Populated by the system. Read-only. Optional.

Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) objects. May match selectors of replication controllers and services. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels Optional.

ManagedFields maps workflow-id and version to the set of fields that are managed by that workflow. This is mostly for internal housekeeping, and users typically shouldn't need to set or understand this field. A workflow can be the user's name, a controller's name, or the name of a specific apply path like "ci-cd". The set of fields is always in the version that the workflow used when modifying the object. Optional.
The API version used to manage the fields in this managedFields entry. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The type of the fields field. Currently only 'FieldsV1' is supported. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

fields_v1 is the Kubernetes fieldsV1 field, which contains a JSON representation of the fields managed by this entry. It stores a set of field paths and their ownership information used for server-side apply conflict detection. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the manager (entity, such as a controller or user) that last applied or updated the managed fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Operation is the type of operation that last modified the field, such as 'Update' or 'Apply'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The subresource of the resource that this managed field entry applies to, such as 'status' or 'scale'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Time is the timestamp, in RFC3339 format, when the managed fields entry was last updated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Name must be unique within a namespace. Is required when creating resources, although some resources may allow a client to request the generation of an appropriate name automatically. Name is primarily intended for creation idempotence and configuration definition. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names#names Optional.

Namespace defines the space within which each name must be unique. An empty namespace is equivalent to the "default" namespace, but "default" is the canonical representation. Not all objects are required to be scoped to a namespace - the value of this field for those objects will be empty. Must be a DNS_LABEL. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/namespaces Optional.

List of objects depended by this object. If ALL objects in the list have been deleted, this object will be garbage collected. If this object is managed by a controller, then an entry in this list will point to this controller, with the controller field set to true. There cannot be more than one managing controller. Optional.
The API version of the referenced owner object, e.g. 'v1' or 'apps/v1'. This matches the apiVersion field of the owner's resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

If true, prevents deletion of the owner object if this dependent resource would prevent the owner's garbage collection. This is part of the standard Kubernetes OwnerReference schema and helps ensure safe deletion ordering. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the owner reference is the managing controller for the resource. This matches the `controller` field in Kubernetes OwnerReference, which is a boolean pointer (set to true when the owner is the primary controller). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The kind of the referenced owner resource, matching the API resource type for the owner (e.g., 'Deployment'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the owner object that this owner_reference points to. In Kubernetes, this matches the name of the referenced resource as defined in its metadata. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
UID of the referenced owner object. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

MutatingAdmissionPolicySpec defines the desired behavior of the admission policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

failurePolicy defines how to handle failures for the admission policy. Failures can occur from CEL expression parse errors, type check errors, runtime errors and invalid or mis-configured policy definitions or bindings. A policy is invalid if paramKind refers to a non-existent Kind. A binding is invalid if paramRef.name refers to a non-existent resource. failurePolicy does not define how validations that evaluate to false are handled. Allowed values are Ignore or Fail. Defaults to Fail. Optional.

matchConditions is a list of conditions that must be met for a request to be validated. Match conditions filter requests that have already been matched by the matchConstraints. An empty list of matchConditions matches all requests. There are a maximum of 64 match conditions allowed. If a parameter object is provided, it can be accessed via the `params` handle in the same manner as validation expressions. The exact matching logic is (in order): 1. If ANY matchCondition evaluates to FALSE, the policy is skipped. 2. If ALL matchConditions evaluate to TRUE, the policy is evaluated. 3. If any matchCondition evaluates to an error (but none are FALSE): - If failurePolicy=Fail, reject the request - If failurePolicy=Ignore, the policy is skipped Optional.

The Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that must evaluate to true for the admission policy to match the request. It is evaluated against the admission review object, with access to fields such as `request.object` and `request.userInfo`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the match condition, used to uniquely identify it within the list of match conditions for this admission policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

MatchResources decides whether to run the admission control policy on an object based on whether it meets the match criteria. The exclude rules take precedence over include rules (if a resource matches both, it is excluded) Optional.

excludeResourceRules describes what operations on what resources/subresources the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy should not care about. The exclude rules take precedence over include rules (if a resource matches both, it is excluded) Optional.
The API groups to which this resource rule applies. For example, 'apps', 'networking.k8s.io', or '*' to match all groups. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of API versions (e.g., 'v1', 'apps/v1') of the resources to which this exclude rule applies. Requests for resources with matching API versions are excluded from the admission policy's match constraints. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of operations (e.g., CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, CONNECT, or '*') to exclude from matching in this resource rule. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of specific resource names (e.g., 'my-nginx') that this rule applies to. When used in exclude_resource_rules, these names are excluded from the match constraints. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of Kubernetes resource names (e.g., 'pods', 'services') that are excluded from the match constraints. This field is used within exclude_resource_rules to define the resources to which the exclusion rule applies. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the scope of resources to which this exclude rule applies. Allowed values are 'Cluster', 'Namespaced', or '*' to match both. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

matchPolicy defines how the "MatchResources" list is used to match incoming requests. Allowed values are "Exact" or "Equivalent". - Exact: match a request only if it exactly matches a specified rule. For example, if deployments can be modified via apps/v1, apps/v1beta1, and extensions/v1beta1, but "rules" only included `apiGroups:["apps"], apiVersions:["v1"], resources: ["deployments"]`, a request to apps/v1beta1 or extensions/v1beta1 would not be sent to the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy. - Equivalent: match a request if modifies a resource listed in rules, even via another API group or version. For example, if deployments can be modified via apps/v1, apps/v1beta1, and extensions/v1beta1, and "rules" only included `apiGroups:["apps"], apiVersions:["v1"], resources: ["deployments"]`, a request to apps/v1beta1 or extensions/v1beta1 would be converted to apps/v1 and sent to the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy. Defaults to "Equivalent" Optional.

A label selector is a label query over a set of resources. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all objects. A null label selector matches no objects. Optional.
matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed. Optional.
The key of the label selector expression. This is the label key that the expression filters on, such as 'app' or 'environment'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values that the label key must match, as specified by the operator in this match expression. For example, if the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', these values provide the set to compare against; if the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed. Optional.

A label selector is a label query over a set of resources. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all objects. A null label selector matches no objects. Optional.
matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed. Optional.

The label key that this match expression applies to. In a Kubernetes LabelSelectorRequirement, the key is the label name that the operator and values are evaluated against. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the relationship between the label key and a set of values. Allowed values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values that must match the specified key and operator in the match expression. Required for operators `In` and `NotIn`; must be empty for `Exists` and `DoesNotExist`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed. Optional.
resourceRules describes what operations on what resources/subresources the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy matches. The policy cares about an operation if it matches _any_ Rule. Optional.

List of API groups that the resource belongs to. Use an empty string for the core API group (e.g., '') or '*' to match all API groups. For example, 'apps' for Deployments or 'batch' for Jobs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of API versions (e.g., 'v1', 'apps/v1') that the resource rule matches. The rule applies only to resources from these versions. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operations field lists the Kubernetes API operations (e.g., CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE) that the resource rule matches. Valid values are CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, CONNECT, or * to match all operations. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Optional list of specific resource names to match. If empty or omitted, the rule applies to all resources of the selected resource type. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The list of Kubernetes resource names (e.g., pods, deployments) that this resource rule applies to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the scope of the resources to match. Allowed values are '*' (all scopes), 'Cluster', or 'Namespaced'. Defaults to '*'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

mutations contain operations to perform on matching objects. mutations may not be empty; a minimum of one mutation is required. mutations are evaluated in order, and are reinvoked according to the reinvocationPolicy. The mutations of a policy are invoked for each binding of this policy and reinvocation of mutations occurs on a per binding basis. Optional.

Configures the mutation as an apply configuration operation, where the supplied configuration is applied to the object via server-side apply, merging with existing configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The expression is a Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that evaluates to a partial object to be applied to the request object. It is evaluated for each admission request, and the result is merged with the original object. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The JSON Patch to apply to the object as part of this mutation. It contains an expression that evaluates to a JSON Patch string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Expression is an optional CEL expression that computes the value for the JSON patch operation. It may reference fields of the object, and either this field or 'value' must be set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the type of patch to apply. Valid values are 'JSONPatch' and 'ApplyConfiguration'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
ParamKind is a tuple of Group Kind and Version. Optional.
apiVersion is the API group version the resources belong to. In format of "group/version". Required. Optional.
kind is the API kind the resources belong to. Required. Optional.

reinvocationPolicy indicates whether mutations may be called multiple times per MutatingAdmissionPolicyBinding as part of a single admission evaluation. Allowed values are "Never" and "IfNeeded". Never: These mutations will not be called more than once per binding in a single admission evaluation. IfNeeded: These mutations may be invoked more than once per binding for a single admission request and there is no guarantee of order with respect to other admission plugins, admission webhooks, bindings of this policy and admission policies. Mutations are only reinvoked when mutations change the object after this mutation is invoked. Required. Optional.

variables contain definitions of variables that can be used in composition of other expressions. Each variable is defined as a named CEL expression. The variables defined here will be available under `variables` in other expressions of the policy except matchConditions because matchConditions are evaluated before the rest of the policy. The expression of a variable can refer to other variables defined earlier in the list but not those after. Thus, variables must be sorted by the order of first appearance and acyclic. Optional.

The CEL (Common Expression Language) expression used to compute the value of this variable. It is evaluated in the context of the admission request and must return a value compatible with the declared variable type. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the variable in the admission policy. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., alphanumeric characters and underscores, not starting with a digit). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

failurePolicy defines how to handle failures for the admission policy. Failures can occur from CEL expression parse errors, type check errors, runtime errors and invalid or mis-configured policy definitions or bindings.

A policy is invalid if paramKind refers to a non-existent Kind. A binding is invalid if paramRef.name refers to a non-existent resource.

matchConditions is a list of conditions that must be met for a request to be validated. Match conditions filter requests that have already been matched by the matchConstraints. An empty list of matchConditions matches all requests. There are a maximum of 64 match conditions allowed.

If a parameter object is provided, it can be accessed via the `params` handle in the same manner as validation expressions.

The exact matching logic is (in order):
  1. If ANY matchCondition evaluates to FALSE, the policy is skipped.
  2. If ALL matchConditions evaluate to TRUE, the policy is evaluated.
  3. If any matchCondition evaluates to an error (but none are FALSE):
     - If failurePolicy=Fail, reject the request
     - If failurePolicy=Ignore, the policy is skipped

Configures the mutation as an apply configuration operation, where the supplied configuration is applied to the object via server-side apply, merging with existing configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The expression is a Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that evaluates to a partial object to be applied to the request object. It is evaluated for each admission request, and the result is merged with the original object. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The JSON Patch to apply to the object as part of this mutation. It contains an expression that evaluates to a JSON Patch string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Expression is an optional CEL expression that computes the value for the JSON patch operation. It may reference fields of the object, and either this field or 'value' must be set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the type of patch to apply. Valid values are 'JSONPatch' and 'ApplyConfiguration'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
ParamKind is a tuple of Group Kind and Version.
apiVersion is the API group version the resources belong to. In format of "group/version". Required.
kind is the API kind the resources belong to. Required.

reinvocationPolicy indicates whether mutations may be called multiple times per MutatingAdmissionPolicyBinding as part of a single admission evaluation. Allowed values are "Never" and "IfNeeded".

Never: These mutations will not be called more than once per binding in a single admission evaluation.

IfNeeded: These mutations may be invoked more than once per binding for a single admission request and there is no guarantee of order with respect to other admission plugins, admission webhooks, bindings of this policy and admission policies.  Mutations are only reinvoked when mutations change the object after this mutation is invoked. Required.

variables contain definitions of variables that can be used in composition of other expressions. Each variable is defined as a named CEL expression. The variables defined here will be available under `variables` in other expressions of the policy except matchConditions because matchConditions are evaluated before the rest of the policy.

The expression of a variable can refer to other variables defined earlier in the list but not those after. Thus, variables must be sorted by the order of first appearance and acyclic.

The CEL (Common Expression Language) expression used to compute the value of this variable. It is evaluated in the context of the admission request and must return a value compatible with the declared variable type. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the variable in the admission policy. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., alphanumeric characters and underscores, not starting with a digit). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

If the deletionTimestamp of the object is non-nil, entries in this list can only be removed. Finalizers may be processed and removed in any order.  Order is NOT enforced because it introduces significant risk of stuck finalizers. finalizers is a shared field, any actor with permission can reorder it. matchPolicy defines how the "MatchResources" list is used to match incoming requests. Allowed values are "Exact" or "Equivalent".

- Exact: match a request only if it exactly matches a specified rule. For example, if deployments can be modified via apps/v1, apps/v1beta1, and extensions/v1beta1, but "rules" only included `apiGroups:["apps"], apiVersions:["v1"], resources: ["deployments"]`, the admission policy does not consider requests to apps/v1beta1 or extensions/v1beta1 API groups.

- Equivalent: match a request if modifies a resource listed in rules, even via another API group or version. For example, if deployments can be modified via apps/v1, apps/v1beta1, and extensions/v1beta1, and "rules" only included `apiGroups:["apps"], apiVersions:["v1"], resources: ["deployments"]`, the admission policy **does** consider requests made to apps/v1beta1 or extensions/v1beta1 API groups. The API server translates the request to a matched resource API if necessary.

Defaults to "Equivalent"

MutatingAdmissionPolicySpec is the specification of the desired behavior of the admission policy.

failurePolicy defines how to handle failures for the admission policy. Failures can occur from CEL expression parse errors, type check errors, runtime errors and invalid or mis-configured policy definitions or bindings.

A policy is invalid if paramKind refers to a non-existent Kind. A binding is invalid if paramRef.name refers to a non-existent resource.

failurePolicy does not define how validations that evaluate to false are handled.

Allowed values are Ignore or Fail. Defaults to Fail.

matchConditions is a list of conditions that must be met for a request to be validated. Match conditions filter requests that have already been matched by the matchConstraints. An empty list of matchConditions matches all requests. There are a maximum of 64 match conditions allowed.

If a parameter object is provided, it can be accessed via the `params` handle in the same manner as validation expressions.

The exact matching logic is (in order):
  1. If ANY matchCondition evaluates to FALSE, the policy is skipped.
  2. If ALL matchConditions evaluate to TRUE, the policy is evaluated.
  3. If any matchCondition evaluates to an error (but none are FALSE):
     - If failurePolicy=Fail, reject the request
     - If failurePolicy=Ignore, the policy is skipped

matchPolicy defines how the "MatchResources" list is used to match incoming requests. Allowed values are "Exact" or "Equivalent".

- Exact: match a request only if it exactly matches a specified rule. For example, if deployments can be modified via apps/v1, apps/v1beta1, and extensions/v1beta1, but "rules" only included `apiGroups:["apps"], apiVersions:["v1"], resources: ["deployments"]`, a request to apps/v1beta1 or extensions/v1beta1 would not be sent to the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy.

- Equivalent: match a request if modifies a resource listed in rules, even via another API group or version. For example, if deployments can be modified via apps/v1, apps/v1beta1, and extensions/v1beta1, and "rules" only included `apiGroups:["apps"], apiVersions:["v1"], resources: ["deployments"]`, a request to apps/v1beta1 or extensions/v1beta1 would be converted to apps/v1 and sent to the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy.

Defaults to "Equivalent"

validationActions declares how Validations of the referenced ValidatingAdmissionPolicy are enforced. If a validation evaluates to false it is always enforced according to these actions. "Warn" specifies that a validation failure is reported to the request client in HTTP Warning headers, with a warning code of 299. Warnings can be sent both for allowed or denied admission responses. "Audit" specifies that a validation failure is included in the published audit event for the request. "Deny" and "Warn" may not be used together since this combination needlessly duplicates the validation failure both in the API response body and the HTTP warning headers. Required. Required.

kubernetes_apps_controller_revision.data.text: RawExtension is used to hold extensions in external versions. To use this, make a field which has RawExtension as its type in your external, versioned struct, and Object in your internal struct. You also need to register your various plugin types. // Internal package: type MyAPIObject struct { runtime.TypeMeta `json:""` MyPlugin runtime.Object `json:"myPlugin"` } type PluginA struct { AOption string `json:"aOption"` } // External package: type MyAPIObject struct { runtime.TypeMeta `json:""` MyPlugin runtime.RawExtension `json:"myPlugin"` } type PluginA struct { AOption string `json:"aOption"` } // On the wire, the JSON will look something like this: { "kind":"MyAPIObject", "apiVersion":"v1", "myPlugin": { "kind":"PluginA", "aOption":"foo", }, } So what happens? Decode first uses json or yaml to unmarshal the serialized data into your external MyAPIObject. That causes the raw JSON to be stored, but not unpacked. The next step is to copy (using pkg/conversion) into the internal struct. The runtime package's DefaultScheme has conversion functions installed which will unpack the JSON stored in RawExtension, turning it into the correct object type, and storing it in the Object. (TODO: In the case where the object is of an unknown type, a runtime.Unknown object will be created and stored.) Required.

HorizontalPodAutoscalerSpec describes the desired functionality of the HorizontalPodAutoscaler.
HorizontalPodAutoscalerBehavior configures the scaling behavior of the target in both Up and Down directions (scaleUp and scaleDown fields respectively).

HPAScalingRules configures the scaling behavior for one direction via scaling Policy Rules and a configurable metric tolerance.

Scaling Policy Rules are applied after calculating DesiredReplicas from metrics for the HPA. They can limit the scaling velocity by specifying scaling policies. They can prevent flapping by specifying the stabilization window, so that the number of replicas is not set instantly, instead, the safest value from the stabilization window is chosen.

The tolerance is applied to the metric values and prevents scaling too eagerly for small metric variations.

policies is a list of potential scaling polices which can be used during scaling. If not set, use the default values: - For scale up: allow doubling the number of pods, or an absolute change of 4 pods in a 15s window. - For scale down: allow all pods to be removed in a 15s window.
The window, in seconds, this scaling policy's own rate limit is measured over.
Whether this scaling policy's own limit is a `Pods` count or a `Percent` of current replicas.
The real limit this scaling policy enforces -- a pod count or a percentage, per its own `type`.
selectPolicy is used to specify which policy should be used. If not set, the default value Max is used.

stabilizationWindowSeconds is the number of seconds for which past recommendations should be considered while scaling up or scaling down. StabilizationWindowSeconds must be greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to 3600 (one hour). If not set, use the default values: - For scale up: 0 (i.e. no stabilization is done). - For scale down: 300 (i.e. the stabilization window is 300 seconds long).

Quantity is a fixed-point representation of a number. It provides convenient marshaling/unmarshaling in JSON and YAML, in addition to String() and AsInt64() accessors.

The serialization format is:

``` <quantity>        ::= <signedNumber><suffix>

	(Note that <suffix> may be empty, from the "" case in <decimalSI>.)

<digit>           ::= 0 | 1 | ... | 9 <digits>          ::= <digit> | <digit><digits> <number>          ::= <digits> | <digits>.<digits> | <digits>. | .<digits> <sign>            ::= "+" | "-" <signedNumber>    ::= <number> | <sign><number> <suffix>          ::= <binarySI> | <decimalExponent> | <decimalSI> <binarySI>        ::= Ki | Mi | Gi | Ti | Pi | Ei

	(International System of units; See: http://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Units/binary.html)

<decimalSI>       ::= m | "" | k | M | G | T | P | E

	(Note that 1024 = 1Ki but 1000 = 1k; I didn't choose the capitalization.)

<decimalExponent> ::= "e" <signedNumber> | "E" <signedNumber> ```

No matter which of the three exponent forms is used, no quantity may represent a number greater than 2^63-1 in magnitude, nor may it have more than 3 decimal places. Numbers larger or more precise will be capped or rounded up. (E.g.: 0.1m will rounded up to 1m.) This may be extended in the future if we require larger or smaller quantities.

When a Quantity is parsed from a string, it will remember the type of suffix it had, and will use the same type again when it is serialized.

Before serializing, Quantity will be put in "canonical form". This means that Exponent/suffix will be adjusted up or down (with a corresponding increase or decrease in Mantissa) such that:

- No precision is lost - No fractional digits will be emitted - The exponent (or suffix) is as large as possible.

The sign will be omitted unless the number is negative.

Examples:

- 1.5 will be serialized as "1500m" - 1.5Gi will be serialized as "1536Mi"

Note that the quantity will NEVER be internally represented by a floating point number. That is the whole point of this exercise.

Non-canonical values will still parse as long as they are well formed, but will be re-emitted in their canonical form. (So always use canonical form, or don't diff.)

This format is intended to make it difficult to use these numbers without writing some sort of special handling code in the hopes that that will cause implementors to also use a fixed point implementation.

kubernetes_core_node.status.config.error.text: Error describes any problems reconciling the Spec.ConfigSource to the Active config. Errors may occur, for example, attempting to checkpoint Spec.ConfigSource to the local Assigned record, attempting to checkpoint the payload associated with Spec.ConfigSource, attempting to load or validate the Assigned config, etc. Errors may occur at different points while syncing config. Earlier errors (e.g. download or checkpointing errors) will not result in a rollback to LastKnownGood, and may resolve across Kubelet retries. Later errors (e.g. loading or validating a checkpointed config) will result in a rollback to LastKnownGood. In the latter case, it is usually possible to resolve the error by fixing the config assigned in Spec.ConfigSource. You can find additional information for debugging by searching the error message in the Kubelet log. Error is a human-readable description of the error state; machines can check whether or not Error is empty, but should not rely on the stability of the Error text across Kubelet versions. Optional.

Must be empty before the object is deleted from the registry. Each entry is an identifier for the responsible component that will remove the entry from the list. Order is NOT enforced because it introduces significant risk of stuck finalizers. finalizers is a shared field, any actor with permission can reorder it. Each entry is an identifier for the responsible component that will remove the entry from the list. If the deletionTimestamp of the object is non-nil, entries in this list can only be removed. Finalizers may be processed and removed in any order. Order is NOT enforced because it introduces significant risk of stuck finalizers. finalizers is a shared field, any actor with permission can reorder it. If the finalizer list is processed in order, then this can lead to a situation in which the component responsible for the first finalizer in the list is waiting for a signal (field value, external system, or other) produced by a component responsible for a finalizer later in the list, resulting in a deadlock. Without enforced ordering finalizers are free to order amongst themselves and are not vulnerable to ordering changes in the list. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.generate_na.text: GenerateName is an optional prefix, used by the server, to generate a unique name ONLY IF the Name field has not been provided. If this field is used, the name returned to the client will be different than the name passed. This value will also be combined with a unique suffix. The provided value has the same validation rules as the Name field, and may be truncated by the length of the suffix required to make the value unique on the server. If this field is specified and the generated name exists, the server will return a 409. Applied only if Name is not specified. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#idempotency Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.generation.text: A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state. Populated by the system. Read-only. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.labels.text: Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) objects. May match selectors of replication controllers and services. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.managed_fie.text: ManagedFields maps workflow-id and version to the set of fields that are managed by that workflow. This is mostly for internal housekeeping, and users typically shouldn't need to set or understand this field. A workflow can be the user's name, a controller's name, or the name of a specific apply path like "ci-cd". The set of fields is always in the version that the workflow used when modifying the object. Optional.

The API version of the Kubernetes resource that the manager applied. For example, 'v1' for core Pods. This is part of the managedFields entry that tracks the manager's last applied configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The type of fields in the managed fields entry, typically 'FieldsV1'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The fields managed by this manager, represented as a dynamic structure containing field paths and their values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the manager (e.g., kubectl, a controller) that owns or manages these fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The management operation associated with the managed field, typically 'Apply' or 'Update'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the subresource that was updated, such as 'status', or an empty string if the update applied to the whole resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The time at which this managed fields entry was added or modified, in RFC3339 format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.name.text: Name must be unique within a namespace. Is required when creating resources, although some resources may allow a client to request the generation of an appropriate name automatically. Name is primarily intended for creation idempotence and configuration definition. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names#names Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.namespace.text: Namespace defines the space within which each name must be unique. An empty namespace is equivalent to the "default" namespace, but "default" is the canonical representation. Not all objects are required to be scoped to a namespace - the value of this field for those objects will be empty. Must be a DNS_LABEL. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/namespaces Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.owner_refer.text: List of objects depended by this object. If ALL objects in the list have been deleted, this object will be garbage collected. If this object is managed by a controller, then an entry in this list will point to this controller, with the controller field set to true. There cannot be more than one managing controller. Optional.
API version of the owner resource (e.g., 'v1' or 'apps/v1'), matching the group and version of the referent object. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

If true, and if the owner has the 'foregroundDeletion' finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this reference is removed. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A boolean indicating whether this owner reference is the controller of the pod. When true, the owner manages the pod's lifecycle. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The kind of the owning object (e.g., 'ReplicaSet', 'DaemonSet', 'StatefulSet'). This field is part of the OwnerReference and is required. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the owner object that this resource references, as defined in the Kubernetes OwnerReference. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The UID of the object referenced by this owner reference, used to uniquely identify the owner resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.resource_ve.text: An opaque value that represents the internal version of this object that can be used by clients to determine when objects have changed. May be used for optimistic concurrency, change detection, and the watch operation on a resource or set of resources. Clients must treat these values as opaque and passed unmodified back to the server. They may only be valid for a particular resource or set of resources. Populated by the system. Read-only. Value must be treated as opaque by clients and . More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#concurrency-control-and-consistency Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.self_link.text: Deprecated: selfLink is a legacy read-only field that is no longer populated by the system. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.metadata.uid.text: UID is the unique in time and space value for this object. It is typically generated by the server on successful creation of a resource and is not allowed to change on PUT operations. Populated by the system. Read-only. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names#uids Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.name.text: path parameter, not part of the API's own resource representation Required.

kubernetes_core_pod.namespace.text: path parameter, not part of the API's own resource representation Required.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.text: PodSpec is a description of a pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.active_deadline.text: Optional duration in seconds the pod may be active on the node relative to StartTime before the system will actively try to mark it failed and kill associated containers. Value must be a positive integer. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.affinity.text: Affinity is a group of affinity scheduling rules. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.affinity.node_a.text: Node affinity is a group of node affinity scheduling rules. Optional.

The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy the affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose a node that violates one or more of the expressions. The node that is most preferred is the one with the greatest sum of weights, i.e. for each node that meets all of the scheduling requirements (resource request, requiredDuringScheduling affinity expressions, etc.), compute a sum by iterating through the elements of this field and adding "weight" to the sum if the node matches the corresponding matchExpressions; the node(s) with the highest sum are the most preferred. Optional.

The node selector term that defines the node selection criteria for this preferred scheduling preference. It contains matchExpressions and matchFields, which are used to match nodes based on labels and fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a list of node selector requirements that constrain eligible nodes by labels. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt), and optionally value(s) that must be matched. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The Kubernetes label key that the match expression applies to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator to apply when matching the key against the listed values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of values for the node selector expression. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name, spec.unschedulable) rather than node labels. Each requirement contains a key, operator, and optional values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key of the node field (e.g., metadata.name) that the match_fields requirement applies to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Operator is the logical operator applied when matching the field. Valid values: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of field values that must match the node's corresponding field value for the node to be selected. At least one value must match. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The weight (1-100) assigned to this preferred node affinity term, used to calculate the overall preference score for nodes that match the associated selector term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A node selector represents the union of the results of one or more label queries over a set of nodes; that is, it represents the OR of the selectors represented by the node selector terms. Optional.
Required. A list of node selector terms. The terms are ORed. Required.

A list of node selector requirements that must be satisfied for a pod to be eligible to run on a node. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values used with the operator. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The label key that the node must have in order to match the selector expression. This corresponds to a specific node label key that the expression is evaluated against. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator defines the relationship between the label key and the specified values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt, controlling how the node's labels are matched against the selector terms. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values for the match expression. For operators In and NotIn, this list is required and contains the values that must match the key. For operators Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name) rather than labels. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values, and is used to constrain pod scheduling to nodes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The key of a node field used in a matchFields expression, such as 'metadata.name'. It identifies which node field to match against in the node selector term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines the relationship between the field key and the specified values. Allowed operators include In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. For example, In requires the field value to be one of the specified values, while Exists requires the field to be present. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of values that must be matched for the node selector requirement. For operators such as In or NotIn, these are the values the node's label or field must (or must not) have. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.affinity.pod_af.text: Pod affinity is a group of inter pod affinity scheduling rules. Optional.

The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy the affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose a node that violates one or more of the expressions. The node that is most preferred is the one with the greatest sum of weights, i.e. for each node that meets all of the scheduling requirements (resource request, requiredDuringScheduling affinity expressions, etc.), compute a sum by iterating through the elements of this field and adding "weight" to the sum if the node has pods which matches the corresponding podAffinityTerm; the node(s) with the highest sum are the most preferred. Optional.

The pod affinity term defines the set of pods to which the preferred scheduling applies, including a label selector to identify the target pods and a topology key to specify the domain for co-location. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Label selector used to identify the set of pods that the affinity term applies to. It typically includes matchLabels and matchExpressions to select pods based on their labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a set of values, enabling more expressive label matching than exact matchLabels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector expression applies to. This key must match a label on the target resource for the expression to match. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values for the label selector expression. Must be non-empty for the 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, and must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist' operators. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels of the target pod. Each key-value in the map is equivalent to an In operator matchExpression with the given key and value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a list of label keys. The values for these keys are extracted from the pod being scheduled and used to select the set of existing pods that this affinity term applies to, enabling dynamic matching based on the incoming pod's labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of pod label keys used to filter candidate pods for the affinity rule. A pod is considered a match only if its value for any of these keys differs from the incoming pod's value for that key. The keys must not overlap with those in match_label_keys. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A label selector for namespaces. When specified, the pod affinity term applies only to pods running in namespaces that match this selector. If omitted, the affinity term applies to all namespaces. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements used to match namespaces. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. The pod affinity term applies only to pods in namespaces that satisfy these expressions. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector applies to. Must be a valid label key, such as 'app' or 'example.com/key'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a match expression. For Kubernetes label selectors, allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of values that the label key must match, as dictated by the operator. For the In and NotIn operators, this contains the actual values to match against; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty (or omitted). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

match_labels is a map of label keys to values used to select namespaces. Only namespaces with all specified labels are matched for this pod affinity term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of namespaces to which the label selector for this affinity term applies. If empty or unset, only the namespace of the pod is considered. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The key of node labels used to define topology domains (e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname) for evaluating pod affinity/anti-affinity. The scheduler uses these domains to group nodes and determine preferred scheduling behavior. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Weight associated with the pod affinity term, ranging from 1 to 100. Higher weights give the term higher precedence during scheduling. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

If the affinity requirements specified by this field are not met at scheduling time, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node. If the affinity requirements specified by this field cease to be met at some point during pod execution (e.g. due to a pod label update), the system may or may not try to eventually evict the pod from its node. When there are multiple elements, the lists of nodes corresponding to each podAffinityTerm are intersected, i.e. all terms must be satisfied. Optional.

A label selector used to identify the set of pods that the affinity term applies to. Supports matchLabels and matchExpressions to define the selection criteria. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The selector matches pods whose labels satisfy all requirements. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The label key that the match expression evaluates. This is the key of a label on pods that the affinity selector matches against, used together with the operator and values fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a label selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values that the label selector key must match, depending on the operator. For operators In and NotIn, this list must be non-empty; for Exists and DoesNotExist, it must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of label keys and values used to select pods that match all specified labels. This selector is used by pod affinity to identify the set of pods that the affinity rule applies to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label keys that the incoming pod must not have matching values for in the candidate pods. If the incoming pod has a label with a key in this list, candidate pods sharing the same label value are excluded from the affinity selection. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Label selector to filter namespaces to which the pod affinity term applies. Only namespaces matching this selector are considered when determining pod affinity. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements that define which namespaces are considered for the pod affinity match. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values according to Kubernetes label selector semantics. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector requirement applies to. Must be a valid Kubernetes label key. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator to use for the match expression. Allowed values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'. For 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', the values list must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of values that the label selector matches for the given key. When the operator is `In` or `NotIn`, this list must be non-empty; when the operator is `Exists` or `DoesNotExist`, it must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of label keys and values that must match the labels of a namespace for it to be selected. The selector requires that all specified labels are present on the target namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of namespace names that restricts the set of pods evaluated for this affinity term. If not set, the term applies only to pods in the pod's own namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The node label key that defines the failure domain for pod affinity/anti-affinity. For example, 'kubernetes.io/hostname' or 'topology.kubernetes.io/zone'. Required for required_during_scheduling_ignored_during_execution. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.affinity.pod_an.text: Pod anti affinity is a group of inter pod anti affinity scheduling rules. Optional.

The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy the anti-affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose a node that violates one or more of the expressions. The node that is most preferred is the one with the greatest sum of weights, i.e. for each node that meets all of the scheduling requirements (resource request, requiredDuringScheduling anti-affinity expressions, etc.), compute a sum by iterating through the elements of this field and subtracting "weight" from the sum if the node has pods which matches the corresponding podAffinityTerm; the node(s) with the highest sum are the most preferred. Optional.

Configures a pod affinity term, which defines the target pods (via a label selector) and the topology domain (topology key) for the anti-affinity rule. Optionally, a list of namespaces can scope the selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A label query over pods to select the group of pods to which the affinity term applies. Uses standard Kubernetes label matching semantics. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optional values, used to match pods for this anti-affinity term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that this match expression applies to, used to select pods based on their labels in the pod anti-affinity term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. For In/NotIn, the values field must be non-empty; for Exists/DoesNotExist, the values field must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of string values that the key must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. For 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of label keys and values that must match a resource's labels for the label selector to be satisfied. All specified labels must be present for the selector to match. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of label keys used to filter candidate pods for the affinity/anti-affinity term. Only pods that have the same value for each of these keys as the current pod are considered for the rule. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Label query over the set of namespaces to which the pod affinity term applies. The term applies to the union of namespaces selected by this field and the namespaces listed in the namespaces field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. The requirements are used to select namespaces based on their labels for this pod anti-affinity term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key of the label selector requirement. Identifies the label that the match expression applies to within the namespace selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator to use for the label selector requirement. Allowed values are `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, and `DoesNotExist`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values that the label selector's key must match. For the 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, this list must be non-empty; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

match_labels is a map of key/value pairs that must match the labels on a namespace for it to be selected by this namespace selector. Each key-value pair in the map corresponds to an exact match requirement on the namespace's labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the list of namespaces to which the pod affinity/anti-affinity term applies. If not set, the term applies to the pod's own namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

topology_key is the key for node labels that the system uses to denote the topology domain. It defines the scope of the affinity/anti-affinity, such as kubernetes.io/hostname for node-level topology. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Weight associated with the pod anti-affinity term, ranging from 1 to 100. Higher weights give the term more influence during scheduling. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

If the anti-affinity requirements specified by this field are not met at scheduling time, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node. If the anti-affinity requirements specified by this field cease to be met at some point during pod execution (e.g. due to a pod label update), the system may or may not try to eventually evict the pod from its node. When there are multiple elements, the lists of nodes corresponding to each podAffinityTerm are intersected, i.e. all terms must be satisfied. Optional.

A label selector that identifies the group of pods that the pod must not be co-located with during scheduling. The selector supports matchLabels and matchExpressions to define the selection criteria, matching the standard Kubernetes LabelSelector object. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a set of values. Operators include In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist; values are only used with In and NotIn. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the match expression applies to. This key is used to select pods based on the value of the specified label. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

An array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels of pods to be selected as targets for the anti-affinity rule. Only pods with all specified labels are considered. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label keys that should not match the labels of existing pods in the same topology domain. Pods with labels matching any of these keys are excluded from the anti-affinity rule, allowing more fine-grained control over which pods are considered for scheduling. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A label selector over namespaces that restricts the scope of the pod anti-affinity rule. If specified, the rule only applies to pods in the selected namespaces; if omitted, all namespaces are considered. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements for selecting namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The selector matches namespaces that satisfy all specified requirements. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector requirement matches against. It specifies which label on a namespace to evaluate for pod anti-affinity. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator applied to the key and values in the match expression. Valid values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The values field in a namespace selector match expression is a list of strings that the expression matches against. It is required for the In and NotIn operators, and must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels on the namespaces. All specified labels must be present and have matching values for a namespace to be selected. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of namespaces to which this pod anti-affinity term applies. If empty, the namespace of the current pod is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The key of a node label that defines the topology domain for this anti-affinity rule. Pods are scheduled such that no two pods from the same topology domain are placed on the same node, based on the label value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.automount_servi.text: AutomountServiceAccountToken indicates whether a service account token should be automatically mounted. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.text: List of containers belonging to the pod. Containers cannot currently be added or removed. There must be at least one container in a Pod. Cannot be updated. Required.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.args.text: Arguments to pass to the container's entrypoint command. These override the image's default arguments (CMD) when specified. Each string is passed as a separate argument to the command. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.comm.text: Entrypoint array. This is the container's command, equivalent to the Docker ENTRYPOINT. It overrides the image's default entrypoint and is not executed within a shell. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.env.text: List of environment variables to set in the container. Each item specifies a variable name and optionally its value or a value source (such as a config map, secret, or field reference). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.env..text: The name of the environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The value of the environment variable. Provide a static string to set the environment variable to this value in the container. To dynamically source the value from a Kubernetes resource, use the separate valueFrom block instead. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a source for the environment variable's value, such as a ConfigMap key, Secret key, or field reference. This field is mutually exclusive with 'value'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects a key from a ConfigMap in the pod's namespace to populate the environment variable's value. This object includes the ConfigMap's name, the key to select, and an optional flag to specify if the ConfigMap must exist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the ConfigMap's data to select the value from for this environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference. Must match an existing ConfigMap in the pod's namespace or the pod will fail to start if the field is required. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap key is optional. If false (default), the key must exist and the pod will fail to start if it is missing. If true, the key may be absent, and the environment variable will be omitted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName) to use as the value of the environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
API version of the referent. Defaults to v1 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The path to the pod field to select, such as 'metadata.name' or 'status.podIP'. In a FieldRef, this specifies which field of the pod to reference for the environment variable value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A boolean flag that indicates whether the referenced key is optional. If set to true, the pod will start even if the key does not exist; if false (default), the key must exist for the container to start. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a resource field (e.g., requests.cpu or limits.memory) of the running container and exposes it as an environment variable value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the container whose resource value is referenced. If empty, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the divisor to divide the resource value by before assigning it to the environment variable. This allows adjusting the value's unit (for example, using '1m' to get millicores). The value is a Kubernetes quantity, such as '1k' or '1Gi', and defaults to '1' if not set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. This refers to a container's resource request or limit value to be exposed as an environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects a key from a Secret in the pod's namespace. Typically contains 'name' (the Secret name) and 'key' (the key to retrieve) to expose the secret value as an environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the referenced Secret to select. This key must exist in the Secret's data. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Secret in the same namespace from which to fetch the key. This field is required when using a secret key reference. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If true, the pod will start even if the referenced secret key is missing. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.env_.text: List of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each source can reference a Kubernetes ConfigMap or Secret, allowing environment variables to be set from those objects, with optional prefix support. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Reference to a ConfigMap whose key-value pairs are used to populate environment variables in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ConfigMap to source environment variables from. This ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. When set to true, a missing ConfigMap is allowed and the environment variables are not set; when false or unset, the ConfigMap must exist before the pod can start. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
An optional identifier that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a valid C identifier. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

SecretRef is a reference to a Secret to use for populating environment variables. It contains the name of the Secret and an optional flag indicating whether the Secret must be defined. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret to reference for injecting environment variables. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the Secret referenced by this envFrom source must be defined. When set to true, a missing Secret does not cause an error. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.imag.text: The container image to run, including the registry, repository, and tag or digest (e.g., nginx:latest). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the pull policy for the container image, controlling when the kubelet should pull the image. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never; if unset, the default depends on the image tag (Always for latest or omitted, IfNotPresent otherwise). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.life.text: Specifies lifecycle hooks for the container. Hooks are executed by the container runtime at specific events: postStart (immediately after the container is started) and preStop (immediately before the container is terminated). Each hook can define an exec command or an HTTP request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

postStart represents a lifecycle hook that is executed immediately after a container is created. It contains either an exec action or an HTTP GET request to be performed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies a command to execute inside the container as the postStart lifecycle handler. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run in the container as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. It is a list of strings where the first element is the command path and the remaining elements are arguments passed to it. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
An HTTP GET request to perform when the container is started, as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. This is a Kubernetes HTTPGetAction object. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields, allowing you to set specific headers such as Authorization or Content-Type for the lifecycle HTTP GET action. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of an HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request for the post-start lifecycle hook. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request for the post-start lifecycle hook. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP path to request when executing the HTTP GET on the container's postStart lifecycle hook. For example, '/health'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a sleep action for the postStart lifecycle hook, which pauses container startup for a specified number of seconds. The object contains a 'seconds' field (integer) that determines the delay duration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds the container should sleep when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered. It specifies the duration of the sleep action. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A TCP socket handler that the kubelet attempts to open on the container's port to determine when the postStart lifecycle hook has succeeded. The hook is considered complete when the TCP connection to the specified port succeeds. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If omitted, the pod's IP address is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port number or name of the port to connect to for the TCP socket lifecycle hook. This can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a handler that Kubernetes executes immediately before a container is stopped, allowing for graceful shutdown (e.g., sending a signal or running a cleanup script). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It is an ExecAction that defines the command to execute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run in the container during the preStop lifecycle hook. It is specified as an array of strings and is executed directly without a shell, so shell features like pipes or variables are not available. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to be executed when the container is about to be terminated as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This request is sent to the given host and port with optional path and headers, and responses are ignored. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If omitted, it defaults to the pod IP address. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header is defined by a name and value pair. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request (for example, 'X-Custom-Header'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header entry used in the preStop hook's HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to access on the HTTP server when performing the pre-stop lifecycle HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Port number or name of the port to access on the container. Valid values are numeric (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports block. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) used for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL scheme (protocol) to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The sleep action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It configures a delay (in seconds) to allow the container to terminate gracefully before it is stopped. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the number of seconds the sleep action should last. For a preStop lifecycle hook, this is the duration the container pauses before termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a TCP socket action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook, which opens a connection to a specified port on the container to signal graceful termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to send the pre-stop request to. This can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container. Required. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.live.text: Configuration for the liveness probe of the container. It defines the method and parameters used by Kubernetes to determine if the container is alive, restarting it if the probe fails. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The exec action runs a specified command inside the container. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with a status code of 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to execute inside the container as part of the exec-based liveness probe. It is a list of strings where the first item is the command and the remaining items are arguments to that command. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of consecutive failures before the container is restarted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The gRPC probe configuration. When set, the kubelet performs a gRPC health check on the specified port to determine container liveness. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number of the gRPC service that the probe will check. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the gRPC service to check in the health probe. If omitted, the gRPC health check is performed against the whole service, as defined by the gRPC Health Checking Protocol. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the HTTP GET request parameters used for the liveness probe to check container health. This object configures the path, port, headers, and other HTTP request details. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the request. Each item contains a header name and value, allowing addition of headers such as Host or authentication tokens. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header used in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server when performing the health check. Defaults to '/' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number or name to access on the container. Accepts a numeric port between 1 and 65535, or an IANA_SVC_NAME for a named port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
