The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated. The probe will wait this long before running its first check. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. Must be 1 for a liveness probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the TCP socket action for the liveness probe, including the port (and optionally the host) that the kubelet will attempt to connect to. If the connection succeeds, the probe is considered successful. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to connect to for the liveness probe. Accepts a numeric port number or a named port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.name.text: Name of the container. Must be a valid DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.port.text: A list of network ports exposed by the container. Each entry specifies a container port (and optionally a host port, IP, protocol, and name) as defined by the Kubernetes container spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number that the container exposes on the pod's network. Valid port numbers range from 1 to 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host IP address to bind the host port to. Defaults to 0.0.0.0 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The host port number to which the container port is mapped, allowing external access to the container. If omitted, the port is only accessible from within the cluster. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) when specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the port. If specified, this must be an IANA_SVC_NAME and unique within the pod. Each named port in a pod must have a unique name. This name can be referenced by services. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol for the container port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. Defaults to TCP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.read.text: Configuration for the readiness probe, which checks whether the container is ready to serve traffic. The container is considered ready when the probe succeeds, and only then will it receive traffic from services. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec specifies an exec action to perform within the container as part of the readiness probe. It runs a command and uses its exit status to determine container readiness. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run inside the container, as a list of strings where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. It is executed directly (not via a shell) in the container's root filesystem; for probes, an exit status of 0 indicates success. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed, after which the container is marked as not ready. Defaults to 3. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines the gRPC action for the readiness probe, including the port to check and optionally the service name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number of the gRPC service to check. This is required for gRPC probes and must be a valid TCP port (1-65535). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the gRPC service to query in the health check. If not specified, the default health check service is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines the parameters for an HTTP GET request used as a readiness probe. The kubelet sends an HTTP GET to the specified path and port on the container's IP address to determine if the container is ready. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Optional list of custom HTTP headers to send with the probe request. Each item is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the readiness probe request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port to access on the container. Accepts a port number (as a string) or a named port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are "HTTP" and "HTTPS". Defaults to "HTTP". Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0; minimum value is 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The minimum number of consecutive successful probes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Must be 1 for liveness and startup probes. Defaults to 1, with a minimum value of 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a TCP socket probe for the container readiness probe. The probe checks whether a TCP connection to the given port can be established, and the container is considered ready if the connection succeeds. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name or IP to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port to check for the TCP readiness probe. This can be a numeric port (as a string) or a named port defined in the container's ports list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.resi.text: A list of policies defining how the container's resources (e.g., CPU, memory) are resized when the pod's resource requests or limits change. Each policy specifies a resource name and a restart policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether a container must be restarted for a resource resize to take effect. Valid values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.reso.text: Defines the compute resources (CPU, memory, and ephemeral storage) for the container, specifying resource requests and limits. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of resource claims that the container requires. Each claim references a ResourceClaim by name to request specific resources. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name must match the name of a ResourceClaim in the same namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Keys are resource names like 'cpu' and 'memory', and values are quantities such as '500m' for CPU cores or '128Mi' for memory. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If requests are omitted for a container, it defaults to limits if those are explicitly specified, or to an implementation-defined value. The map keys are resource names like cpu and memory, and values are quantities like '100m' or '1Gi'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.rest.text: Specifies the restart policy for the pod's containers. Allowed values are Always, OnFailure, and Never. In standard Kubernetes, this is a pod-level field, not a container-level field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The logical operator used to compare the container exit code against the list of exit_codes in the restart policy rule. It defines the condition for matching, such as whether the exit code must be in the list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of container exit codes that match this rule. If the container exits with any of these codes, the restart policy rule is applied. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.secu.text: Security settings for the container, such as user IDs, capabilities, SELinux options, read-only root filesystem, and privilege escalation control. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Controls whether a process in the container can gain more privileges than its parent process. When false, the container runs with the no_new_privs flag set, preventing privilege escalation via setuid or other mechanisms. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Object that specifies the AppArmor profile to apply to the container. It includes the profile type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and may include a localhost profile name when type is Localhost. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of a pre-loaded AppArmor profile on the node, used when the AppArmor profile type is set to Localhost. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Valid values are "Localhost" (use a profile specified in localhostProfile), "RuntimeDefault" (use the container runtime's default profile), or "Unconfined" (disable AppArmor). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines the Linux capabilities to add to or drop from the container. This field contains 'add' and 'drop' lists to grant or remove specific capabilities from the container's default set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Adds the specified Linux capabilities to the container's permitted set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's security context. Each entry is a capability name (e.g., 'ALL', 'NET_ADMIN'), and the container will have those capabilities removed from its allowed set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Run the container in privileged mode, granting all capabilities and access to host devices. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Sets the proc mount mode for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' (use container runtime's default proc mounts) and 'Unmasked' (unmask the proc mount for visibility). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

When set to true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem. This is a common security hardening practice. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's entrypoint process with. If omitted, the runtime default group is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the Kubernetes kubelet will validate the container image at runtime to ensure it does not run as UID 0, and will refuse to start the container if it does. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The user ID (UID) that the container's main process runs as. If not set, the container runs as the user specified in the container image, defaulting to root (UID 0) if the image does not specify one. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the SELinux context for the container, including the user, role, type, and level to be applied. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux level (e.g., 's0', 's0:c1') for the SELinux label, forming part of the se_linux_options configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux role label that applies to the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux type label applied to the container's security context, such as 'svirt_sandbox_file_t'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
SELinux user label assigned to the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines the seccomp profile applied to the container. Contains settings for the seccomp profile type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and, for Localhost, the path to the profile file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Path to a seccomp profile on the node's local filesystem. Must be a descending path relative to the kubelet's configured seccomp profile location, and should only be set when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The type of seccomp profile to apply to the container. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Windows-specific security context options for the container, including GMSA credentials and host process settings. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The GMSA credential spec content for the container's Windows security context. This is the raw JSON string of the credential spec, typically injected by the GMSA admission webhook, either from a referenced credential spec name or provided directly. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This credential spec defines the Group Managed Service Account to be used by the container for authentication. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the container should be run as a 'Host Process' container. All containers in the pod must have the same effective value, and this cannot be set with hostNetwork or runAsUserName. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The Windows user name to run the container's entrypoint process as. Defaults to the user specified in the image metadata if not set; if set in both this security context and the pod security context, the value here takes precedence. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.star.text: The startup probe checks whether the application in the container has started successfully. It is useful for containers with slow startup times; after the startup probe succeeds, the liveness and readiness probes take over. This field is an object representing the probe configuration, such as HTTP GET, TCP socket, or command. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the command to execute inside the container as part of the startup probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0; any non-zero exit indicates a failure. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run inside the container to perform the startup probe. It is specified as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe that are allowed before the container is considered failed and is restarted. Must be set to a positive integer. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the gRPC health check parameters for the startup probe. This block defines the port to connect to and, optionally, the service name to query. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number that the gRPC server is listening on. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, defaults to the empty string, which checks the server's overall health status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Performs an HTTP GET request on the container for the startup probe. This action checks container health by requiring an HTTP response with a status code between 200 and 399 from the specified port, path, and optional host, headers, and scheme. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not set, the pod IP is used. This is the host for the TCP connection, not the Host header; use http_headers to set the Host header instead. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request for the startup probe. Each header is defined by a name and a value, and repeated headers are allowed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to be sent in the startup probe request. For example, 'X-Custom-Header'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the GET request sent by the startup probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. If not set, defaults to '/'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Scheme to use for connecting to the host in the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the startup probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds between each startup probe attempt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1 and must be 1 for startup probes (identical to liveness probe semantics). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a TCP socket probe action, used by the startup probe to check if a TCP connection can be established to the container's IP address on a specified port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod IP is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to connect to for the probe. Can be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the duration in seconds that Kubernetes waits for a pod to terminate gracefully after sending a termination signal. Note: this field is not a part of a startup probe; it is a pod-level setting. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Must be greater than 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.stdi.text: Whether to allocate a stdin for the container. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, the container's stdin is closed after the first attach session, so subsequent attach sessions will not receive stdin. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.term.text: The path inside the container where the termination message is written. This message is captured by kubelet and can be used to report the reason for container termination. Defaults to `/dev/termination-log`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates how the container's termination message is read. Allowed values are 'File' (read from /dev/termination-log) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' (read from a file if container exits with error, otherwise use container logs). Defaults to 'File'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.tty.text: Indicates whether a pseudo-TTY is allocated for the container, enabling interactive shell sessions. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.volu.text: A list of block device mappings for the container. Each item specifies the name of a volume that references a block device and the devicePath where the device appears inside the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path inside the container where the raw block volume device is mounted (e.g., /dev/sdb). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume that this device refers to. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of volume mounts for the container. Each item defines a volume to mount and the mount path inside the container, along with options like read-only and sub-path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Controls how mount propagation is handled for this volume mount. Valid values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'. This determines whether mounts from the host are visible in the container and vice versa. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume to mount, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the volume mount is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the container can only read from the mounted volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the volume mount uses recursive read-only semantics. Allowed values are 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'; if unset, the default behavior for the volume type applies. Only supported for volumes that support recursive read-only mounts and only when read_only is true. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path within the volume to mount instead of the volume's root. Used to mount a subdirectory or file from the volume into the container's mount path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

sub_path_expr is an alternative to sub_path that supports environment variable expansion. It specifies a subpath within the volume to mount, with references like $(VAR_NAME) expanded using container environment variables. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.work.text: The container's working directory. If not specified, the default is the root directory (/). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.dns_config.text: PodDNSConfig defines the DNS parameters of a pod in addition to those generated from DNSPolicy. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.dns_config.name.text: A list of DNS name server IP addresses. This will be appended to the base nameservers generated from DNSPolicy. Duplicated nameservers will be removed. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.dns_config.opti.text: A list of DNS resolver options. This will be merged with the base options generated from DNSPolicy. Duplicated entries will be removed. Resolution options given in Options will override those that appear in the base DNSPolicy. Optional.
The name of the DNS resolver option, such as 'ndots' or 'timeout'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value for a DNS resolver option, as a string. If omitted, the option is treated as a flag. For example, for the 'ndots' option, set value to '2'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.dns_config.sear.text: A list of DNS search domains for host-name lookup. This will be appended to the base search paths generated from DNSPolicy. Duplicated search paths will be removed. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.dns_policy.text: Set DNS policy for the pod. Defaults to "ClusterFirst". Valid values are 'ClusterFirstWithHostNet', 'ClusterFirst', 'Default' or 'None'. DNS parameters given in DNSConfig will be merged with the policy selected with DNSPolicy. To have DNS options set along with hostNetwork, you have to specify DNS policy explicitly to 'ClusterFirstWithHostNet'. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.enable_service_.text: EnableServiceLinks indicates whether information about services should be injected into pod's environment variables, matching the syntax of Docker links. Optional: Defaults to true. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.ephemeral_conta.text: List of ephemeral containers run in this pod. Ephemeral containers may be run in an existing pod to perform user-initiated actions such as debugging. This list cannot be specified when creating a pod, and it cannot be modified by updating the pod spec. In order to add an ephemeral container to an existing pod, use the pod's ephemeralcontainers subresource. Optional.
Arguments to the entrypoint. The container image's CMD is used if this is not provided. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run in the ephemeral container, as an entrypoint array. It overrides the image's default ENTRYPOINT. The command is not executed within a shell, and variable references like $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the container's environment. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of environment variables for the ephemeral container. Each entry defines a variable name and optionally a value or a valueFrom source (e.g., config map, secret, or field reference). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the environment variable, used to reference it within the container. Must be a valid Kubernetes environment variable name, typically a C identifier (e.g., MY_VAR). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the environment variable. This is the string value assigned to the environment variable named in the 'name' field of the same env entry. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a source for the environment variable's value, such as a reference to a ConfigMap, Secret, or pod field. It is mutually exclusive with the 'value' field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to use as the value of the environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select the value from for this environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ConfigMap to select the key from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specify whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If false, the referenced key must exist; if true, the pod will still start even if the key is absent. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents a reference to a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName) whose value is used as the environment variable's value. It contains apiVersion and fieldPath attributes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The API version of the schema that fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to the pod field whose value should be used for the environment variable. For example, metadata.name or spec.nodeName. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key name to retrieve from the referenced file, providing the environment variable's value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the referenced key is optional. If true, the key does not need to exist; if false, its absence causes an error. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume from which the file is read for the environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents a reference to a resource field of the container, such as CPU or memory limits/requests, allowing the environment variable to be set to that resource value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the container from which to select the resource field. When referring to container-specific resource fields (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory), this is required; if omitted, defaults to the container where the field reference is defined. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The divisor to apply when reading the selected resource quantity, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity. The resource value is divided by this amount; defaults to 1 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the container resource to select, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace to provide the value for the environment variable. The referenced Secret must exist before the pod is created. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the Secret to select the value from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Secret from which to select the key. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the secret key must be defined. When set to true, the key is optional and its absence will not cause the container to fail. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, optionally with a prefix to apply to variable names. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

config_map_ref is a reference to a ConfigMap in the same namespace that provides environment variables to the container. When specified, the keys from the ConfigMap become environment variable names and their values become the environment variable values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ConfigMap to use as a source of environment variables for the ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. If true, the ConfigMap may be absent and the pod will still start; if false (default), a missing ConfigMap causes an error. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Optional string that, if specified, is prepended to each key name of the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when generating environment variables for the ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a reference to a Secret in the same namespace as the Pod. The Secret's data is used to populate environment variables when this object appears in an envFrom list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Secret to use for populating environment variables from the referenced secret. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If true, the Secret may be absent; if false or omitted, the Secret must exist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container image to use for the ephemeral container (e.g., nginx:latest). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies when the kubelet should pull the image for this ephemeral container. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. Defaults to Always if the image tag is 'latest' or if the image name is not specified, otherwise IfNotPresent. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Lifecycle configuration for the ephemeral container, defining hooks such as postStart and preStop that execute commands or HTTP/TCP requests at specific container lifecycle events. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The postStart lifecycle hook is executed immediately after the container is started. It can contain exec or httpGet actions to run commands or make HTTP requests before the container is marked as ready. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec specifies the action to run when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered for the ephemeral container. It contains the command to execute inside the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Performs an HTTP GET request against a specified endpoint when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered. This action is configured with host, port, path, and headers to run a custom request after the container starts. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set 'Host' in http_headers instead. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each item should contain a header name and value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The header field value sent in the HTTP request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP request path to access on the HTTP server. For example, /healthz. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port number or name of the port to access on the container. The port must be a valid port number (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Must be either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Sleep defines a lifecycle hook action that pauses for a specified number of seconds before the hook completes. The object contains a required 'seconds' field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds to sleep. This value specifies the duration for the sleep lifecycle hook action. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a TCP socket action for the postStart lifecycle hook. Kubernetes opens a TCP connection to the container's address and the specified port to trigger the lifecycle callback. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, the pod IP address is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to connect to for the postStart lifecycle hook. Accepts a numeric port or a named port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is called immediately before a container is terminated. This object defines the action to take, such as an exec command, an HTTP GET request, or a TCP socket check, allowing the container to gracefully shut down before being stopped. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec specifies the action to run a command inside the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook. It is represented by an ExecAction object containing a command array. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Command to execute inside the ephemeral container when the preStop lifecycle hook is triggered. It is an array of strings, where the first element is the executable and the rest are arguments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines an HTTP GET request that the kubelet sends to the container's IP address to trigger the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This configuration is part of the lifecycle preStop handler for an ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set 'Host' in httpHeaders instead. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to send with the HTTP GET request. Each item in the list defines a header name and value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the pre-stop hook GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request: either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Sleep represents the sleep action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It specifies how long the container should sleep before termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the duration in seconds to sleep before the container is terminated. This is used in the lifecycle pre-stop hook to delay termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a TCP socket action to be performed during the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified host and port, signaling the container to begin shutdown. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, the pod IP address is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The TCP port number (as a string) or named port to connect to when performing the TCP socket check. For example, '8080' or a port name defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Liveness probe configuration for the ephemeral container, used to determine if the container is healthy and running. If the probe fails, the container is considered unhealthy, though ephemeral containers are not automatically restarted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec specifies the command to execute inside the container. The command runs directly within the container; a non-zero exit code indicates failure for the probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, with the working directory set to '/' in the container's filesystem. Since the command is not run inside a shell, traditional shell instructions such as '|' won't work; invoke a shell explicitly if needed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The number of consecutive failures allowed before the liveness probe is considered failed and the container is restarted. Minimum value is 1, default is 3. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the gRPC health check configuration for the liveness probe. This includes the service name and port to use for the gRPC probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number on which the gRPC service is listening. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health checking protocol. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configure the HTTP GET request used by the liveness probe, including the path, port, and custom HTTP headers. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You may want to set the Host header in httpHeaders instead. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Custom HTTP headers to send in the HTTP GET request. Each item in the list is an object containing a header name and value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header as a string. This is used in the headers of the HTTP GET request sent by the liveness probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated. This corresponds to the Kubernetes probe field initialDelaySeconds. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1 and defaults to 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configuration for a TCP socket probe, used to check container liveness by attempting to establish a TCP connection. It specifies the port to probe and optionally the host. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a numeric port number as a string, or a named port defined on the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully. Must be a non-negative integer. A value of 0 indicates delete immediately. This is a pod-level setting, not a probe parameter. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Timeout in seconds after which the liveness probe is considered failed. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 1 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of ports to expose from the ephemeral container. Each entry can specify a container port, protocol, and optional host port and name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number the container listens on. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host IP address to bind the external port to. If not specified, the port is bound to all interfaces. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port on the host node to which the container port is mapped. If specified, this must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535; if omitted, the container port is not accessible externally via a host port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of this port within the container. Optional, but if specified must be a valid DNS label and unique among all ports in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The network protocol used by the container port, such as TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the readiness probe for the ephemeral container, which indicates when the container is ready to serve requests. The probe can be defined with an HTTP GET, TCP socket, or an exec command. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec specifies the action to take, which is to run a command inside the container. The command is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and the rest are arguments. This is used by the readiness probe to check container health. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to execute in the container as part of the exec readiness probe. It is a list of command arguments. A zero exit status indicates success; non-zero indicates failure. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines a gRPC-based health check for the ephemeral container's readiness probe. Includes the port to connect to and an optional service name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number on which the gRPC health check is performed. This field is required and must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If omitted, the gRPC health check is performed against the overall container status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures an HTTP GET request that the kubelet executes against the container to determine readiness. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of custom HTTP headers to send with the HTTP GET request. Each header is an object containing 'name' and 'value' fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request. For example, "Authorization" or "Content-Type". Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP path to request in the HTTP GET probe, such as '/healthz', specifying the endpoint to check on the server. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Port number or name of the port on the container to access for the HTTP GET readiness probe. Accepts a numeric port (e.g., '8080') or a named port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The network protocol to use for the HTTP probe, either "HTTP" or "HTTPS". Defaults to "HTTP". Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The frequency, in seconds, at which the readiness probe is executed. Must be greater than 0; defaults to 10 if unspecified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The minimum number of consecutive successful probe results required for the readiness probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Defaults to 1; for readiness probes this value may be greater than 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
TCPSocket specifies an action involving a TCP port. This block configures a TCP socket check for the readiness probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port number or name of the TCP socket to connect to for the readiness probe. This can be a numeric port (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Timeout in seconds after which the readiness probe is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the resource resize policy for the ephemeral container. Each entry defines a resourceName (e.g., cpu or memory) and a restartPolicy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) that controls how resizing that resource affects the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource (for example, cpu or memory) to which the resize policy applies. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the restart policy for the container when its resources are resized. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The resource requirements for the ephemeral container, specifying the minimum and maximum amounts of compute resources (e.g., CPU, memory) the container can use, typically defined via `requests` and `limits`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of resource claim references used by the container. Each object contains a name that refers to a ResourceClaim defined in the pod's spec.resourceClaims field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Name of the resource claim (e.g., a ResourceClaim object) that this container's resource requirements reference. The claim must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of a specific request within the referenced ResourceClaim to use. If omitted, all resources from the claim are made available. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the ephemeral container. Keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are quantities (e.g., '100m', '1Gi'). More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified, or to an implementation-defined value. The map keys are resource names (such as 'cpu' and 'memory') and values are quantities. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The restart policy for the ephemeral container, controlling whether it is restarted after it exits. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The comparison operator used to determine if an exit code matches the specified values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of numeric container exit codes. If the ephemeral container terminates with one of these codes, the associated restart policy rule is applied. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

SecurityContext holds security configuration that will be applied to the ephemeral container, such as user and group IDs, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and seccomp profiles. It allows specifying security settings distinct from the pod-level security context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether the ephemeral container's process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When false, it prevents privilege escalation via mechanisms like setuid binaries or file capabilities; when true or omitted, privilege escalation is permitted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The AppArmor profile settings for the container. This object specifies the type of AppArmor profile to apply (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined), and when type is Localhost, the localhostProfile field provides the name of a profile preloaded on the node. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the AppArmor profile to use when the AppArmorProfile type is set to 'Localhost'. This profile must already be loaded on the node. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Type of AppArmor profile to apply. Valid values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'. If set to 'Localhost', the 'localhost_profile' field must also be specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines the Linux capabilities to add to or drop from the container's default set. The object contains 'add' and 'drop' lists of capability names. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of Linux capabilities to add to the container's capability set. Each entry is a capability name such as 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME' that grants additional privileges beyond the default set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default capability set for the ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the ephemeral container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to all devices on the host and bypassing many security restrictions. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the proc mount behavior for the ephemeral container, controlling how the /proc filesystem is exposed to the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the group ID (GID) to run the container's entrypoint process as. If set, it overrides the image's default group and any pod-level security context. Must be a valid integer GID. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

If true, the container must run as a non-root user (UID not 0). The kubelet will validate the image at runtime and fail to start the container if it is configured to run as root. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the user ID (UID) that the ephemeral container process will run as. This overrides the runAsUser setting from the pod or container security context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures the SELinux context for the ephemeral container, specifying the user, role, type, and level options. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux level (e.g., s0, s1:c123) applied to the container. This defines the sensitivity level and optional categories for the SELinux policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux role label for the container process. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Type is a SELinux type label that applies to the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The SELinux user label for the container's security context. This is part of the SELinux context definition, specifying the user identity used for mandatory access control. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The seccomp profile configuration for the ephemeral container. This object specifies the seccomp profile type (e.g., Unconfined, RuntimeDefault, Localhost) and optionally the path to a localhost profile. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to a seccomp profile on the node's local filesystem, used when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Type of seccomp profile to be applied to the container. Allowed values are: Localhost, RuntimeDefault, Unconfined. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Windows-specific security context options for the ephemeral container, such as GMSA credential specs and run-as-user settings. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

GMSACredentialSpec is where the GMSA admission webhook (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-gmsa) inlines the contents of the GMSA credential spec named by the GMSACredentialSpecName field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This is used to configure Group Managed Service Accounts (GMSA) for Windows pods. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

HostProcess determines whether the container runs as a HostProcess container on Windows nodes. This field is honored only when the WindowsHostProcessContainers feature gate is enabled. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The Windows user name to run the container process as. If unspecified, defaults to the user specified in the image metadata. May also be set in the pod's security context, but this value takes precedence if set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec specifies the action to take within the container, typically running a command to determine if the container is healthy. The command is provided as a list of strings in the 'command' field of this object. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to execute in the container for the startup probe. It is provided as a list of strings, and the probe succeeds if the command exits with a status code of 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The minimum consecutive number of failures of the startup probe that will cause the container to be terminated and restarted. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies a gRPC-based health check for the startup probe. The object defines the port to check and optionally the service name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number on which the gRPC health check will be performed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the gRPC default behavior is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the HTTP GET request used by the startup probe to check container health. This action makes an HTTP GET request to the container's IP address on a given port and path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; setting this is generally discouraged in favor of using the 'Host' header in httpHeaders. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request. Each header is defined by a name and value, allowing you to set headers such as Authorization or Content-Type for the probe request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP header name to be sent in the request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the startup probe request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL path to request when performing the HTTP GET probe. For example, /healthz. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name or number of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the startup probe is initiated. Minimum value is 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The frequency in seconds at which the startup probe is performed. It determines how often the kubelet checks the container's health during the startup period. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. For startup probes, this value must be 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a TCP socket probe action for the startup probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address on the specified port; a successful connection indicates the container is ready. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to probe. Can be a port number (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The time in seconds that Kubernetes waits after a startup probe failure before forcefully terminating the container. This value overrides the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds for this container's probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Whether this ephemeral container should have stdin open. When true, the container's standard input is connected, allowing interactive processes to read from it. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

When set to true and stdin is also true, the ephemeral container's standard input is closed after the first attach, so subsequent attaches cannot write to stdin. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the container within the pod that this ephemeral container targets. When specified, the ephemeral container shares the process namespace of that target container; otherwise it shares the pod's process namespace if one is defined. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path where the container's termination message is written. This message is used for debugging and can be retrieved after termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies how the termination message is read. Valid values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY (teletype) for the container, enabling interactive terminal sessions. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of block device mappings for the ephemeral container. Each item specifies the volume name and the device path inside the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path inside the container where the block device is mounted. This field is required for each volume device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume in the pod that this device references. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of volume mounts for the ephemeral container, specifying how volumes are mounted into the container's filesystem. Each item defines a volume name and mount path, with optional mount options like read-only and subPath. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of strings that specify options for a bind mount, such as 'ro', 'noexec', or 'nosuid'. These options are passed to the mount operation when the volume is mounted in an ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path within the ephemeral container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines how mounts are propagated from the host to the container and between containers. Valid values are None, HostToContainer, and Bidirectional. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the volume mount is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise it is read-write. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

RecursiveReadOnly specifies whether read-only mounts should be handled recursively. This field is only supported on Linux. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'IfPossible', and 'Disabled'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a sub-path inside the referenced volume that should be mounted instead of the volume's root, allowing selective mounting of a directory or file from the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

subPathExpr is an alternative to subPath that allows the sub-path to be defined using environment variable references (e.g., $(VAR_NAME)). It is resolved at container startup and used to mount a sub-path of the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Container's working directory for the ephemeral container. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.eviction_respon.text: evictionResponders reference responders that react to Evictions based on EvictionRequests. Responders should observe and communicate through the Eviction Resource API to help with the graceful termination of a pod. The responders are selected sequentially, according to their specified priority. Responders should periodically report on an eviction progress by updating the .status.responders[].heartbeatTime field of the Eviction object. If this field is not updated within the heartbeat deadline defined by the Eviction API (currently 20 minutes), the eviction is passed over to the next responder with a lower priority. If there is no other responder, the last default imperative-eviction.k8s.io/evictor responder with a priority of 100 will evict the pod using the imperative Eviction API (pods/<name>/eviction subresource). The maximum length of the responders list is 10. Responders are not supported when the pod is part of a PodGroup (.spec.schedulingGroup is set). This field can only be set on creation and is immutable afterwards. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.host_aliases.text: HostAliases is an optional list of hosts and IPs that will be injected into the pod's hosts file if specified. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.host_aliases.ho.text: A list of hostnames that are mapped to the IP address specified in the hostAliases entry. These hostnames are added to the Pod's /etc/hosts file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.host_aliases.ip.text: The IP address for the host alias entry. This IP is associated with the specified hostnames and added to the pod's /etc/hosts file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.host_ipc.text: Use the host's ipc namespace. Optional: Default to false. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.host_network.text: Host networking requested for this pod. Use the host's network namespace. When using HostNetwork you should specify ports so the scheduler is aware. When `hostNetwork` is true, specified `hostPort` fields in port definitions must match `containerPort`, and unspecified `hostPort` fields in port definitions are defaulted to match `containerPort`. Default to false. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.host_pid.text: Use the host's pid namespace. Optional: Default to false. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.host_users.text: Use the host's user namespace. Optional: Default to true. If set to true or not present, the pod will be run in the host user namespace, useful for when the pod needs a feature only available to the host user namespace, such as loading a kernel module with CAP_SYS_MODULE. When set to false, a new userns is created for the pod. Setting false is useful for mitigating container breakout vulnerabilities even allowing users to run their containers as root without actually having root privileges on the host. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.hostname.text: Specifies the hostname of the Pod If not specified, the pod's hostname will be set to a system-defined value. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.hostname_overri.text: HostnameOverride specifies an explicit override for the pod's hostname as perceived by the pod. This field only specifies the pod's hostname and does not affect its DNS records. When this field is set to a non-empty string: - It takes precedence over the values set in `hostname` and `subdomain`. - The Pod's hostname will be set to this value. - `setHostnameAsFQDN` must be nil or set to false. - `hostNetwork` must be set to false. This field must be a valid DNS subdomain as defined in RFC 1123 and contain at most 64 characters. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.image_pull_secr.text: ImagePullSecrets is an optional list of references to secrets in the same namespace to use for pulling any of the images used by this PodSpec. If specified, these secrets will be passed to individual puller implementations for them to use. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images#specifying-imagepullsecrets-on-a-pod Optional.
Name of the image pull secret. Must reference a Secret in the same namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.init_containers.text: List of initialization containers belonging to the pod. Init containers are executed in order prior to containers being started. If any init container fails, the pod is considered to have failed and is handled according to its restartPolicy. The name for an init container or normal container must be unique among all containers. Init containers may not have Lifecycle actions, Readiness probes, Liveness probes, or Startup probes. The resourceRequirements of an init container are taken into account during scheduling by finding the highest request/limit for each resource type, and then using the max of that value or the sum of the normal containers. Limits are applied to init containers in a similar fashion. Init containers cannot currently be added or removed. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/init-containers/ Optional.

Arguments to the container's entrypoint. This corresponds to the CMD directive in the container image and overrides the image's default command arguments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run in the init container, corresponding to the entrypoint in Docker. This is not executed by a shell; if shell behavior is desired, explicitly invoke the shell (e.g., ["sh", "-c", "echo hi"]). If omitted, the container image's default entrypoint is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of environment variables to set in the init container. Each entry defines a variable name and either a direct value or a value source (e.g., secret, config map, field ref). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The literal value of the environment variable as a string. This field is optional; if not set, use valueFrom to source the value from a config map, secret, or field reference. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a source for the environment variable's value, such as a reference to a ConfigMap, Secret, or a field in the pod spec. This is used when the value is not directly set but pulled from another resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap. This can be used to populate an environment variable with the value of a specific key in a ConfigMap. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select the value from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ConfigMap from which to select a key. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true and the ConfigMap or key does not exist, the environment variable is not set and the container can start. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a field from the pod definition and uses its value as the environment variable's value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The API version of the schema that the field path is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path of the field to select from the pod's object, such as metadata.name or status.podIP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the referenced file key must exist. When set to true, the container starts even if the key is absent; when false (default), the pod fails if the key is missing. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

ResourceFieldRef selects a resource field of the container (such as requests.cpu, limits.memory) and exposes its value as an environment variable in the init container. It is used in the valueFrom source of an environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the container to select the resource field from. If not specified, the pod's container is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The divisor to divide the resource value by. Must be a valid quantity string (e.g., '1', '100m'). If unspecified, the default divisor is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource field to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
secret_key_ref selects a specific key from a Secret in the pod's namespace to supply the value for the environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key of the secret to select. This must be a valid key name within the referenced Secret. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Secret to select the key from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If set to true, the reference is optional and the container can start even if the secret does not exist or the key is missing. Defaults to false, meaning the secret and key must exist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of sources to populate environment variables in the init container. Each source can reference a ConfigMap or Secret (via config_map_ref or secret_ref) and optionally define a prefix for the variable names. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Reference to a ConfigMap whose data is exposed as environment variables in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ConfigMap from which to inject environment variables. This must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. If true, a missing ConfigMap is allowed and no environment variables from it are set; if false or omitted, the ConfigMap must exist or the pod will fail to start. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
An optional prefix to prepend to each key in the ConfigMap or Secret when populating environment variables. Must be a valid C identifier. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret. The key-value pairs of the referenced secret are exposed as environment variables in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Secret to reference. This Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the referenced Secret must exist. Defaults to false (the Secret must be present); if true, the Secret is optional and its absence is allowed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container image to run, e.g., 'nginx:latest'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The image pull policy for this init container. Valid values are 'Always', 'IfNotPresent', and 'Never'. 'Always' pulls the image every time the container starts; 'IfNotPresent' pulls only if the image is not already present on the node; 'Never' never pulls the image and fails if it is not already present locally. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Lifecycle defines handlers for container lifecycle events (postStart and preStop). For init containers, Kubernetes does not execute lifecycle hooks, so this field is ignored for them. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Represents the post-start lifecycle hook that runs immediately after a container is created. It can contain an exec command or an HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Exec specifies the action to take in the form of a command to be executed inside the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command line to execute inside the container during the postStart hook. Specified as a list of strings; the first item is the command and subsequent items are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

http_get specifies an HTTP GET request to perform in the postStart lifecycle hook. It defines the endpoint, port, headers, and other request parameters for the probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name (key) of the HTTP header to send in the GET request of the post-start lifecycle hook. This is the header field name, such as 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type', paired with its corresponding value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port number or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol scheme used for the HTTP GET request, such as 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP' if unspecified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds the container should sleep as part of the post-start lifecycle hook's sleep action. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The tcp_socket block defines a TCP socket check to be performed during the postStart lifecycle hook. It attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container, with an optional host. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Port number or name of the TCP socket to connect to on the container. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port; if omitted, defaults to the container's first port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that executes a handler immediately before a container is terminated. It allows you to run commands or make HTTP/TCP requests to gracefully stop the container, such as cleaning up resources or saving state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Exec defines a command to execute inside the container as part of the pre_stop lifecycle hook. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Command to run inside the container. This is an array of strings, executed directly without a shell; shell features like pipes or variables are not supported unless you explicitly invoke a shell. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. Contains endpoint details such as host, port, path, and headers. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with a name and a value field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request, for example 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Can be a port number or a named port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP protocol to use for the request. Allowed values are `HTTP` and `HTTPS`, with a default of `HTTP`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
