Scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Sleep performs a sleep action during the pre-stop hook, pausing the container for a specified number of seconds before termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds for the sleep action in the preStop lifecycle hook. Delays container termination by the specified duration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines the TCP socket handler for the preStop lifecycle hook, specifying the port (and optionally host) to connect to when the container is about to be terminated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, it defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port number (e.g., 8080) or the name of a port defined in the container (e.g., "http"). This field is required. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Periodic probe of container liveness. The container will be restarted if the probe fails. Cannot be updated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the command to execute in the container to perform the liveness probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to execute inside the container to perform the liveness probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0, otherwise the container is restarted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

grpc specifies an action that involves a gRPC request for the liveness probe. It includes the port to check and optionally the service name to resolve, allowing the kubelet to perform a gRPC health check on the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number on which the gRPC endpoint is exposed. Must be between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If empty (default), the gRPC server's overall health status is checked. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform on the container as part of the liveness probe to check container health. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each object must contain 'name' and 'value' fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request for this liveness probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Provide a numeric port (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request in the liveness probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The frequency, in seconds, at which the liveness probe is performed. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The minimum consecutive successes for the liveness probe to be considered successful. For liveness probes, this value must be 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures the liveness probe to perform a TCP socket check by attempting to open a connection to the container's IP address on the specified port. The port is required, and an optional host can be specified to override the connection target. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the TCP probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port number or named port to probe for the liveness check. Accepts an integer port or a name that refers to a port of the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out and is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the init container. Must be a valid DNS label and unique within the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of ports to expose from the container. Each port defines a container port number and protocol, and optionally a name and host port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number that the container exposes. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host IP address to bind the port to. If not set, the port is bound to all host interfaces (0.0.0.0). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number on the host node to expose this container port. Must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A name for this container port. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME (e.g., a DNS label) and unique within the pod. This name can be used to reference the port from services or other configurations. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol used for the port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a probe that checks whether the container is ready to accept traffic. In Kubernetes, this field is part of the container spec, though for init containers it is generally not used since they run to completion. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec specifies a command to run in the container as part of the readiness probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with a status code of 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. It is specified as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The probe succeeds if the command exits with exit code 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Minimum number of consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a gRPC-based readiness probe. The object includes a required port (integer) and an optional service name (string) to include in the gRPC health check request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number of the gRPC service to probe. In a gRPC readiness probe, this specifies the port on the container that the probe will connect to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not set, the gRPC server's default service is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform against the container as a readiness check. A response with an HTTP status code between 200 and 399 indicates the container is ready. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name to connect to, defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set "Host" in httpHeaders instead. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the request sent by the HTTP GET probe. Each item must contain a name and a value, representing a header to be added to the probe's request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request, e.g., 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request. It is paired with the header name (the 'name' field) to form the HTTP header entry. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use when making the HTTP request to the readiness probe endpoint. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the scheme to use for the HTTP request: HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0 seconds. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds between each readiness probe execution. Defaults to 10 seconds if not set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The minimum number of consecutive successful probe results required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. This defaults to 1 for readiness probes. Must be 1 for liveness and startup probes, and the minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures a TCP socket probe. Kubernetes attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port to determine readiness. This is one of the allowed probe types within a readiness probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a numeric port string (e.g., '80') or a named port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 1 second. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of resource resize policies for the init container. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) when that resource is resized, controlling whether the container needs to be restarted for the resize to take effect. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the restart behavior of the container when the assigned resource is resized. Valid values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Resources defines the compute resource requirements (requests and limits) for the init container, such as CPU and memory. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of resource claims that must be satisfied for this container. Each item references a ResourceClaim by name, enabling access to resources like persistent volumes or specialized hardware. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ResourceClaim that this container requires. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the maximum amount of compute resources that the container is allowed to use. Maps resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to their quantities. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of Kubernetes resource names to quantity strings, specifying the minimum amount of compute resources (e.g., cpu, memory) required for the container. Example values: '100m' for CPU, '128Mi' for memory. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the restart policy for this init container. The only supported value is 'Always', which runs the container as a sidecar. When omitted, the default behavior is to run the init container to completion. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
exit_codes is an object that defines which container exit codes this restart policy rule applies to for restart decisions. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The comparison operator used to match the container's exit code against the values in `exit_codes`. Examples include `In` and `NotIn`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of integer exit codes that trigger this restart policy rule for the init container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

SecurityContext defines the security options the init container should be run with. If set, the fields of SecurityContext override the equivalent fields of PodSecurityContext. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Controls whether the process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container will have the no_new_privs bit set, preventing privilege escalation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The AppArmor profile to apply to the container. This can be a predefined profile (RuntimeDefault or Unconfined) or a custom profile defined on the node (Localhost), optionally specifying the localhost profile name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the AppArmor profile to load on the local node when the type is 'Localhost'. This profile must exist on the node's local profile store. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The AppArmor profile type. Must be one of `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, or `Unconfined`. If set to `Localhost`, the `localhostProfile` field must also be specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures Linux capabilities for the container, allowing specific capabilities to be added or dropped via the add and drop lists. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies additional capabilities to grant to the container process. For example, 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default capability set. Each entry is a capability name such as 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode. Privileged containers have access to all host devices and run with extended capabilities beyond the default. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

ProcMount denotes the type of proc mount to use for the container. Allowed values are 'DefaultProcMount' and 'UnmaskedProcMount'. Defaults to 'DefaultProcMount', which masks paths in /proc for security; 'UnmaskedProcMount' provides the full /proc without masking. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The GID to run the init container's entrypoint process as. If set, it overrides the group specified in the container image. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and will refuse to start the container if it does. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the numeric user ID (UID) under which the init container's main process will run. Overrides the pod-level runAsUser if both are set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
seLinuxOptions configures the SELinux context for the init container. It allows specifying the user, role, type, and level of the SELinux label. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux level label applied to the container, typically a Multi-Category Security (MCS) level such as 's0:c123,c456'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux role label for the container process. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux type label for the container, e.g., 'container_t'. This is part of the SELinux security context applied to the container processes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux user label for the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Seccomp profile applied to the init container. Supports types Unconfined, RuntimeDefault, and Localhost; when Localhost is used, localhostProfile specifies the path to the node-local profile. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to the seccomp profile file on the node, used when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The type of seccomp profile to apply. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Unconfined', and 'Localhost'. When set to 'Localhost', a 'localhostProfile' must also be provided. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Windows-specific security context options for the init container. This field configures Windows-only security attributes and is applicable only to Windows containers. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The contents of a GMSA credential spec (as a JSON string) used by the Windows container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container. GMSA (Group Managed Service Accounts) allow containers to inherit Active Directory identities; this must reference a credential spec available on the node. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the container should run as a HostProcess container. All containers in the pod must have the same effective HostProcess value. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The UserName in Windows to run the container's process as. If unspecified, the default is the user specified in the container image. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures a probe to check whether the container's startup has completed. In init containers, this field has no effect because init container success is based on exit status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Exec specifies a command to execute inside the container for the startup probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container for the startup probe. It is a list of strings; the first element is the command, and subsequent elements are arguments. Non-zero exit status indicates probe failure. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of consecutive failures that must occur for the startup probe to be considered failed, after which the container is marked as unhealthy. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
grpc defines the gRPC-based probe handler for the startup probe, specifying the port to check and optionally the service name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number of the gRPC service for the startup probe. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is an empty string, meaning the health check is performed on the overall service. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP GET action for the startup probe. Specifies how the probe performs an HTTP GET request to check the container's health. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe, defaults to the pod IP. This value is used as the Host header in the HTTP request, and you typically set the Host header via httpHeaders instead of this field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request. Each item specifies a header name and value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the startup probe's HTTP GET request (e.g., 'Authorization', 'X-Custom-Header'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to access on the HTTP server, e.g., '/healthz'. Defaults to '/' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The TCP port number or named port on the container to send the HTTP GET request to. Can be a numeric port (e.g., '8080') or a named port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) used for the HTTP GET probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies how often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. The default is 10 seconds; the minimum allowed value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Minimum consecutive successes for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Must be 1 for startup probes, as higher values are not allowed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures a TCP socket check for the startup probe, which determines if the container has started successfully by attempting to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to connect to for the startup probe. Accepts a port number or a named port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The duration in seconds that the pod is allowed to gracefully terminate before being forcefully killed. A value of 0 means immediate termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds after which the startup probe times out and is considered failed if no response is received. Must be a positive integer. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Whether to allocate a standard input stream for the container, enabling interactive sessions or input to the container process. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, the container's stdin is closed after the first attach when stdin is enabled. Defaults to false when not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Path to the file where the container's termination message is written. This message is then exposed to the kubelet and can be retrieved via the pod status. Defaults to /dev/termination-log. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Determines how the container's termination message is read. Allowed values are 'File' (default), which reads the message from /dev/termination-log, and 'FallbackToLogsOnError', which falls back to the container's log if the termination message file is empty and the container exits with error. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether a TTY should be allocated for the container. This requires 'stdin' to be true. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of volume devices (block storage) to be mounted into the container. Each entry specifies a device name and the path inside the container where the device will appear. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path inside the container where the block device will be mounted (devicePath). This is required for each volume device entry. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume that the device refers to. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies volumes to mount into the init container's filesystem. Each item defines a volume mount, typically including the volume name and mount path, along with options such as read-only or subPath. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must not contain ':'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mount propagation mode for this volume mount. Allowed values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume to mount. This must correspond to the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Whether the volume mount is read-only. If true, the container has read-only access to the mounted volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

recursive_read_only controls whether the volume mount is mounted recursively read-only. Possible values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', and 'IfPossible', where 'IfPossible' applies recursive read-only only if the volume driver supports it. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The sub-path within the volume that should be mounted instead of the volume's root. This allows mounting a specific directory of the volume into the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Similar to subPath, but can reference environment variables with the syntax $(VAR_NAME); the kubelet resolves the variables. Mutually exclusive with subPath. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used, which may be configured in the container image. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.node_name.text: NodeName indicates in which node this pod is scheduled. If empty, this pod is a candidate for scheduling by the scheduler defined in schedulerName. Once this field is set, the kubelet for this node becomes responsible for the lifecycle of this pod. This field should not be used to express a desire for the pod to be scheduled on a specific node. https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#nodename Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.node_selector.text: NodeSelector is a selector which must be true for the pod to fit on a node. Selector which must match a node's labels for the pod to be scheduled on that node. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/assign-pod-node/ Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.os.text: PodOS defines the OS parameters of a pod. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.os.name.text: Name is the name of the operating system. The currently supported values are linux and windows. Additional value may be defined in future and can be one of: https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec/blob/master/config.md#platform-specific-configuration Clients should expect to handle additional values and treat unrecognized values in this field as os: null Required.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.overhead.text: Overhead represents the resource overhead associated with running a pod for a given RuntimeClass. This field will be autopopulated at admission time by the RuntimeClass admission controller. If the RuntimeClass admission controller is enabled, overhead must not be set in Pod create requests. The RuntimeClass admission controller will reject Pod create requests which have the overhead already set. If RuntimeClass is configured and selected in the PodSpec, Overhead will be set to the value defined in the corresponding RuntimeClass, otherwise it will remain unset and treated as zero. More info: https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-node/688-pod-overhead/README.md Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.preemption_poli.text: PreemptionPolicy is the Policy for preempting pods with lower priority. One of Never, PreemptLowerPriority. When Priority Admission Controller is enabled, it prevents users from setting this field. The admission controller populates this field from PriorityClassName. Defaults to PreemptLowerPriority if unset. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.priority.text: The priority value. Various system components use this field to find the priority of the pod. When Priority Admission Controller is enabled, it prevents users from setting this field. The admission controller populates this field from PriorityClassName. The higher the value, the higher the priority. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.priority_class_.text: If specified, indicates the pod's priority. "system-node-critical" and "system-cluster-critical" are two special keywords which indicate the highest priorities with the former being the highest priority. Any other name must be defined by creating a PriorityClass object with that name. If not specified, the pod priority will be default or zero if there is no default. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.readiness_gates.text: If specified, all readiness gates will be evaluated for pod readiness. A pod is ready when all its containers are ready AND all conditions specified in the readiness gates have status equal to "True" More info: https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-network/580-pod-readiness-gates Optional.

The name of the condition that must be satisfied for the pod to be considered ready. This condition is defined outside the pod spec, typically by a custom controller or resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.resource_claims.text: ResourceClaims defines which ResourceClaims must be allocated and reserved before the Pod is allowed to start. The resources will be made available to those containers which consume them by name. This is a stable field but requires that the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate is enabled. This field is immutable. Optional.
The name of the resource claim. Must be unique within the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the ResourceClaim resource that this pod references. Must match an existing ResourceClaim in the same namespace, or be omitted if a template is provided. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of a ResourceClaimTemplate in the same namespace that will be used to create a ResourceClaim for this pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.resources.text: ResourceRequirements describes the compute resource requirements. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.resources.claim.text: Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This field depends on the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate. This field is immutable. It can only be set for containers. Optional.
The name of the ResourceClaim resource that this pod references. This must match the name of an existing ResourceClaim in the same namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ResourceClaim that this pod requests. The named ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.resources.limit.text: Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.resources.reque.text: Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.restart_policy.text: Restart policy for all containers within the pod. One of Always, OnFailure, Never. In some contexts, only a subset of those values may be permitted. Default to Always. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#restart-policy Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.runtime_class_n.text: RuntimeClassName refers to a RuntimeClass object in the node.k8s.io group, which should be used to run this pod. If no RuntimeClass resource matches the named class, the pod will not be run. If unset or empty, the "legacy" RuntimeClass will be used, which is an implicit class with an empty definition that uses the default runtime handler. More info: https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-node/585-runtime-class Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.scheduler_name.text: If specified, the pod will be dispatched by specified scheduler. If not specified, the pod will be dispatched by default scheduler. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.scheduling_gate.text: SchedulingGates is an opaque list of values that if specified will block scheduling the pod. If schedulingGates is not empty, the pod will stay in the SchedulingGated state and the scheduler will not attempt to schedule the pod. SchedulingGates can only be set at pod creation time, and be removed only afterwards. Optional.

The name of the scheduling gate. This name identifies a gate that can block a pod from being scheduled; the pod will not be scheduled until all scheduling gates are removed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.scheduling_grou.text: PodSchedulingGroup identifies the runtime scheduling group instance that a Pod belongs to. The scheduler uses this information to apply workload-aware scheduling semantics. Exactly one field must be specified. Optional.
PodGroupName specifies the name of the standalone PodGroup object that represents the runtime instance of this group. Must be a DNS subdomain. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.security_contex.text: PodSecurityContext holds pod-level security attributes and common container settings. Some fields are also present in container.securityContext. Field values of container.securityContext take precedence over field values of PodSecurityContext. Optional.
AppArmorProfile defines a pod or container's AppArmor settings. Optional.

localhostProfile indicates a profile loaded on the node that should be used. The profile must be preconfigured on the node to work. Must match the loaded name of the profile. Must be set if and only if type is "Localhost". Optional.

type indicates which kind of AppArmor profile will be applied. Valid options are: Localhost - a profile pre-loaded on the node. RuntimeDefault - the container runtime's default profile. Unconfined - no AppArmor enforcement. Required.

A special supplemental group that applies to all containers in a pod. Some volume types allow the Kubelet to change the ownership of that volume to be owned by the pod: 1. The owning GID will be the FSGroup 2. The setgid bit is set (new files created in the volume will be owned by FSGroup) 3. The permission bits are OR'd with rw-rw---- If unset, the Kubelet will not modify the ownership and permissions of any volume. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

fsGroupChangePolicy defines behavior of changing ownership and permission of the volume before being exposed inside Pod. This field will only apply to volume types which support fsGroup based ownership(and permissions). It will have no effect on ephemeral volume types such as: secret, configmaps and emptydir. Valid values are "OnRootMismatch" and "Always". If not specified, "Always" is used. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process. Uses runtime default if unset. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence for that container. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does. If unset or false, no such validation will be performed. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence. Optional.

The UID to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence for that container. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

seLinuxChangePolicy defines how the container's SELinux label is applied to all volumes used by the Pod. It has no effect on nodes that do not support SELinux or to volumes does not support SELinux. Valid values are "MountOption" and "Recursive". "Recursive" means relabeling of all files on all Pod volumes by the container runtime. This may be slow for large volumes, but allows mixing privileged and unprivileged Pods sharing the same volume on the same node. "MountOption" mounts all eligible Pod volumes with `-o context` mount option. This requires all Pods that share the same volume to use the same SELinux label. It is not possible to share the same volume among privileged and unprivileged Pods. Eligible volumes are in-tree FibreChannel and iSCSI volumes, and all CSI volumes whose CSI driver announces SELinux support by setting spec.seLinuxMount: true in their CSIDriver instance. Other volumes are always re-labelled recursively. If not specified, "MountOption" is used. This field affects only Pods that have SELinux label set, either in PodSecurityContext or in SecurityContext of all containers. All Pods that use the same volume should use the same seLinuxChangePolicy, otherwise some pods can get stuck in ContainerCreating state. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.
SELinuxOptions are the labels to be applied to the container Optional.
Level is SELinux level label that applies to the container. Optional.
Role is a SELinux role label that applies to the container. Optional.
Type is a SELinux type label that applies to the container. Optional.
User is a SELinux user label that applies to the container. Optional.
SeccompProfile defines a pod/container's seccomp profile settings. Only one profile source may be set. Optional.

localhostProfile indicates a profile defined in a file on the node should be used. The profile must be preconfigured on the node to work. Must be a descending path, relative to the kubelet's configured seccomp profile location. Must be set if type is "Localhost". Must NOT be set for any other type. Optional.

type indicates which kind of seccomp profile will be applied. Valid options are: Localhost - a profile defined in a file on the node should be used. RuntimeDefault - the container runtime default profile should be used. Unconfined - no profile should be applied. Required.

A list of groups applied to the first process run in each container, in addition to the container's primary GID and fsGroup (if specified). If the SupplementalGroupsPolicy feature is enabled, the supplementalGroupsPolicy field determines whether these are in addition to or instead of any group memberships defined in the container image. If unspecified, no additional groups are added, though group memberships defined in the container image may still be used, depending on the supplementalGroupsPolicy field. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

Defines how supplemental groups of the first container processes are calculated. Valid values are "Merge" and "Strict". If not specified, "Merge" is used. (Alpha) Using the field requires the SupplementalGroupsPolicy feature gate to be enabled and the container runtime must implement support for this feature. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

Sysctls hold a list of namespaced sysctls used for the pod. Pods with unsupported sysctls (by the container runtime) might fail to launch. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.
The name of the sysctl parameter to set, such as kernel.shm_rmid_forced or net.ipv4.ip_forward. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the sysctl parameter. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
WindowsSecurityContextOptions contain Windows-specific options and credentials. Optional.

GMSACredentialSpec is where the GMSA admission webhook (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-gmsa) inlines the contents of the GMSA credential spec named by the GMSACredentialSpecName field. Optional.
GMSACredentialSpecName is the name of the GMSA credential spec to use. Optional.

HostProcess determines if a container should be run as a 'Host Process' container. All of a Pod's containers must have the same effective HostProcess value (it is not allowed to have a mix of HostProcess containers and non-HostProcess containers). In addition, if HostProcess is true then HostNetwork must also be set to true. Optional.

The UserName in Windows to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to the user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.service_account.text: DeprecatedServiceAccount is a deprecated alias for ServiceAccountName. Deprecated: Use serviceAccountName instead. Optional.
ServiceAccountName is the name of the ServiceAccount to use to run this pod. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/ Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.set_hostname_as.text: If true the pod's hostname will be configured as the pod's FQDN, rather than the leaf name (the default). In Linux containers, this means setting the FQDN in the hostname field of the kernel (the nodename field of struct utsname). In Windows containers, this means setting the registry value of hostname for the registry key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\Tcpip\\Parameters to FQDN. If a pod does not have FQDN, this has no effect. Default to false. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.share_process_n.text: Share a single process namespace between all of the containers in a pod. When this is set containers will be able to view and signal processes from other containers in the same pod, and the first process in each container will not be assigned PID 1. HostPID and ShareProcessNamespace cannot both be set. Optional: Default to false. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.subdomain.text: If specified, the fully qualified Pod hostname will be "<hostname>.<subdomain>.<pod namespace>.svc.<cluster domain>". If not specified, the pod will not have a domainname at all. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.termination_gra.text: Optional duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully. May be decreased in delete request. Value must be non-negative integer. The value zero indicates stop immediately via the kill signal (no opportunity to shut down). If this value is nil, the default grace period will be used instead. The grace period is the duration in seconds after the processes running in the pod are sent a termination signal and the time when the processes are forcibly halted with a kill signal. Set this value longer than the expected cleanup time for your process. Defaults to 30 seconds. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.text: If specified, the pod's tolerations. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.eff.text: The pod scheduling effect this toleration matches, such as NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, or NoExecute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.key.text: The taint key that this toleration matches. When omitted with operator 'Exists', the toleration matches all keys. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.ope.text: The operator to use when matching taints. Allowed values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. If 'Exists', the toleration matches all taints with the given key; if 'Equal', it matches taints with the given key and value. Defaults to 'Equal'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.tol.text: The duration in seconds that the toleration is effective for, after which the pod may be evicted if the taint persists. If unset, the toleration does not expire. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.val.text: The value to match the taint value when using the Equal operator. If the operator is Exists, this field must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.topology_spread.text: TopologySpreadConstraints describes how a group of pods ought to spread across topology domains. Scheduler will schedule pods in a way which abides by the constraints. All topologySpreadConstraints are ANDed. Optional.
Label selector used to identify the set of pods to which the topology spread constraint applies. Must match the pods whose spread is constrained. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement contains a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector applies to. This must match a label on the resource for the match expression to be satisfied. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator used to compare the label value against the set of values. Allowed values are `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, and `DoesNotExist`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values that the label key must match. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty when the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A map of label keys and values that must match the pod's labels for the label selector to match. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of pod label keys that must exist on pods for them to be considered by this topology spread constraint. Spreading is calculated over the label values associated with these keys, allowing refinement of the pod set used for distribution. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Maximum degree of skew (difference in number of pods) allowed between any two topology domains when distributing pods, as defined in Kubernetes topology spread constraints. Must be greater than zero. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The minimum number of eligible topology domains for spreading. If the number of eligible domains is less than this value, the spread constraint calculation treats the global minimum as zero and evaluates skew across the existing eligible domains. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates how to treat the Pod's nodeAffinity when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are 'Honor' and 'Ignore', with 'Honor' as the default. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Policy for handling node taints when computing topology spread. Allowed values are 'Honor' (only consider nodes that match taints) and 'Ignore' (default, ignore taints). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key of node labels used to group nodes into topology domains for spreading pods; defines the failure domain over which pods are spread. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Determines the action taken when a pod does not satisfy the spread constraint. Valid values are 'DoNotSchedule' (the pod is not scheduled) and 'ScheduleAnyway' (the pod is scheduled anyway, potentially violating the constraint). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.text: List of volumes that can be mounted by containers belonging to the pod. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.aws_ela.text: Represents an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume as a volume source in the pod specification, allowing the pod to mount an AWS EBS volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to mount for the AWS EBS volume, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The partition number of the AWS EBS volume to mount. If omitted, the first partition is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Optional: Defaults to false (read/write). If set to true, the volume is mounted as read-only. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The unique identifier of the AWS EBS volume to mount in the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.azure_d.text: Configuration for an Azure Disk volume that can be attached to the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the caching mode for the Azure disk. Allowed values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Azure data disk to use as a volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The URI of the Azure disk to attach, in the format /subscriptions/{subscription-id}/resourcegroups/{resource-group}/providers/microsoft.compute/disks/{disk-name}. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Filesystem type to mount for the Azure disk volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host OS (e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'). Defaults to 'ext4' if unset. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Kind of the Azure disk. Allowed values are `Managed` (default), `Shared`, and `Unmanaged`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the Azure disk volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; when false (default), it is mounted read-write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.azure_f.text: Represents an Azure File volume source that mounts a Microsoft Azure file share into the pod. Requires a Kubernetes secret containing the Azure storage account name and key, and the share name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mount the Azure File share as read-only. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the Azure Storage account name and key. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Azure File share to be mounted as a volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.cephfs.text: CephFS represents a Ceph Filesystem volume mount that allows a CephFS share to be mounted into a pod. It contains configuration such as monitors, path, user, and secret references for the CephFS mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.cephfs..text: List of Ceph monitor endpoints (hostnames or IP addresses) for the CephFS volume. Required to connect to the Ceph cluster. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path within the CephFS volume to mount. Defaults to "/" if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Marks the CephFS volume as read-only. If true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions; otherwise it is mounted read-write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to the keyring file used for CephFS authentication. Defaults to /etc/ceph/user.secret. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

secretRef is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret that provides the CephFS keyring. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod and contains the key material for accessing the CephFS volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Secret that provides the CephFS credentials. This Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The RADOS user name used for CephFS authentication. If not provided, the default user is 'admin'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.cinder.text: Cinder represents an OpenStack Cinder volume that is mounted as a volume in the pod. It is one of the supported volume sources in Kubernetes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.cinder..text: Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system (e.g., ext4, xfs). Defaults to the volume's filesystem type if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mounts the Cinder volume as read-only when set to true. Defaults to false, meaning the volume is read-write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Reference to a Secret containing Cinder authentication credentials (user and password). The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod. If omitted, default Cinder credentials from the cloud provider are used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the authentication credentials for the Cinder volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The unique ID of the Cinder volume to mount, as defined in OpenStack Cinder. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.config_.text: ConfigMap volume source. Specifies the name of a ConfigMap whose data will be exposed as files in the volume, and optionally, a list of keys to project. If no items are specified, all keys from the ConfigMap are exposed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the file mode (permission bits) applied to files in the ConfigMap volume. If unset, defaults to 0644. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Optional list of key-to-path mappings that specifies which keys of the referenced ConfigMap to project into the volume as files. Each item maps a ConfigMap key to a file path within the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key in the ConfigMap to select. The value corresponding to this key will be mounted at the specified path within the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The permission mode for the file, represented as an integer (e.g., 0644 for owner read/write, group/others read). If omitted, the default mode from the volume is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The relative path within the volume where the config map key's value is mounted. Must not be an absolute path, must not contain '..', and must not start with '..'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ConfigMap to mount as a volume. Must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. When set to true, the volume can be populated even if the referenced ConfigMap or keys are missing, avoiding pod startup errors. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.text: Configures a volume sourced from a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver. This block allows mounting a volume provided by an external CSI driver in the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.dri.text: The name of the CSI driver to use for this volume. This must match the driver name registered with the kubelet. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.fs_.text: Filesystem type to mount (e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'). If omitted, the CSI driver's default filesystem is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.nod.text: Reference to the Kubernetes secret that contains sensitive information needed by the CSI driver to perform the node publish operation. The secret must be in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the secret to use for node publish operations. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.rea.text: Marks the CSI volume as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only access. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.vol.text: Map of attributes to pass to the CSI driver for this volume. These correspond to the volumeAttributes field in the CSI volume source. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.downwar.text: Defines a downward API volume that injects pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and resource limits) into the pod as files accessible to containers. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The permissions, in octal, to set on files in the downward API volume. Defaults to 0644. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of files to expose via the downward API volume, where each item specifies a file path and the corresponding pod or container field (such as metadata or resource limits) to project into that file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The fieldRef is an ObjectFieldSelector that selects a field of the pod (for example, metadata.name or spec.nodeName) whose value is written to the downward API volume file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The API version of the schema that the field_path refers to. For example, 'v1'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to the field in the Pod specification to expose. For example, `metadata.name` or `metadata.labels`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The Unix file permission bits to set on the projected file, expressed as an octal number (e.g., 0644). If not specified, the default is 0644. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Relative path within the volume where the file is created. Must not be absolute and must not contain '..' segments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Reference to a container resource field (like requests.cpu, limits.memory) to be projected into the Downward API volume item. It includes the target container, the resource name, and an optional divisor to scale the value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Name of the container to which the resource field reference applies. Required when using resourceFieldRef to select a container resource (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the divisor for the resource quantity. The resource field value is divided by this divisor before being exposed. Defaults to 1 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Resource is the name of the container resource to expose, such as 'cpu' or 'memory' for requests/limits. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.empty_d.text: Configures a volume of type emptyDir. An emptyDir volume is created empty when the pod is assigned to a node and persists as long as the pod exists. It is commonly used to share data between containers in the same pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume. Use 'Memory' to back the volume with tmpfs (RAM-backed storage); an empty string or no value uses the default disk-backed storage. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a storage size limit for the emptyDir volume as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., "1Gi"). If not set, the volume is limited only by the node's available storage. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.ephemer.text: Configures an ephemeral volume that is created with the pod and deleted when the pod is removed. This is typically used for generic ephemeral volumes (via a PersistentVolumeClaim template) or CSI ephemeral volumes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Template for a PersistentVolumeClaim that will be created for this pod. The claimed volume is ephemeral, with the PVC created when the pod starts and deleted when the pod is removed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Standard Kubernetes object metadata for the PersistentVolumeClaim generated from this volume claim template. Includes fields such as labels, annotations, and name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Annotations is a map of string keys and values that can be used to attach arbitrary non-identifying metadata to the ephemeral volume claim template's metadata. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The server-generated timestamp (RFC3339, UTC) indicating when the PersistentVolumeClaim is created. This field is read-only and cannot be set by clients. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The timestamp (in RFC3339 format) at which the object was marked for deletion. This field is set when deletion has been requested and the object is still being terminated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of finalizer names. Finalizers prevent the deletion of the object until all finalizers are removed, enabling cleanup before deletion. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

generate_name is an optional prefix for generating a unique name for the volume claim template when name is not specified. The Kubernetes API server appends a random string to this prefix to create a unique name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state. This field is set by the system and is read-only. It monotonically increases each time the desired state of the object is changed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Labels to attach to the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this template. These labels help select and organize the generated PVCs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

managedFields is a list of managed fields entries. Each entry records the manager, operation, and the fields that the manager owns, used for field management and conflict resolution. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The Kubernetes API version against which the managed fields in this entry were recorded. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The type of the fields in this managed field set, typically 'FieldsV1'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The set of fields managed by the manager, represented as a JSON object mapping field paths to their values. This is part of the Kubernetes ManagedFieldsEntry and allows tracking of field ownership. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the manager (e.g., kubectl, a controller) that last applied this managed field set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The type of operation that created this managed fields entry. Allowed values are 'Apply' and 'Update'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the subresource that the operation was performed on, if any. For example, 'status' when the field manager updated the status subresource. Empty when the operation was on the main resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp of when the managed field entry was last updated, in RFC3339 format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The namespace in which the volume claim template should be created. If omitted, it defaults to the namespace of the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of references to owning objects. If all owners are deleted, this object may be garbage collected, subject to the owner reference policy (e.g., blockOwnerDeletion and controller flags). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The API version of the referenced owner object (e.g., 'v1', 'apps/v1'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, the owner reference blocks deletion of the dependent object until the owner is deleted, as defined by Kubernetes OwnerReference semantics. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A boolean flag indicating whether this owner reference is the controlling owner. If true, the referenced object is the controller of the dependent resource, and only one controller can exist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The kind of the owner object (e.g., ReplicaSet, DaemonSet). Must match the kind of the referenced object. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the referenced owner object. This is required when creating an owner reference. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The unique identifier (UID) of the owner object referenced by this owner reference. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The version of the resource as maintained by the server. This value is used for optimistic concurrency and changes on every write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A URL referencing the object itself, used for API navigation. In Kubernetes, this field is deprecated and may be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The unique identifier assigned by the Kubernetes API server to the persistent volume claim created from this template. This value is generated by the server and is not user-configurable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

spec defines the desired characteristics of the persistent volume claim to be created, such as access modes, resource requests, storage class, and volume mode. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.text: Represents a Fibre Channel volume source, allowing the Pod to mount a Fibre Channel storage device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.fs_t.text: Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. If not specified, the default filesystem type of the underlying volume is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.lun.text: An integer representing the logical unit number (LUN) of the Fibre Channel target volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.read.text: If true, the Fibre Channel volume is mounted as read-only. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.targ.text: The list of Fibre Channel target World Wide Names (WWNs) that the volume will connect to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.wwid.text: List of Fibre Channel World Wide Identifiers (WWIDs) used to identify the volume. Either wwids or targetWWNs must be set, but not both. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.flex_vo.text: Configuration block for a FlexVolume volume source. This allows a Pod to mount a volume using a FlexVolume driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the name of the FlexVolume driver to use for this volume. This driver must be installed on the host and is responsible for mounting and unmounting the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The filesystem type to be mounted by the FlexVolume, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. If unspecified, it defaults to ext4. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Options is a map of additional command-line arguments to pass to the flexvolume plugin. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, the FlexVolume is mounted as read-only, preventing write operations to the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

secret_ref is an optional reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains sensitive information, such as credentials, to be used by the FlexVolume driver. It references a Secret object in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the secret. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.flocker.text: Defines a Flocker volume source for a Kubernetes pod volume, which mounts a Flocker dataset into the pod. This is a supported volume type in the pod's spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Flocker dataset to be used for this volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to mount. This uniquely identifies the dataset, as an alternative to datasetName. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.gce_per.text: Configures a Google Compute Engine Persistent Disk as a volume source for the pod. This allows the pod to mount a GCE Persistent Disk that exists in the same GCP project, with options for filesystem type, partition, and read-only access. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The filesystem type to mount on the Google Compute Engine persistent disk, such as ext4 or xfs. Defaults to ext4 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk to mount. If omitted, the entire disk is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the GCE persistent disk to mount. This corresponds to the `pdName` field in the Kubernetes GCEPersistentDiskVolumeSource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Marks the GCE persistent disk volume as read-only, preventing writes from the pod to the volume. Defaults to false (read-write). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.git_rep.text: Represents a Git repository volume source. It specifies the repository URL, revision, and optional directory to mount; this volume source is deprecated in favor of using an init container to clone the repository. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Target directory name for the git repo volume. Must not contain or start with '..'. If '.' is supplied, the volume directory will be the git repository; otherwise, the volume will contain the git repository in the subdirectory with the given name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL of the git repository to clone into the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The commit hash (revision) of the Git repository to checkout for this volume. This selects a specific commit, tag, or branch from the repository. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.gluster.text: Glusterfs represents a Glusterfs mount that lasts the lifetime of a pod. It configures a volume sourced from a GlusterFS cluster. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Kubernetes Endpoints object that represents the GlusterFS cluster. This field is required. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to the GlusterFS volume, identifying the specific volume within the GlusterFS cluster. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the GlusterFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.host_pa.text: Configures a hostPath volume, which mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod. The object specifies the path on the host and the type of mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path on the host node to mount into the pod for a hostPath volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The type of the hostPath volume, controlling how the host path is checked or created. Possible values include: '', Directory, DirectoryOrCreate, File, FileOrCreate, Socket. For example, 'Directory' ensures the path exists and is a directory. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.image.text: Image represents an OCI image volume source. This volume is backed by an OCI image, and its content is mounted read-only into the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.image.p.text: Specifies the image pull policy for this image volume source. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never, controlling when the image is pulled. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.image.r.text: The image reference to use for this volume, such as 'nginx:latest' or 'registry.example.com/app:v1'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.iscsi.text: Represents an iSCSI volume, used to attach a block storage device accessible via iSCSI. It includes configuration such as target portal, IQN, LUN, and filesystem type. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.iscsi.c.text: Whether to enable CHAP authentication for iSCSI target discovery. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Enables CHAP authentication for the iSCSI session. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.iscsi.f.text: Filesystem type to be mounted on the ISCSI volume (e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs'). If unspecified, the default filesystem type is inferred to be 'ext4'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.iscsi.i.text: Custom iSCSI initiator name. If not set, the system default initiator name is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the target. Must be a valid IQN, typically of the form iqn.yyyy-mm.reverse.domain:identifier. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The iSCSI interface to use. Defaults to 'default'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.iscsi.l.text: The iSCSI target's logical unit number (LUN) that the volume will use. It is a required integer identifying the specific logical unit to connect to on the target. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.iscsi.p.text: List of additional iSCSI portals (IP addresses or hostnames) for multipath connectivity. The primary portal is specified by targetPortal. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.iscsi.r.text: ReadOnly here will force the ReadOnly setting in VolumeMounts. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.iscsi.s.text: secretRef is a reference to a Secret object that contains CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI volume. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Secret containing CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI volume. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.iscsi.t.text: The iSCSI target portal. This is the IP address or hostname of the iSCSI target, optionally with a port number (ip:port) when using a non-default port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.name.text: Name of the volume, used to reference it in container volumeMounts. Must be a DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.nfs.text: NFS volume source for mounting a Network File System export. Specify the NFS server and path in this object to make the share available to the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.nfs.pat.text: Path that is exported by the NFS server. Must be an absolute path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.nfs.rea.text: Indicates whether the NFS volume is mounted read-only. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.nfs.ser.text: The hostname or IP address of the NFS server that exports the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.persist.text: Configures the volume to reference a PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace, using the claimName field to specify which claim to mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim resource in the same namespace that this volume should use. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the persistent volume claim is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.photon_.text: Defines a Photon Controller persistent disk volume source, allowing a pod to mount a Photon persistent disk by referencing its disk ID (pdID) and optional filesystem type (fsType). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The unique identifier of the Photon persistent disk to mount as a volume. This corresponds to the `pdID` field in the Kubernetes PhotonPersistentDiskVolumeSource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.portwor.text: Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If unspecified, defaults to 'ext4'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mounts the Portworx volume as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions, preventing writes from the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The ID of the Portworx volume to mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.project.text: Projected volume source that combines multiple existing volume sources into a single directory within the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

defaultMode is the mode bits used to set permissions on created files by default. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal 0-511); defaults to 0644. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the list of volume sources to project into the same directory. Each entry can be a secret, configMap, downwardAPI, or serviceAccountToken. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The `cluster_trust_bundle` block configures a projected volume source that injects a Kubernetes ClusterTrustBundle into the container's file system, selected by name, signer name, or label selector, and mounted at a specified path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Label selector used to filter ClusterTrustBundle objects by their labels. When specified, only ClusterTrustBundles matching this selector are projected into the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements used to filter ClusterTrustBundle resources by their labels. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the match expression applies to. This is the Kubernetes label key used in the label selector requirement. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator used to evaluate the label selector match expression, such as In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values that correspond to the label selector match expression. This field is required when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn' and must be empty for operators 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ClusterTrustBundle resource to project into the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
