Optional specifies whether the ClusterTrustBundle can be omitted from the pod. When set to true, the pod will still start even if the referenced ClusterTrustBundle does not exist; when false, the pod will be blocked if the ClusterTrustBundle is missing. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Relative path within the projected volume to mount the trust bundle. Must be a relative path, not absolute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the signer for the ClusterTrustBundle to be projected. For example, 'kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-bundle'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The config_map field defines a ConfigMap source for a projected volume, allowing the contents of a Kubernetes ConfigMap to be exposed as files in the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Optional list of key-to-path mappings that specifies which ConfigMap keys to project and their target paths. If omitted, all keys from the selected ConfigMap are projected. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key in the ConfigMap's data to project into the volume. This is the name of the entry in the ConfigMap's data map that will be exposed as a file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Optional mode bits used to set permissions on this file. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (decimal 0 and 511). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The relative path within the projected volume where the config map item's data is exposed. This path is relative to the volume's root directory. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the referenced ConfigMap. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specify whether the referenced ConfigMap and its keys must be defined. If true, the pod will start even if the ConfigMap or some of its keys are missing. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
downwardAPI configures a projected volume source that exposes Pod and container metadata as files to the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of downward API volume files. Each item defines a path and a field reference or resource field reference to populate. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

field_ref selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.labels, spec.nodeName, status.podIP) to expose as a file in the projected volume. It uses the ObjectFieldSelector schema. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
API version of the schema the field_path is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to the Pod field to expose, using dot notation like 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The file permission mode bits, expressed as an integer (e.g., 0644). If not set, the mode of the source item is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The relative path of the file within the projected volume where the downward API field value is exposed. The path must not contain '..' and must be a valid POSIX path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a resource field (e.g., CPU or memory limits/requests) of a container in the pod to be exposed via the downward API volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the container for which the resource field is requested. If omitted, this defaults to the first container in the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Divisor is a string representing a quantity (e.g., '1', '100m', '1Ki') by which the resource value is divided to produce the output value. If not specified, defaults to 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The resource name to select, such as `limits.cpu` or `requests.memory`, from the container's resource requirements. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path relative to the volume mount where the certificate chain is exposed for the pod certificate projection. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path within the projected volume where the private key for the pod certificate is mounted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The type of private key used for the pod certificate. Valid values are 'rsa' and 'ec'. Defaults to 'rsa'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The maximum validity period for the projected pod certificate, in seconds. This limits the lifetime of the issued certificate. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the certificate signer to use when requesting the pod certificate. This specifies which signer will issue the certificate, and must correspond to a signer name registered in the cluster. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Projected volume source that populates the volume from a Secret. Specify the secret name and optionally items to select paths from the secret. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of key-to-path mappings. Each item specifies a key in the referenced Secret and the relative path within the projected volume where that key's value should be written. Unlisted keys are not projected. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The key in the secret's data map to include in the projected volume. This selects the specific entry from the Secret's data field to expose at the corresponding path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The permission mode bits (in octal) for the file created from this secret item. If omitted, the volume's default mode is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The relative path in the volume where the value of the secret key is mounted. If omitted, the key name is used as the path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Secret to project into the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, the secret is optional, and the volume mount will succeed even if the secret does not exist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The service account token configuration for this projected volume source. This selects a Kubernetes ServiceAccountTokenProjection, which injects the service account token into the volume at a specified path with optional audience and expiration settings. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Audience is the intended audience of the service account token. A recipient of the token must identify itself with an identifier specified in the audience, and otherwise should reject the token. If not specified, the audience defaults to the identifier of the API server. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The duration in seconds before the projected service account token expires. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Path (relative to the volume root) where the service account token file will be mounted. Must be a relative path and cannot contain '..' to escape the volume directory. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.quobyte.text: Represents a Quobyte volume source to be mounted into the pod. This configures the volume to use a Quobyte storage system. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Group to map volume access to. Defaults to 'default' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, forces the Quobyte volume to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Registry represents a single or multiple Quobyte Registry services specified as a string in the format host:port pair (multiple entries separated by commas). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The Quobyte tenant that owns the volume. This is an optional field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The user to map volume access to for this Quobyte volume. If not specified, the default service account user is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Quobyte volume to mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.rbd.text: rbd configures a Rados Block Device (Ceph) volume. It allows the pod to mount a Ceph block device as a volume, specifying details like the Ceph monitors, image name, and filesystem type. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.rbd.fs_.text: Filesystem type to be used when mounting the RBD volume, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If not specified, the default filesystem type is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.rbd.ima.text: The name of the RBD image to mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.rbd.key.text: Path to the keyring file used for authentication with the Ceph cluster. Defaults to /etc/ceph/keyring if not set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.rbd.mon.text: A list of Ceph monitor addresses (hostnames or IPs) that the RBD volume will connect to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.rbd.poo.text: The name of the RBD pool. If not specified, the default is 'rbd'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.rbd.rea.text: Indicates whether the RBD volume is mounted as read-only on the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.rbd.sec.text: secret_ref is an object reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the Ceph authentication key for accessing the RBD image. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the secret that contains the authentication key for the RBD volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.rbd.use.text: The RADOS user name for the RBD volume. Defaults to 'admin'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.scale_i.text: Volume source that represents a ScaleIO storage volume to be mounted into the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to mount for the ScaleIO volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host, e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs', or 'ntfs'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host address of the ScaleIO API Gateway. This is required for accessing the ScaleIO system to provision the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The ScaleIO protection domain in which the storage pool resides. This determines the scope of storage resources used for the volume. If not specified, the default 'default' protection domain is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the ScaleIO volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume becomes read-only; defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the ScaleIO credentials required to access the storage system. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the secret in the pod's namespace that contains the ScaleIO credentials. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether SSL is enabled for communication with the ScaleIO storage backend. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the provisioning mode for the ScaleIO volume. Allowed values are 'ThinProvisioned' (default) and 'ThickProvisioned', controlling how storage is allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Storage Pool in which the ScaleIO volume should be created. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ScaleIO system (the storage cluster) to attach the volume from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ScaleIO volume to mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.secret.text: Configuration for a Kubernetes Secret volume source, allowing the Pod to mount a Secret as a volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.secret..text: The default file mode in octal for files exposed by the secret volume. Must be an integer between 0 and 0777 (e.g., 0644). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Maps specific keys from the secret to file paths in the volume. Each item can specify the key, the target path, and optional file mode permissions. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key in the Secret's data map whose value is exposed as a file. This is used when a Secret volume is configured with specific items to include. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Mode is the permission bits (file mode) for the item file, specified as an octal number (e.g., 0644). It defines read/write/execute access for owner, group, and others. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The relative path inside the volume where the secret key's value is written as a file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specify whether the referenced Secret or its keys must be defined. If true, a missing Secret or missing keys will not cause the Pod to fail and the corresponding volume is ignored. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Secret to use as the volume source. This must correspond to a Secret in the same namespace as the Pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.storage.text: Represents a StorageOS volume source in a Kubernetes pod volume. When specified, this configures the pod to mount a volume from a StorageOS storage system. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, such as "ext4", "xfs", or "ntfs". If not specified, the filesystem type is inferred from the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
When true, the StorageOS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A reference to a Secret object in the same namespace that contains the StorageOS API credentials. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the secret that contains the credentials for the StorageOS volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the StorageOS volume to mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The namespace within the StorageOS cluster where the volume is located. Defaults to the pod's namespace if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.vsphere.text: Configuration for a vSphere (VMware) volume that can be attached to a pod. This is a volume source type used to mount storage from a vSphere Cloud Provider. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to mount for the vSphere volume, such as ext4, xfs, or ext3. Defaults to ext4 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

storage_policy_id is the identifier of the vSphere Storage Policy Based Management (SPBM) policy to apply to the volume. It determines storage characteristics such as performance and availability. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the vSphere storage policy to use with this volume. If not specified, the default storage policy is applied. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path of the vSphere volume, typically in the format '[datastore_name] path/to/volume'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.text: PodStatus represents information about the status of a pod. Status may trail the actual state of a system, especially if the node that hosts the pod cannot contact the control plane. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.allocated_res.text: AllocatedResources is the total requests allocated for this pod by the node. If pod-level requests are not set, this will be the total requests aggregated across containers in the pod. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.conditions.text: Current service state of pod. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#pod-conditions Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.conditions.la.text: The timestamp (RFC3339) of the last time this condition was probed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This is typically represented as an RFC3339 timestamp string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.conditions.me.text: Human-readable message indicating details about the condition's last transition. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.conditions.re.text: A machine-readable, CamelCase reason for the condition's last transition. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.conditions.st.text: The status of the condition, indicating whether the condition is currently True, False, or Unknown. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.conditions.ty.text: The type of pod condition, typically one of PodScheduled, Ready, Initialized, or ContainersReady. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.container_sta.text: Statuses of containers in this pod. Each container in the pod should have at most one status in this list, and all statuses should be for containers in the pod. However this is not enforced. If a status for a non-existent container is present in the list, or the list has duplicate names, the behavior of various Kubernetes components is not defined and those statuses might be ignored. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#pod-and-container-status Optional.
The resources allocated to the container, such as CPU and memory, expressed as a map of resource names to the allocated quantities (in string form). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource to which this status applies, such as cpu, memory, or a named device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of health statuses for the resources allocated to the container, where each entry includes a resource ID and its health condition (e.g., Healthy, Unhealthy). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A human-readable message providing details about the status of the resource claim allocated to the container, such as an error or warning message. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The unique identifier of an allocated resource, such as a device ID or resource handle, as reported by the resource driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The unique identifier of the container, including the container runtime prefix (e.g., 'docker://', 'containerd://'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container image reference (e.g., `nginx:latest`) used by this container, as reported in its status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The image ID (digest) of the container image, as reported by the container runtime. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The last terminated state of the container, if any, including details like exit code, reason, and timestamps from the previous run. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents the running state of the container, containing details such as the start time. This field is populated when the container is in a running state, and is part of the last observed state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp indicating when the container was last started in its current running state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Represents the state of a container that has terminated, containing details such as exit code, reason, and timestamps. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The runtime-specific identifier of the terminated container, typically in the format <runtime>://<container-id> (e.g., docker://abc123). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The exit code returned by the container when it last terminated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The time at which the container terminated or completed its execution. Represented as a string in RFC3339 format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A human-readable message providing additional details about the container's termination, such as why it exited. This field is set by Kubernetes when the container terminates with a non-zero exit code or due to an error. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A brief, human-readable reason why the container terminated, such as 'OOMKilled' or 'Completed'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The numeric signal number that caused the container to terminate, if it was terminated by a signal (e.g., 9 for SIGKILL, 15 for SIGTERM). This field is set only when a signal was the termination cause. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp (in RFC3339 UTC format) indicating when the terminated container started. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents the last observed waiting state of the container. This object provides details (reason and message) explaining why the container is waiting rather than running. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A human-readable message indicating details about why the container is in the waiting state, providing context for the container's last state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A brief reason why the container is in the waiting state, such as 'ContainerCreating' or 'CrashLoopBackOff'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the container within the pod, matching the container name defined in the pod's spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the container is currently passing its readiness probe, meaning it is ready to accept traffic. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of resource claim references that the container requires. Each claim identifies a ResourceClaim object by name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource claim, which must correspond to a ResourceClaim object in the pod's namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Limits specifies the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Keys are resource names such as 'cpu' or 'memory', and values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '500m', '1Gi'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of resource names (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') to the quantity requested for the container. These specify the minimum amount of each resource that the container requires. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of times the container has restarted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the container has started its main process. This is true once the container has been launched, even if it subsequently exited. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The current state of the container, represented as an object that contains one of waiting, running, or terminated sub-statuses, with details such as reason, message, or exit code specific to that state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The running state of the container, containing details such as the time it was last started. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp (RFC3339 format) indicating when the container started running. Present when the container is in the Running state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Represents the state of a container that has terminated, with details about the termination such as exit code, reason, and timestamps. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The unique identifier of the container that has terminated, as assigned by the container runtime (e.g., containerd or Docker). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The exit code of the container process when it terminated. Typically, zero indicates success and non-zero indicates an error. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The time at which the container terminated, in RFC 3339 format (e.g., 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z). This field is set only when the container is in the terminated state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Message regarding the last termination of the container, providing details on why it terminated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The reason the container's termination occurred, such as `OOMKilled`, `Completed`, or `Error`. This field provides a brief, machine-readable cause for the terminated state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The signal number that caused the container to terminate, if the termination was due to a signal. For example, SIGTERM (15) or SIGKILL (9). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The timestamp indicating when the container started, in RFC3339 format. This is part of the terminated state, providing the start time for a container that has since terminated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The waiting state of the container, containing a human-readable reason and message explaining why the container is not yet running. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The message detail from the waiting state, indicating why the container is waiting (e.g., pulling image, container creating). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The reason the container is in the waiting state, such as 'CrashLoopBackOff' or 'ImagePullBackOff'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Linux-specific user information for the container, including UID, GID, and supplemental groups. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The numeric group ID (GID) of the Linux user under which the container runs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of supplementary group IDs (GIDs) assigned to the container's Linux user, in addition to the primary group, for permission checks. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The numeric Unix user ID (UID) that the container's processes run with in the Linux namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path inside the container at which the volume is mounted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume mount, matching the name of a volume defined in the pod specification. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the container can only read from the mount; if false, it can read and write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

recursiveReadOnly indicates whether recursive read-only mounts are enabled for this volume mount. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', or 'IfPossible'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The reference of the image used for the volume image, such as a container image name and tag (e.g., 'nginx:latest'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.ephemeral_con.text: Statuses for any ephemeral containers that have run in this pod. Each ephemeral container in the pod should have at most one status in this list, and all statuses should be for containers in the pod. However this is not enforced. If a status for a non-existent container is present in the list, or the list has duplicate names, the behavior of various Kubernetes components is not defined and those statuses might be ignored. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#pod-and-container-status Optional.

The set of resources (such as CPU and memory) allocated to the ephemeral container, represented as a map from resource name to the allocated quantity (a string in Kubernetes quantity format). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the allocated resource, such as cpu or memory. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Health status of the resource. Valid values are 'Healthy' or 'Unhealthy'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The unique identifier of the resource allocated to the ephemeral container, as reported in the allocated resources status (e.g., device ID or volume name). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container ID of the ephemeral container, as reported by the container runtime. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The image the ephemeral container is running with, as reported in its container status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Image ID of the ephemeral container's image, as reported by the container runtime. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The state of the previous instance of the ephemeral container before the most recent restart. This object holds the same sub-structure as the current state (waiting, running, or terminated) and is populated only after a restart occurs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Represents the running state of the container. Populated when the container is currently running, and includes details such as the start time. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp indicating when the Kubernetes ephemeral container last entered the running state, in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The last observed terminated state of the container, containing details such as exit code, signal, reason, message, and the timestamps for when the container started and finished termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container ID of the terminated ephemeral container, as reported by the container runtime. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The exit code returned by the container when it last terminated, as reported by the container runtime. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The time at which the container terminated, in RFC3339 format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Human-readable message indicating details about why the container terminated. This is typically the container's termination message, if any. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A brief reason for the container's termination, as reported by the kubelet. Common values include 'OOMKilled', 'Completed', 'Error', etc. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The Unix signal number that caused the process to terminate, if it was killed by a signal. For example, 9 (SIGKILL) or 15 (SIGTERM). Not set if the container exited normally. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp at which the container was started, expressed as a string in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The waiting state of the ephemeral container. It includes a reason and message describing why the container is in a waiting state, such as a missing dependency or an image pull issue. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Message regarding why the container is not yet running. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The reason the container is waiting, such as 'CrashLoopBackOff' or 'ErrImagePull'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ephemeral container that this status describes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Ready indicates whether the ephemeral container is ready to serve requests. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of resource claims that specify additional resources required by the ephemeral container. Each claim references a ResourceClaim defined in the Pod's spec by name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ResourceClaim that this resource entry refers to. Must match the name of a ResourceClaim in the same namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of a specific request within the referenced ResourceClaim, used to allocate a particular request when the claim provides multiple options. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Each key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the value is a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '100m', '1Gi'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Map of resource request names to quantities (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') that specify the minimum amount of compute resources required for the ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of times the ephemeral container has been restarted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A boolean indicating whether the ephemeral container has started successfully. It becomes true after the container has been started and remains true even if the container subsequently exits. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
State represents the current status of the ephemeral container, including details of its waiting, running, or terminated phase. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents the running state of the ephemeral container. Contains the timestamp (startedAt) when the container started running, populated when the container is in the running state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp at which the ephemeral container started running, expressed in RFC 3339 format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The terminated state of the ephemeral container, containing details about its termination including exit code, reason, and timestamps (started at and finished at). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The unique identifier of the terminated ephemeral container, as assigned by the container runtime. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The exit code returned by the container process when it terminated. A value of 0 indicates success, while non-zero values indicate an error or abnormal termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp (in RFC3339 format) indicating when the container terminated. This field is set when the container process exits. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A human-readable message providing additional details about why the container terminated, such as an error or exit reason. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Human-readable reason for the container's termination, such as OOMKilled or Error. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The numeric signal code (if any) that caused the ephemeral container's termination. This field is set when the container was terminated by a signal rather than exiting with an exit code. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The time at which the container was started, in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents the waiting state of the ephemeral container. This block provides the reason and message explaining why the container is not yet running (e.g., pulling image, waiting to start). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A human-readable message providing details about why the container is in the waiting state. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A short, machine-readable reason for why the container is in a waiting state, such as ErrImagePull or CrashLoopBackOff. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The effective user of the container process, if known. This object contains platform-specific user identity information, such as Linux (UID, GID) or Windows (username). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Object that specifies Linux-specific user attributes for the ephemeral container, such as UID and GID. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The group ID (GID) of the Linux user under which the ephemeral container's process runs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Supplemental group IDs (GIDs) assigned to the container process in addition to its primary group. These are Linux group IDs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The user ID (UID) of the Linux user that the container process runs as. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Volume mounts specifies how storage volumes are mounted into the ephemeral container's filesystem. Each entry defines a volume name and the mount path within the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path within the ephemeral container at which the volume is mounted, e.g., '/var/log'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume mounted. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Whether the volume is mounted read-only for the ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the volume mount is made recursively read-only. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', and 'IfPossible', controlling the recursive read-only behavior of the mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container image reference (e.g., `nginx:latest` or a digest) for the image-backed volume mounted by the ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.extended_reso.text: PodExtendedResourceClaimStatus is stored in the PodStatus for the extended resource requests backed by DRA. It stores the generated name for the corresponding special ResourceClaim created by the scheduler. Optional.
RequestMappings identifies the mapping of <container, extended resource backed by DRA> to device request in the generated ResourceClaim. Required.
The name of the container that this extended resource claim request mapping applies to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the resource claim request as defined in the pod's specification. It serves as the key in the mapping to associate the request with the actual resource claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the specific resource that fulfills the extended resource claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
ResourceClaimName is the name of the ResourceClaim that was generated for the Pod in the namespace of the Pod. Required.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.host_ip.text: hostIP holds the IP address of the host to which the pod is assigned. Empty if the pod has not started yet. A pod can be assigned to a node that has a problem in kubelet which in turns mean that HostIP will not be updated even if there is a node is assigned to pod Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.host_ips.text: hostIPs holds the IP addresses allocated to the host. If this field is specified, the first entry must match the hostIP field. This list is empty if the pod has not started yet. A pod can be assigned to a node that has a problem in kubelet which in turns means that HostIPs will not be updated even if there is a node is assigned to this pod. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.host_ips.ip.text: The IP address of the host node on which the pod is running. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.init_containe.text: Statuses of init containers in this pod. The most recent successful non-restartable init container will have ready = true, the most recently started container will have startTime set. Each init container in the pod should have at most one status in this list, and all statuses should be for containers in the pod. However this is not enforced. If a status for a non-existent container is present in the list, or the list has duplicate names, the behavior of various Kubernetes components is not defined and those statuses might be ignored. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#pod-and-container-status Optional.

The resources allocated to the init container, such as cpu and memory, specified as a map of resource names to quantities in Kubernetes resource quantity format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') whose allocated status is reported in this entry. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of resources allocated to the init container, as reported in its allocated resources status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Health status of the allocated resource, indicating whether it is Healthy, Unhealthy, or Unknown. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Identifies the specific resource instance allocated to the container, such as a device ID for device-level resources. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container ID of the init container, in the format `<runtime>://<container_id>` (e.g., `docker://abc123`), as reported by the container runtime. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container image that the init container is running. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The image ID of the container image used by the init container, as reported by the container runtime. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The last observed state of the init container before its current state. This typically reflects the previous run's terminated state, including details such as exit code, reason, and message. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Represents the details of the container's last running state, such as its start timestamp. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The time at which the init container's last running state started, in RFC3339 format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents the terminated state of a container, providing details such as exit code, termination reason, and timestamps for when the container started and finished. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container ID of the terminated container, in the format <runtime>://<container_id>. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The exit code returned by the container process when it terminated. A non-zero value typically indicates a failure. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The time at which the container terminated, in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A human-readable message providing details about the reason for the init container's termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A brief reason for the container's last termination, such as 'OOMKilled' or 'Completed', providing a human-readable explanation for why the container exited. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The Unix signal number that caused the container to terminate, if it was killed by a signal; otherwise 0 or unset. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp (RFC3339) at which the container was started. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents the waiting state of a container in Kubernetes, indicating that the container is not yet running and is waiting for a condition such as image pull or dependency readiness. This object contains details like a reason and a human-readable message. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Human-readable message indicating details about why the container is in the waiting state. This field provides additional context about the reason, such as an error message or conditions preventing the container from starting. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A machine-readable reason for the container being in the waiting state, such as 'CrashLoopBackOff', 'ErrImagePull', or 'ImagePullBackOff'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the init container to which this status belongs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A boolean value indicating whether the init container is ready, meaning it has completed its initialization successfully. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.nominated_nod.text: nominatedNodeName is set only when this pod preempts other pods on the node, but it cannot be scheduled right away as preemption victims receive their graceful termination periods. This field does not guarantee that the pod will be scheduled on this node. Scheduler may decide to place the pod elsewhere if other nodes become available sooner. Scheduler may also decide to give the resources on this node to a higher priority pod that is created after preemption. As a result, this field may be different than PodSpec.nodeName when the pod is scheduled. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.observed_gene.text: If set, this represents the .metadata.generation that the pod status was set based upon. The PodObservedGenerationTracking feature gate must be enabled to use this field. Optional.

kubernetes_core_pod.status.phase.text: The phase of a Pod is a simple, high-level summary of where the Pod is in its lifecycle. The conditions array, the reason and message fields, and the individual container status arrays contain more detail about the pod's status. There are five possible phase values: Pending: The pod has been accepted by the Kubernetes system, but one or more of the container images has not been created. This includes time before being scheduled as well as time spent downloading images over the network, which could take a while. Running: The pod has been bound to a node, and all of the containers have been created. At least one container is still running, or is in the process of starting or restarting. Succeeded: All containers in the pod have terminated in success, and will not be restarted. Failed: All containers in the pod have terminated, and at least one container has terminated in failure. The container either exited with non-zero status or was terminated by the system. Unknown: For some reason the state of the pod could not be obtained, typically due to an error in communicating with the host of the pod. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#pod-phase Optional.

The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy the affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose a node that violates one or more of the expressions. The node that is most preferred is the one with the greatest sum of weights, i.e. for each node that meets all of the scheduling requirements (resource request, requiredDuringScheduling affinity expressions, etc.), compute a sum by iterating through the elements of this field and adding "weight" to the sum if the node matches the corresponding matchExpressions; the node(s) with the highest sum are the most preferred. Optional.

Defines the operator for the match expression, such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, or Lt. It specifies the relationship between the label key and the specified values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy the affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose a node that violates one or more of the expressions. When there are multiple elements, the lists of nodes corresponding to each podAffinityTerm are intersected, i.e. all terms must be satisfied. Optional.

The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy the anti-affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose a node that violates one or more of the expressions. A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement matches a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, or DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. All requirements are logically ANDed to form the complete selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that this match expression applies to. This is the label key against which the operator and value list are evaluated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values that the label selector requirement matches. This is used with operators such as In or NotIn; it must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist operators. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of key-value pairs. The selector matches resources (e.g., pods) that have all specified labels with exact values, used to select pods for the affinity/anti-affinity rule. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a list of pod label keys to match when selecting pods. Only these label keys are considered when determining pod affinity/anti-affinity, and they are combined with the label selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A label selector for namespaces to consider for pod anti-affinity. If omitted, only namespaces of the pods in the cluster are considered. This selector matches against the labels of namespaces. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The namespace selector matches namespaces whose labels satisfy all the requirements in this list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector operates on. Must be a valid Kubernetes label key. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator to use for the label selector. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values for the label selector expression. For operators like In and NotIn, this list contains the allowed or excluded label values. For Exists and DoesNotExist, values must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A map of label keys and values used to select namespaces. The pod affinity term applies to namespaces matching all specified labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The namespaces to which the label selector applies. If omitted or empty, the selector applies to the pod's own namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The key of the node label that defines the topology domain. Nodes with the same label value are considered part of the same domain for this affinity term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The weight associated with the pod anti-affinity term. Must be an integer between 1 and 100. It determines the relative importance of this term when ranking nodes for preferred scheduling. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

If the anti-affinity requirements specified by this field are not met at scheduling time, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node. When there are multiple elements, the lists of nodes corresponding to each podAffinityTerm are intersected, i.e. all terms must be satisfied. Optional.

A label selector used to identify the pods that the anti-affinity rule applies to. This ensures the pod is scheduled away from pods matching these labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements that define the pods the anti-affinity rule applies to. Each requirement consists of a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, or DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector operates on. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values that the label key must match for the operator. For operators 'In' and 'NotIn', this must be non-empty; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', this must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of pod label keys to select which topology domains the pod should NOT be scheduled in. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A label selector that identifies which namespaces the pod anti-affinity term applies to. If omitted, it applies to the namespace of the pod being scheduled. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values, and all requirements are combined with a logical AND. Used to select namespaces by their labels for pod anti-affinity. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The label key that the selector matches against. In namespace selectors, this is the key of a label on the namespace object that the match expression evaluates. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines the relationship between the key and the set of values in the match expression. Supported values are `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, and `DoesNotExist`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values that the key must match according to the operator. Required for 'In' and 'NotIn' operators; must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist' operators. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of label keys and values that a namespace must have to be selected. The namespace selector matches namespaces whose labels include all specified key-value pairs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A static list of namespaces that the anti-affinity term applies to. If neither this field nor namespaceSelector is specified, the term applies to the pod's own namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of environment variables to set in the container. Each item defines a variable name and its value or value source. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the environment variable as a literal string. This should not be set if value_from is specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the ConfigMap to select a key from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Optional name of the container to select the resource from. If empty, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The divisor to divide the resource value by. Defaults to 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The resource name to select, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'. This specifies which resource quantity of the container is exposed as the environment variable value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects a key from a Kubernetes Secret to provide the value for the environment variable. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod, and the referenced key must be present in that Secret. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the referenced secret to select the value from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Secret in the pod's namespace to select the key from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If set to true, the container can start even if the secret or key does not exist, and the value is treated as an empty string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of sources to populate environment variables from. Each item defines a ConfigMap or Secret reference, allowing environment variables to be set from those sources. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies an action involving a gRPC port, used to perform a gRPC health check as part of the readiness probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port number on the container that the gRPC readiness probe will connect to for performing the health check. This should be the port on which the container's gRPC server is listening. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health checking protocol. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

HTTP GET action to perform against a container path and port. Used by the readiness probe to determine if the container is ready based on the HTTP response status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP address if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a list of HTTP headers to include in the readiness probe request. Each item is an object with `name` and `value` fields defining a custom header. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request, such as 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header that will be sent in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request. Specifies the value for the header named by the 'name' field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP path to request on the container's server, e.g., /healthz. If not specified, defaults to /. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number or name of the container port to send the HTTP GET request to. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET probe. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; the minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the readiness probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Defaults to 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a TCP socket probe configuration for the readiness probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container; the probe succeeds if the connection is established. This is an alternative to HTTP and exec probes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Optional host name to connect to for the TCP probe; defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port number or named port to connect to for the readiness probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The duration in seconds that a pod is allowed to gracefully terminate after receiving a termination signal before it is forcibly killed. This field is part of the pod specification, not the readiness probe configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; the minimum allowed value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of resource resize policies for the container. Each policy defines how a specific resource (e.g., CPU or memory) should be resized and whether the container must be restarted for the change to take effect. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the restart policy for the container when its resource limits are resized, as defined in the container's resize policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the compute resource requirements for the container, such as requests and limits for CPU and memory, which the scheduler uses to determine placement and the kubelet uses to enforce constraints. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of ResourceClaim references that the container requires. Each claim specifies the name of a ResourceClaim object in the pod's namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ResourceClaim that this container requires. This name must match a ResourceClaim in the same namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ResourceClaim that this container requests. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to the maximum amount of that resource that the container is allowed to use. Values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '500m', '2Gi'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of minimum resource requests for the container, with resource names (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') as keys and Kubernetes quantity strings as values (e.g., '100m', '1Gi'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Operator used to define the matching condition between a container's exit code and the specified values in the restart policy rule. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of numeric exit codes that define the condition for this restart policy rule. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines the security settings for the container, including user and group IDs, Linux capabilities, and other security options. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. Set to false to prevent privilege escalation (e.g., from setuid binaries). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

AppArmor profile configuration for the container. Defines the AppArmor profile to apply, with a type (e.g., Localhost, RuntimeDefault, Unconfined) and an optional localhostProfile name when type is Localhost. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
When `type` is `Localhost`, this field specifies the name of the AppArmor profile loaded from the node's local filesystem. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Type of AppArmor profile to use. Valid values are 'Localhost', 'RuntimeDefault', and 'Unconfined'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The capabilities field configures Linux capabilities for the container, allowing specific capabilities to be added (add) or dropped (drop) from the container's effective set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of Linux capabilities to add to the container's permitted capabilities. Each entry is a capability name such as 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The set of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default capabilities. Can include 'ALL' to drop all capabilities. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Run the container in privileged mode. This grants the container all capabilities and access to host devices, essentially providing root-level access to the host. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the proc mount type for the container. Valid values are "Default" (default behavior) and "Unmasked" (allows access to all host processes). Optional. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only. This prevents the container from writing to its root filesystem. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process. If unspecified, the default group ID of the container image is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will refuse to start the container if it would run as UID 0, enforcing a non-root execution. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The UID (user ID) that the container process runs under. If not specified, the container runs as the user defined in the image or by the runtime's default. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

SeLinuxOptions specifies the SELinux context of the container. It is an object that can contain the labels 'level', 'role', 'type', and 'user' to define the SELinux configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux level (MLS/MCS), typically a string such as 's0' or 's0:c123.c456'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux role for the container's security context, such as 'system_r' or 'user_r'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux type label for the container, used to define the type domain for processes and files. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux user label for the container, part of the SELinux options in the security context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures the seccomp profile for the container. The profile type can be one of RuntimeDefault, Localhost, or Unconfined, with an optional localhost profile path for the Localhost type. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to a seccomp profile on the node's local filesystem. This field is only used when the seccomp type is 'Localhost'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The seccomp profile type determines which seccomp profile is used for the container, controlling system-call filtering. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Windows-specific security options for the container, such as GMSA credential spec and run-as username. Only applicable when running on Windows nodes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The full contents of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container, provided as a JSON string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container's Windows security context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Whether the container should be run as a HostProcess container. HostProcess containers allow access to the Windows host, and default to false if not set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The UserName in Windows to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to the user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a probe that checks whether the application in the container is started. If configured, other probes (liveness and readiness) are not activated until the startup probe succeeds. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec specifies the command to run inside the container to perform the startup probe. The probe is successful if the command exits with a status code of 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to execute inside the container as part of the exec startup probe. A list of strings where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Minimum consecutive failures for the startup probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures a gRPC action for the startup probe, which requires a port number and may include a service name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number of the gRPC service to connect to for the probe. Must be between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the gRPC health check is performed against the entire server. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

http_get defines an HTTP GET request used by the startup probe to check container health. It includes configuration for host, port, path, scheme, and HTTP headers to perform the request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. If not specified, the pod IP address is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the startup probe. Each header object contains a `name` and `value` field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to send as part of the HTTP GET request performed by the startup probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
HTTP request path to access on the container. Defaults to '/' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port number to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. This can be an integer port number or a named port (string) defined in the container's ports. Port numbers must be in the range 1 to 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the network protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds between each probe execution. Minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Minimum consecutive successes for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures the startup probe to check a TCP socket. The probe succeeds if a TCP connection to the specified port can be established. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number or name of the TCP socket to probe on the container. Can be an integer port number or a named port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The duration in seconds the container is given to terminate gracefully after this probe fails, overriding the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds. Must be a non-negative integer; the value zero means delete immediately, and if not set, the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Whether to enable stdin for the container, allowing the container to receive input from the standard input stream. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

When true, the container's stdin is closed after the first attach session, rather than remaining open for subsequent attaches. This field only has effect when stdin is also true. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Sets how the kubelet handles the container's termination message. Valid values are 'File' (default, reads from the file specified by terminationMessagePath) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' (uses the last chunk of container logs if the message file is empty). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY for the container. When set to true, the container gets an interactive terminal. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of block devices that the container can access, each defining a device name and the device path inside the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The path inside the container where the block device will be exposed. This is the device path (e.g., /dev/sdb) where the volume device is made available to the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of a volume defined in the pod spec. The volume device references this volume to attach as a block device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines volumes to mount into the container's filesystem, including the volume name, mount path, and additional options such as read-only or subPath. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path within the container at which the volume will be mounted. Must be an absolute path and must not contain ':'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Controls how mounts propagate from the host to the container and vice versa. Valid values are 'None' (no propagation), 'HostToContainer' (mounts from the host are visible in the container), and 'Bidirectional' (mounts propagate both ways). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mounts the volume as read-only if set to true. If false or omitted, the volume is mounted with read-write access. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Controls whether the volume mount is recursively read-only. Valid values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', or 'IfPossible'. 'Enabled' makes the mount and all its subdirectories read-only; 'Disabled' disables recursive read-only; 'IfPossible' enables it only if the underlying volume supports it. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a sub-path within the referenced volume to mount instead of the volume's root. This allows mounting a specific directory from a volume into the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

subPathExpr specifies a sub-path of the volume to mount, using environment variable references like $(VAR_NAME). It allows the sub-path to be computed dynamically based on the pod's environment variables. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default working directory is used (usually the image's WORKDIR or /). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
PodDNSConfig defines the DNS parameters of a pod in addition to those generated from DNSPolicy. Optional.
A list of DNS name server IP addresses. This will be appended to the base nameservers generated from DNSPolicy. Duplicated nameservers will be removed. Optional.

A list of DNS resolver options. This will be merged with the base options generated from DNSPolicy. Duplicated entries will be removed. Resolution options given in Options will override those that appear in the base DNSPolicy. Optional.
The name of the DNS resolver option, such as 'ndots' or 'timeout'. This field is required in each DNS configuration option. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the DNS resolver option named in the associated `name` field. For example, `ndots:5` sets the ndots threshold. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of DNS search domains for host-name lookup. This will be appended to the base search paths generated from DNSPolicy. Duplicated search paths will be removed. Optional.

Set DNS policy for the pod. Defaults to "ClusterFirst". Valid values are 'ClusterFirstWithHostNet', 'ClusterFirst', 'Default' or 'None'. DNS parameters given in DNSConfig will be merged with the policy selected with DNSPolicy. To have DNS options set along with hostNetwork, you have to specify DNS policy explicitly to 'ClusterFirstWithHostNet'. Optional.
EnableServiceLinks indicates whether information about services should be injected into pod's environment variables, matching the syntax of Docker links. Optional: Defaults to true. Optional.

List of ephemeral containers run in this pod. Ephemeral containers may be run in an existing pod to perform user-initiated actions such as debugging. This list cannot be specified when creating a pod, and it cannot be modified by updating the pod spec. In order to add an ephemeral container to an existing pod, use the pod's ephemeralcontainers subresource. Optional.

Arguments to the entrypoint for the ephemeral container. This list is passed to the container's command as arguments, analogous to the args field for regular containers. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run in the ephemeral container, represented as a list of string arguments. This is the container's entrypoint, overriding any default command in the image. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container. Each entry defines a variable name and value or value source. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the environment variable. This sets the literal string value assigned to the environment variable in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

valueFrom is an object that defines a source for the environment variable's value, allowing the value to be dynamically populated from a ConfigMap, Secret, pod field, or resource field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to provide the value for the environment variable. It specifies the ConfigMap name and the key to use. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select the value for this environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ConfigMap from which to select the key for the environment variable value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the referenced key or its containing ConfigMap must be defined. If true, a missing key or ConfigMap does not prevent the container from starting. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects a field of the pod as the value of the environment variable. Supported fields include metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, and status.podIP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The API version of the schema that the field path refers to in the field reference (e.g., v1). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to the field in the Pod spec to select, such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Boolean flag indicating whether the referenced key must be present. If false, the key is required and must exist in the referenced file; if true, the key is optional and its absence will not prevent the container from starting. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a resource field of the container (e.g. limits.cpu or requests.memory) and exposes its value as an environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the container whose resource value is referenced. If omitted, defaults to the container that defines the environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Divisor is the value by which the resource value is divided. Must be a valid Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1Gi', '500m'). Defaults to '1' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource to select from the container's resource requirements, e.g., 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
SecretKeyRef selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. This can be used to expose a secret value as an environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the referenced Secret's data map to select. This specifies which key's value should be used as the value for the environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Secret to retrieve the key from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the referenced secret key must exist. Set to true to allow the container to start even if the secret key or its containing secret is not defined, in which case the environment variable is omitted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, and the keys within the source become environment variable names. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Reference to a ConfigMap from which to pull environment variables. This object specifies the name of the ConfigMap and whether it is optional. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. This is the name of the ConfigMap resource defined in the cluster. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be absent and missing keys are allowed; if false or omitted, the ConfigMap must exist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
