An optional prefix that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. For example, if prefix is 'MY_', each key name becomes MY_<key>. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
SecretRef is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret whose data will be exposed as environment variables in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Secret that supplies the environment variables. This must match an existing Secret in the same namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If true, the container can start even if the Secret does not exist; if false or unset, the Secret is required and the container fails if it is missing. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container image to use for the ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Image pull policy for the ephemeral container. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. If omitted, the policy defaults to Always if the image tag is 'latest' or IfNotPresent otherwise. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

This block configures lifecycle hooks for the ephemeral container, defining actions to take at container startup (postStart) and before shutdown (preStop). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures a handler that runs immediately after the ephemeral container is started. Supports exec, httpGet, or tcpSocket actions within the handler. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The exec action to run when the post-start lifecycle hook is triggered. This block defines a command to execute inside the container, typically specified as a list of command and arguments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run in the container for this exec lifecycle hook. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly, without a shell. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the HTTP GET request that the kubelet sends to trigger the postStart lifecycle hook. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP address. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the postStart lifecycle handler. Each header is defined by a name-value pair. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP path that will be requested by the HTTP GET action. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port to access for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a numeric port or a named port (string) defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URI scheme for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Sleep is an optional configuration that specifies a sleep action for the lifecycle hook. It defines the duration (in seconds) the container should sleep, delaying the post-start hook continuation until the sleep completes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds for the sleep action in the postStart lifecycle hook. The container sleeps for this duration after starting before continuing. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents a TCP socket action that Kubernetes runs as part of the postStart lifecycle hook, which attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Port number for the TCP socket connection. Accepts a numeric port or a named port (as a string). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

PreStop is called immediately before a container is terminated. It allows the container to perform graceful shutdown operations before it is stopped, and the container is terminated once the handler completes or if it fails. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec action to run when the pre-stop hook is triggered. This specifies a command and arguments to be executed inside the container before it is terminated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to execute in the container for the preStop lifecycle hook. It is provided as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This action is executed before the container is terminated and accepts parameters such as host, port, path, scheme, and HTTP headers. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to use for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, the pod IP is used. To set the HTTP Host header, use httpHeaders instead. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request. Each header is an object containing name and value fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the HTTP GET request for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to access on the HTTP server, defaulting to '/' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port on the container to send the HTTP GET request to. Can be a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or a named port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Sleep specifies the Sleep action to be performed before the container is terminated. It accepts a `seconds` field indicating the duration of the sleep. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the number of seconds the container sleeps during the preStop lifecycle hook. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

TCP socket handler for the pre-stop lifecycle hook of an ephemeral container. It specifies a port (and optionally a host) to check for connectivity before the container is terminated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Optional host name or IP address to connect to; defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port number to connect to. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The liveness probe configuration for the ephemeral container. This object defines how to check whether the container is alive, such as by executing a command, making an HTTP request, or opening a TCP socket, along with timing parameters like initial delay and period. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The exec action for the liveness probe, which runs a command inside the container to check its health. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run inside the container for the exec liveness probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly, not through a shell; a zero exit status indicates success (healthy), non-zero indicates failure. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures a gRPC-based health check for the liveness probe. It contains the port to connect to and optionally the service name to check. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number of the gRPC server to query for the liveness probe. This is required for a gRPC probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is the same as the container name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
HTTP GET probe configuration that performs a GET request against the container's IP address to determine liveness. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP address. For setting the HTTP Host header, prefer using httpHeaders instead. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each item defines a header name and value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP request path used by the liveness probe's HTTP GET action. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME port name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URI scheme used for the HTTP request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For a liveness probe, this value must be 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents a TCP socket probe action for the liveness probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port; success indicates the container is healthy, failure triggers the restart policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to probe. This can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The duration in seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed. A value of 0 means delete immediately; if unspecified, a default (typically 30 seconds) is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Timeout in seconds after which the liveness probe is considered failed if no response is received. Defaults to 1 and must be at least 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of ports to expose from the container. Exposing a port here gives the system additional information about the network connections a container uses, but is primarily informational. It also enables Kubernetes to give that information to networking components such as the load balancer. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number that the container listens on and exposes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host IP address to bind the host port to. When not set, the port is bound to all host interfaces (0.0.0.0). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port on the host node to map to the container port. If omitted, the container port is not exposed on the host. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME and unique within the pod. Optional. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The network protocol for the port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. Defaults to TCP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Exec specifies the exec action for the readiness probe. It contains a command to run inside the container; the probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to execute inside the container as part of the exec readiness probe. It is a list of strings representing the command and its arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell; a zero exit status indicates success, non-zero indicates failure. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of consecutive failures required before the probe is considered failed. Defaults to 3, minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures a gRPC health check for the readiness probe. This object specifies the gRPC action used to probe the container, including the port to connect to and optionally the name of the health check service. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number of the gRPC service to connect to for this readiness probe. Required, must be an integer between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC implementation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines the HTTP GET request to perform for the readiness probe, specifying the endpoint to query for container health. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Optional. The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; overrides the Host header and connection target. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request. Each item contains a header name and value, allowing repeated headers as supported by HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header field in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port number or name of the port to access on the container during the readiness probe. This may be an integer port number or a named port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URI scheme for the HTTP request. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the readiness probe is initiated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
How often, in seconds, the readiness probe is executed. Must be at least 1 second. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Minimum consecutive successes for the readiness probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a TCP probe that checks the container's health by attempting to open a connection to a given port. The tcp_socket object configures the port to check and optionally the host to connect to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to connect to for the readiness probe. Accepts a numeric port number or a named port referenced from the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before being forcibly killed. Applies to the pod's shutdown procedure. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines resource resize policies for the ephemeral container. Each policy specifies a resource name and the restart behavior when that resource is resized. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') for which this resize policy is configured. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the restart policy for the ephemeral container when a resize operation is applied. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' (apply resize without restart) and 'RestartContainer' (restart the container to apply the resize). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the compute resources (CPU, memory) required for the ephemeral container. Includes requests and limits for resource usage. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of resource claim references that specify additional resource requests for the ephemeral container. Each claim refers to a ResourceClaim by name, enabling the use of resources defined in ResourceClass or ResourceClaim objects. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Name of the resource claim, matching a logical name defined in the pod's spec.resourceClaims. This makes the referenced resource available to the ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ResourceClaim object in the same namespace as the pod that this container's resource claim references. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of resource names to quantities defining the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the ephemeral container. For example: cpu: '500m', memory: '128Mi'. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A map of resource names to quantities, specifying the minimum amount of compute resources required for the ephemeral container (e.g., cpu, memory). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the restart policy for the ephemeral container, controlling whether the container is restarted on exit. Allowed values are 'Always', 'OnFailure', and 'Never'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of container exit codes that this rule applies to. If the container exits with any of these codes, the restart policy action is triggered. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
SecurityContext holds security configuration that will be applied to an ephemeral container, such as user IDs, capabilities, and SELinux options. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Controls whether the ephemeral container's processes can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, setuid or setgid binaries are prevented from changing the effective user/group ID, effectively disabling privilege escalation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

app_armor_profile defines the AppArmor profile to apply to the ephemeral container. It contains a required type field (one of Localhost, RuntimeDefault, or Unconfined) and an optional localhostProfile field for the profile name when type is Localhost. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of a preconfigured AppArmor profile on the node to use. This profile must already be loaded on the node for the container to run. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The type of AppArmor profile to use. Valid values are 'Localhost', 'RuntimeDefault', and 'Unconfined'. When set to 'Localhost', the 'localhost_profile' field must also be specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The capabilities field configures Linux capabilities for the ephemeral container, allowing extra capabilities to be added or default ones to be dropped. It contains 'add' and 'drop' lists of capability names. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of Linux capabilities to add to the ephemeral container's default capability set (e.g., NET_ADMIN, SYS_TIME). Capabilities are specified without the CAP_ prefix. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's effective and permitted capability sets. For example, 'ALL' drops all capabilities, or specific ones like 'NET_RAW'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Run the container in privileged mode, giving its processes essentially the same access as root on the host. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the proc mount mode for the ephemeral container, controlling how the /proc filesystem is exposed within the security context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only, preventing any writes to it. This is a common security hardening measure to limit the impact of a compromised container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process. Must be a numeric positive integer. If unset, the default is the image's primary group. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. When set to true, the kubelet will validate that the container's user and image do not run as UID 0, and will fail to start the container otherwise. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The user ID (UID) to run the container process as. Overrides the user specified in the container image. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux level label (e.g., 's0' or 's0:c123') for the container. If unspecified, the pod-level SELinux level is inherited. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The SELinux role label for the container process (e.g., system_u). In Kubernetes, this is part of the se_linux_options configuration that specifies the role portion of the SELinux context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux type label that applies to the container process. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The SELinux user label for the container's security context, such as 'system_u' or 'unconfined_u'. This field is part of the SELinux options and typically follows the SELinux user naming convention. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines the seccomp profile for the ephemeral container. It allows specifying the profile type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, Localhost) and optionally the path to a localhost profile. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path to the localhost seccomp profile file on the node. This must be set when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The type of seccomp profile to be applied to the container's security context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Windows-specific security options for the ephemeral container, such as Group Managed Service Account (GMSA) credentials and HostProcess settings. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The GMSA credential spec content to use for the Windows container. This can be provided directly as a JSON string, or it is populated by the GMSA admission webhook when GMSACredentialSpecName is set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec to use for the ephemeral container. This is part of the Windows security context options and enables the container to use a specific GMSA configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Whether the container should be run as a HostProcess container. Only applicable to Windows containers. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The username to run the container's entrypoint process as. For Windows containers only; defaults to the image's user if unspecified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures a startup probe for the ephemeral container, which indicates when the container has started successfully. This probe can be used to gate the start of other probes, ensuring they only run after the application is ready. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Exec defines a command to be executed inside the container for the startup probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with a status code of 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run inside the container for the exec startup probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell; exit status 0 indicates success and non-zero indicates failure. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe after which the container is considered failed and restarted. The default is 3, and the minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures a gRPC-based probe for the container. The probe checks the gRPC service by connecting to a specified port, and optionally uses a service name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Port number of the gRPC service that the probe will connect to. This field is required and must be an integer between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is an empty string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Performs an HTTP GET request against the container. Configures the HTTP probe action, including path, port, and optional headers for the startup probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not set, the pod IP is used. This overrides the default host. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request sent by the probe. Each object defines a header name and value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid HTTP header name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the startup probe's HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server, e.g., /healthz. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number or name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Accepts either a numeric port or a named port on the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Protocol to use for the HTTP GET probe request, such as HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol scheme (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request to the probe endpoint. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0 seconds. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
How often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. Defaults to 10; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Must be 1 for startup probes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies a TCP socket probe, used to check container health by attempting to open a TCP connection to a specific port on the container's IP address. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP address is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to check on the container. Accepts a numeric port or a named port (string). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The duration in seconds the pod is given to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed. Defaults to 30 seconds. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Set to true to enable standard input (stdin) for this ephemeral container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
When true, stdin is only attached once, and after the process reads from it, the channel is closed, preventing further input. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the target container to share the process namespace with. If not specified, the first container in the pod is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Path where the container's termination message is read from, typically used to capture the reason for container termination. Default is /dev/termination-log. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines how the termination message of the ephemeral container is read. Supported values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether a TTY (teletypewriter) should be allocated for the ephemeral container, allowing interactive use. If true, a TTY is allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of block devices to be used by the ephemeral container. Each item maps a named volume to a device path inside the container (e.g., for raw block volume mounts). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path inside the container where the volume device should be exposed (e.g., /dev/sdb). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the volume that this volume device refers to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Volume mounts for the ephemeral container, specifying which volumes to mount and where. Each mount includes a volume name, a mount path inside the container, and options such as read-only. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must not contain ':' and must be an absolute path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Controls mount propagation for the volume mount. Valid values are None (no propagation), HostToContainer (host mounts are propagated to the container), and Bidirectional (mounts are propagated both ways, requiring privileged). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the volume mount is read-only. If true, the mount will be read-only; if false or omitted, it will be read-write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the volume mount is recursive read-only. This field is supported for certain volume types, such as NFS. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
subPath specifies a sub-path inside the referenced volume instead of its root, allowing only a portion of the volume to be mounted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

subPathExpr is an alternative to subPath that allows specifying a path relative to the volume's root using environment variable references. It supports the $(VAR_NAME) syntax for expansion, enabling dynamic subpaths based on container environment variables. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Sets the working directory for the ephemeral container. Commands run from this directory if specified; otherwise, the container runtime default is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

evictionResponders reference responders that react to Evictions based on EvictionRequests. Responders should observe and communicate through the Eviction Resource API to help with the graceful termination of a pod. The responders are selected sequentially, according to their specified priority. Responders should periodically report on an eviction progress by updating the .status.responders[].heartbeatTime field of the Eviction object. If this field is not updated within the heartbeat deadline defined by the Eviction API (currently 20 minutes), the eviction is passed over to the next responder with a lower priority. If there is no other responder, the last default imperative-eviction.k8s.io/evictor responder with a priority of 100 will evict the pod using the imperative Eviction API (pods/<name>/eviction subresource). The maximum length of the responders list is 10. Responders are not supported when the pod is part of a PodGroup (.spec.schedulingGroup is set). This field can only be set on creation and is immutable afterwards. Optional.
HostAliases is an optional list of hosts and IPs that will be injected into the pod's hosts file if specified. Optional.
List of hostnames for this host alias entry. These hostnames will be associated with the specified IP address in the pod's /etc/hosts file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The IP address to associate with the hostnames listed in this host alias entry. This entry is added to the pod's /etc/hosts file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Use the host's ipc namespace. Optional: Default to false. Optional.

Host networking requested for this pod. Use the host's network namespace. When using HostNetwork you should specify ports so the scheduler is aware. When `hostNetwork` is true, specified `hostPort` fields in port definitions must match `containerPort`, and unspecified `hostPort` fields in port definitions are defaulted to match `containerPort`. Default to false. Optional.
Use the host's pid namespace. Optional: Default to false. Optional.

Use the host's user namespace. Optional: Default to true. If set to true or not present, the pod will be run in the host user namespace, useful for when the pod needs a feature only available to the host user namespace, such as loading a kernel module with CAP_SYS_MODULE. When set to false, a new userns is created for the pod. Setting false is useful for mitigating container breakout vulnerabilities even allowing users to run their containers as root without actually having root privileges on the host. Optional.
Specifies the hostname of the Pod If not specified, the pod's hostname will be set to a system-defined value. Optional.

HostnameOverride specifies an explicit override for the pod's hostname as perceived by the pod. This field only specifies the pod's hostname and does not affect its DNS records. When this field is set to a non-empty string: - It takes precedence over the values set in `hostname` and `subdomain`. - The Pod's hostname will be set to this value. - `setHostnameAsFQDN` must be nil or set to false. - `hostNetwork` must be set to false. This field must be a valid DNS subdomain as defined in RFC 1123 and contain at most 64 characters. Optional.

ImagePullSecrets is an optional list of references to secrets in the same namespace to use for pulling any of the images used by this PodSpec. If specified, these secrets will be passed to individual puller implementations for them to use. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images#specifying-imagepullsecrets-on-a-pod Optional.
Name of the Kubernetes secret to use for pulling container images. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of initialization containers belonging to the pod. Init containers are executed in order prior to containers being started. If any init container fails, the pod is considered to have failed and is handled according to its restartPolicy. The name for an init container or normal container must be unique among all containers. Init containers may not have Lifecycle actions, Readiness probes, Liveness probes, or Startup probes. The resourceRequirements of an init container are taken into account during scheduling by finding the highest request/limit for each resource type, and then using the max of that value or the sum of the normal containers. Limits are applied to init containers in a similar fashion. Init containers cannot currently be added or removed. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/init-containers/ Optional.
Arguments to the container's entrypoint command. These override the CMD portion of the image's default configuration, if any. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run in the init container. This corresponds to Docker's ENTRYPOINT and overrides the image's default entrypoint. The list of strings specifies the executable and its arguments, with the first element being the command and the rest as arguments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of environment variables to set in the init container. Each object defines a variable name and either a value or a valueFrom source. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the environment variable to set in the init container. This is the key for the value defined in the same env entry. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Source for the environment variable's value. Can reference a config map key, secret key, or pod/resource field via configMapKeyRef, secretKeyRef, fieldRef, or resourceFieldRef. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects a key from a ConfigMap in the pod's namespace to provide the value for the environment variable. The value is taken from the referenced ConfigMap key. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select the value from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the ConfigMap to select the key from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true, the pod starts even if the referenced ConfigMap or key does not exist, leaving the environment variable unset. If false or omitted, the pod fails if the reference is missing. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, spec.nodeName) to inject as an environment variable value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The API version of the Kubernetes object from which the field is selected. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The path to the field to select from the pod, such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.uid, metadata.labels['<KEY>'], metadata.annotations['<KEY>'], spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, or status.podIPs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key in the referenced file to use as the value for the environment variable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Flag to mark the referenced key as optional. When set to true, the container will start even if the specified key does not exist in the referenced file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the volume that contains the file from which the environment variable value is read. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects a resource field (such as limits.cpu or requests.memory) from the container, and optionally divides its quantity by a divisor, to set the environment variable's value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the container whose resource field is to be selected. If not specified, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The divisor for the resource value, used to scale the value. Must be a quantity string (e.g., '1', '1Ki'); defaults to '1'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the container resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. This is a SecretKeySelector object that specifies the name of the Secret and the key to retrieve. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key within the Secret to select the value from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Secret to select a key from. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the secret key reference is optional. If true, the environment variable is omitted when the secret or key is missing; if false (default), the pod fails to start. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The env_from block describes a source of environment variables, such as a ConfigMap or Secret, whose data is injected into the init container's environment. Each element can specify a config_map_ref or secret_ref. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Reference to a ConfigMap from which to populate environment variables in the container. The ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference. The keys of the ConfigMap will become environment variables in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If true, the ConfigMap may be absent; if false (default), it must exist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

An optional identifier that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when populating environment variables. If specified, it must be a valid C identifier (e.g., starts with a letter or underscore, contains no dashes). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

secretRef is an object that references a Kubernetes Secret to populate environment variables. It contains the name of the Secret and an optional flag indicating whether the Secret must exist. The keys of the Secret become environment variable names in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret to use as the source for environment variables. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If true, the Secret may be absent and any missing keys are ignored. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The container image to run for this init container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the image pull policy for the init container. Valid values are 'Always', 'IfNotPresent', and 'Never'. 'Always' pulls the image every time the container starts, 'IfNotPresent' pulls only if the image is not already present, and 'Never' uses only the local image. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Lifecycle configures hooks that run at specific lifecycle events of the init container, such as postStart and preStop. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The postStart lifecycle hook is triggered immediately after a container is created. It defines a handler (such as exec, HTTP GET, or TCP socket) that runs before the container's primary process starts, commonly used for initialization or setup tasks. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Exec specifies the action to take for the lifecycle hook by running a command inside the container. It is an alternative to the HTTP GET handler. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to be executed inside the container as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. It is provided as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to be sent by the postStart lifecycle handler. The request details include host, port, path, scheme, and HTTP headers, allowing the container to signal readiness or perform initialization via an HTTP endpoint. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; you can override it with a specific hostname. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of HTTP headers to send with the HTTP GET request. Each header is defined by a name and value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server for the GET request. Defaults to '/' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Port number or name for the HTTP GET request. Can be an integer port number or the name of a container port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Typically 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Supported values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with a default of 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Sleep specifies the sleep action for the post-start lifecycle hook. It contains a duration in seconds for the container to sleep. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds to sleep for the postStart lifecycle hook. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configuration for a lifecycle hook handler that performs a TCP socket check by opening a connection to the specified host and port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port for the postStart lifecycle hook's TCP socket check. This can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is executed immediately before a container is terminated. It allows the container to perform graceful shutdown actions, such as draining connections or saving state, via an exec command, HTTP GET request, or TCP socket check. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Exec specifies the action to take in the preStop hook, which runs a command inside the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook. It is an array of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines the HTTP GET request to perform against the container. This is one of the handlers for the pre-stop lifecycle hook, executed before the container is terminated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies a list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header object typically contains a name and a value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to '/'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Port number (1-65535) or name of the container port to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request. Accepts 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS' (case-insensitive), with a default of 'HTTP' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Represents the SleepAction for the pre-stop lifecycle hook, which pauses the container for a specified number of seconds before termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds the container sleeps during the preStop hook, delaying termination. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures a TCP socket check as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This action opens a TCP connection to the specified port (and optionally host) to trigger the stop signal. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Optional host name or IP address to connect to. If not provided, the pod IP is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to connect to. This can be a numeric port or a named port from the container's defined ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines a liveness probe for the container. The kubelet uses this probe to determine when to restart the container based on its health. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines a command-based probe. Executes the specified command inside the container; the probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Command is the command line to run inside the container. The first element is the command, and subsequent elements are arguments. A non-zero exit code indicates probe failure, while exit code 0 indicates success. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The number of consecutive failures that must occur for the liveness probe to be considered failed, after which the container is restarted. Defaults to 3 when not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

grpc specifies the parameters for a gRPC health check performed by the liveness probe. It includes the port number to query and optionally the service name for the gRPC health check. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port on which the gRPC server is listening. This field is required and must be a valid TCP port (1-65535). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default is the container's name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform for the liveness probe. This allows the probe to check the health of the container by making an HTTP request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each object should have a 'name' and a 'value' field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent with the liveness probe's HTTP request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to access on the HTTP server. For example, /healthz. Defaults to / if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number (1-65535) or name of the port on the container to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request, typically either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. When unset, it defaults to 'HTTP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request: either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the TCP socket action for the liveness probe. It checks that a TCP connection can be established to the specified port on the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Host name to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not set, defaults to the pod IP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to connect to for the liveness probe. Can be a numeric port or a named port on the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the number of seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully after a termination signal is sent, before it is forcibly killed. If not set, Kubernetes uses a default of 30 seconds. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 1 if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the init container. This name must be unique within the pod and is used to identify the container in logs, commands, and other references. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of ports to expose from the container. Each port specifies the protocol (e.g., TCP or UDP), the container port number, and optionally the host port, host IP, and a name for the port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP/UDP port number the container listens on and exposes. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The host IP address to bind the host port to. When specified with host_port, the container port is exposed only on that host IP; if omitted, it binds to all host interfaces. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Number of port to expose on the host. If specified, this must be a valid port number, 0 < x < 65536. If HostNetwork is specified, this must match ContainerPort. Most containers do not need this. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the port. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME and unique among all ports in the pod's containers. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The network protocol for this port. Valid values are 'TCP', 'UDP', and 'SCTP'; defaults to 'TCP'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Readiness probe block, which defines a health check that determines when the container is considered ready to accept traffic. If the probe fails, the container is removed from service endpoints. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. The probe is successful if the command exits with a status code of 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The command to run inside the container for the exec probe. This is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and the remaining elements are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3, minimum value is 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
grpc specifies the gRPC action for the readiness probe. It includes the port to probe (required) and an optional service name for the gRPC health check. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number of the gRPC service to probe. Must be between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is empty string, which indicates the health check for the entire service. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

An HTTP GET request configuration used as a readiness probe to check container health. It defines the endpoint to request, including path, port, and optional headers. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header contains a name and a value, allowing you to set headers such as Authorization or Content-Type for the probe request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the GET request. This sets a custom header for the readiness probe's HTTP request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The HTTP path to request when performing the HTTP GET probe. For example, /healthz. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP probe request, either HTTP (default) or HTTPS. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
How often (in seconds) the readiness probe is executed by the kubelet. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10 seconds per Kubernetes specification. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1; must be an integer greater than or equal to 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the TCP socket check to perform for the readiness probe. Defines the port (and optionally host) to test for a listening TCP socket. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The TCP port to check for the readiness probe. This can be a numeric port (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container's ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out and is considered failed. If the probe does not respond within this time, the container is not marked ready. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines the resource resize policy for the init container. Each item specifies the resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the restart policy to apply when the container's resources are resized. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines the restart behavior when a container's requested resource is resized. Valid values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Resource requirements for the init container, specifying the minimum and maximum amounts of compute resources (e.g., CPU, memory) that the container can use. Typically includes 'requests' for the guaranteed amount and 'limits' for the maximum allowed. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Claims is a list of resource claims that the container requires. Each claim refers to a ResourceClaim object by name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ResourceClaim resource that this container requests. The named ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate that is used to create a ResourceClaim for this container. This claim binds the container to the resources allocated from that template. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the init container. The map keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory, ephemeral-storage) and values are quantities such as "1" for CPU or "1Gi" for memory. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. Each map key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the value is the requested quantity as a string (e.g., '250m', '64Mi'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The restart policy for the init container. In Kubernetes, this field is used to configure init containers as sidecar containers, which run for the pod's lifetime. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The comparison operator used to evaluate whether a container's exit code matches the values specified in `exit_codes`. This determines when the associated restart policy rule applies. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of container exit codes to which this restart policy rule applies. When an init container exits with one of these codes, the rule's action is triggered. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

SecurityContext specifies the security settings for the init container, including user/group IDs, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and privilege level. These settings override the pod-level security context for this specific init container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When false, the container runs with the no_new_privs flag, preventing privilege escalation through setuid binaries or other mechanisms. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

AppArmor profile to apply to the container. It is an object containing a `type` field (e.g., RuntimeDefault or Localhost) and an optional `localhostProfile` field that specifies the profile path when `type` is Localhost. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the localhost AppArmor profile to use when the AppArmor profile type is 'Localhost'. This must be set if the type is 'Localhost' and ignored otherwise. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The type of AppArmor profile to apply. Accepts 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', or 'Unconfined'; when 'Localhost' is selected, the localhost_profile field must also be set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures Linux capabilities for the container. The capabilities object can specify a list of capabilities to add (add) and a list to drop (drop). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of Linux capabilities to add to the container's capability set. These augment the default capabilities granted to the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of Linux capabilities to remove from the container's capability set. For example, 'ALL' drops all capabilities, or specify individual ones like 'NET_RAW'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Run the container in privileged mode, giving it access to all host devices and capabilities. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

procMount sets the mount mode for the container's /proc filesystem. Supported values are 'Default' (the default, which masks certain sensitive kernel parameters) and 'Unmasked' (which exposes all of /proc). When not specified, the cluster default is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing write operations to the filesystem. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The GID (group ID) to run the container's main process as. When set, the container process runs with this group ID. If omitted, the group ID is derived from the container image. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. When set to true, the kubelet will refuse to start the container if it runs as UID 0 (root). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the UID (user ID) that the container process will run as. This overrides the user specified in the image metadata if set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
SELinux options for the init container. This object allows setting the SELinux user, role, type, and level labels applied to the container's process. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The SELinux level for the container, e.g., 's0:c1,c2'. This field is part of the SELinux options applied to the container's security context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Role is a SELinux role label that applies to the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
SELinux type label that applies to the container, used as part of the SELinux context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The SELinux user label for the container's security context. This is one of the SELinux options (user, role, type, level) that define the SELinux context applied to the container. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines the seccomp profile for the container, specifying the profile type and optionally a custom localhost profile path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path to the seccomp profile on the node's filesystem. Required when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The type of seccomp profile to use. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, and Localhost. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Windows-specific security options for the container, such as GMSACredentialSpecName, RunAsUserName, and HostProcess. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec for the Windows container. This can be a path to a credential spec file or a JSON string containing the credential spec. Typically populated by the GMSA admission webhook when a credential spec name is provided. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of a GMSA credential spec to use for the pod's init container. This is part of Windows security options and must be paired with a corresponding config map. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

HostProcess specifies whether the container should be run as a HostProcess container on Windows. When true, the container gains extended privileges to access the host's namespace (e.g., Windows services and registry). Defaults to false if not set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The UserName in Windows to run the container process as. If unspecified, the default is the container's user. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a probe that verifies whether the container has started properly. The kubelet will not restart the container until this probe succeeds, making it suitable for containers with slow startup times. This probe runs during the startup phase and stops after success. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Exec specifies the command to execute within the container for the startup probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, with the working directory set to root ('/') in the container's filesystem. The command is exec'd directly, not run inside a shell, so shell constructs like pipes or redirects won't work unless you explicitly invoke a shell. An exit status of 0 is considered successful (healthy/ready), while non-zero is considered a failure. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Number of consecutive failures allowed for the startup probe before it gives up and marks the container as failed. The minimum value is 1; if not set, the default is 3. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The `grpc` field specifies the parameters for a gRPC-based health check performed on the container. It contains the `port` (required) on which the gRPC health check is served, and the optional `service` name to be checked. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The port number on the container that the gRPC health check will connect to. Must be between 1 and 65535. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The service name to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default is the container name of the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the startup probe. Configures the HTTP request details such as path, port, host, scheme, and headers. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The host name or IP address to use when making the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' string fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request. The header name is case-insensitive. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The header value of the HTTP GET request for the startup probe. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. For example, '/healthz'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. The number must be between 1 and 65535; the name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are `HTTP` and `HTTPS`, with `HTTP` being the default if unspecified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The scheme to use when connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. This delays the initial probe to allow the container to initialize before checking its status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the number of seconds between each probe attempt. For startup probes, this controls how often the kubelet performs the startup check. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. For startup probes, this value must be 1. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A TCP socket probe that attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address on a specified port, used to indicate whether the container has started. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for this TCP socket probe. If not set, defaults to the pod IP address. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number or name of the TCP port to connect to for the probe. A numeric value must be in the range 1 to 65535; a name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Must be greater than or equal to 1. Defaults to 1 second if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Whether the container runtime should allocate a buffer for standard input (stdin). Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, the container's stdin is closed immediately after the container starts, rather than remaining open. Only takes effect when `stdin` is also true. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Path at which the file containing the container's termination message is mounted or written. The message is intended to be a brief final status, such as an assertion failure message, and is exposed to the control plane when the container terminates. Defaults to /dev/termination-log if not set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies how the termination message from the container is read. Valid values are 'File' (default) to read from the file specified by termination_message_path, and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' to read from the container's log output if the container exits with error and the message file is empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY for the container. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of volume devices to be exposed to the container. Each entry specifies a volume name and a device path inside the container, enabling raw block device access. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path inside the container where the volume device is mounted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the volume to which this device is attached. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines the volume mounts for the init container. Each mount references a volume defined in the pod spec and specifies the mount path and options like read-only. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path within the container at which the volume is mounted. Must be an absolute path and cannot contain ':'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Controls how mounts are propagated from the host to the container and vice versa. Specifies whether and how volume mounts are shared between the container and other containers or the host. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies that the volume mount is read-only when true, allowing only read access to the mounted volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the read-only setting is applied recursively to all files and directories under the mount path. This differs from standard read_only, which does not propagate to sub-mounts. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path within the volume from which the container's volume should be mounted. Defaults to the volume's root if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Similar to sub_path, but supports environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax to set the mount path dynamically. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Sets the working directory for the container's processes. If not specified, the default working directory from the container image is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

NodeName indicates in which node this pod is scheduled. If empty, this pod is a candidate for scheduling by the scheduler defined in schedulerName. Once this field is set, the kubelet for this node becomes responsible for the lifecycle of this pod. This field should not be used to express a desire for the pod to be scheduled on a specific node. https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#nodename Optional.

NodeSelector is a selector which must be true for the pod to fit on a node. Selector which must match a node's labels for the pod to be scheduled on that node. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/assign-pod-node/ Optional.
PodOS defines the OS parameters of a pod. Optional.

Name is the name of the operating system. The currently supported values are linux and windows. Additional value may be defined in future and can be one of: https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec/blob/master/config.md#platform-specific-configuration Clients should expect to handle additional values and treat unrecognized values in this field as os: null Required.

Overhead represents the resource overhead associated with running a pod for a given RuntimeClass. This field will be autopopulated at admission time by the RuntimeClass admission controller. If the RuntimeClass admission controller is enabled, overhead must not be set in Pod create requests. The RuntimeClass admission controller will reject Pod create requests which have the overhead already set. If RuntimeClass is configured and selected in the PodSpec, Overhead will be set to the value defined in the corresponding RuntimeClass, otherwise it will remain unset and treated as zero. More info: https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-node/688-pod-overhead/README.md Optional.

PreemptionPolicy is the Policy for preempting pods with lower priority. One of Never, PreemptLowerPriority. When Priority Admission Controller is enabled, it prevents users from setting this field. The admission controller populates this field from PriorityClassName. Defaults to PreemptLowerPriority if unset. Optional.

The priority value. Various system components use this field to find the priority of the pod. When Priority Admission Controller is enabled, it prevents users from setting this field. The admission controller populates this field from PriorityClassName. The higher the value, the higher the priority. Optional.

If specified, indicates the pod's priority. "system-node-critical" and "system-cluster-critical" are two special keywords which indicate the highest priorities with the former being the highest priority. Any other name must be defined by creating a PriorityClass object with that name. If not specified, the pod priority will be default or zero if there is no default. Optional.

If specified, all readiness gates will be evaluated for pod readiness. A pod is ready when all its containers are ready AND all conditions specified in the readiness gates have status equal to "True" More info: https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-network/580-pod-readiness-gates Optional.

The condition type that the readiness gate references. The pod will be considered ready only when all readiness gates have their corresponding condition set to True. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

ResourceClaims defines which ResourceClaims must be allocated and reserved before the Pod is allowed to start. The resources will be made available to those containers which consume them by name. This is a stable field but requires that the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate is enabled. This field is immutable. Optional.

The name of the resource claim, which must be unique within the pod's resource claims. This name is used to reference the claim from containers in the pod spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ResourceClaim object to use. The referenced ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate that is used to dynamically create a ResourceClaim for this pod. This is part of the claim source; only one of resourceClaimName or resourceClaimTemplateName should be set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
ResourceRequirements describes the compute resource requirements. Optional.

Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This field depends on the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate. This field is immutable. It can only be set for containers. Optional.

Name of the resource claim, which must match an entry in the pod's spec.resourceClaims to make the claimed resource available to this container in the pod template. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ Optional.

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ Optional.

Restart policy for all containers within the pod. One of Always, OnFailure, Never. In some contexts, only a subset of those values may be permitted. Default to Always. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#restart-policy Optional.

RuntimeClassName refers to a RuntimeClass object in the node.k8s.io group, which should be used to run this pod. If no RuntimeClass resource matches the named class, the pod will not be run. If unset or empty, the "legacy" RuntimeClass will be used, which is an implicit class with an empty definition that uses the default runtime handler. More info: https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-node/585-runtime-class Optional.
If specified, the pod will be dispatched by specified scheduler. If not specified, the pod will be dispatched by default scheduler. Optional.
