SchedulingGates is an opaque list of values that if specified will block scheduling the pod. If schedulingGates is not empty, the pod will stay in the SchedulingGated state and the scheduler will not attempt to schedule the pod. SchedulingGates can only be set at pod creation time, and be removed only afterwards. Optional.

PodSchedulingGroup identifies the runtime scheduling group instance that a Pod belongs to. The scheduler uses this information to apply workload-aware scheduling semantics. Exactly one field must be specified. Optional.
PodGroupName specifies the name of the standalone PodGroup object that represents the runtime instance of this group. Must be a DNS subdomain. Optional.

PodSecurityContext holds pod-level security attributes and common container settings. Some fields are also present in container.securityContext. Field values of container.securityContext take precedence over field values of PodSecurityContext. Optional.
AppArmorProfile defines a pod or container's AppArmor settings. Optional.

localhostProfile indicates a profile loaded on the node that should be used. The profile must be preconfigured on the node to work. Must match the loaded name of the profile. Must be set if and only if type is "Localhost". Optional.

type indicates which kind of AppArmor profile will be applied. Valid options are: Localhost - a profile pre-loaded on the node. RuntimeDefault - the container runtime's default profile. Unconfined - no AppArmor enforcement. Required.

A special supplemental group that applies to all containers in a pod. Some volume types allow the Kubelet to change the ownership of that volume to be owned by the pod: 1. The owning GID will be the FSGroup 2. The setgid bit is set (new files created in the volume will be owned by FSGroup) 3. The permission bits are OR'd with rw-rw---- If unset, the Kubelet will not modify the ownership and permissions of any volume. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

fsGroupChangePolicy defines behavior of changing ownership and permission of the volume before being exposed inside Pod. This field will only apply to volume types which support fsGroup based ownership(and permissions). It will have no effect on ephemeral volume types such as: secret, configmaps and emptydir. Valid values are "OnRootMismatch" and "Always". If not specified, "Always" is used. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process. Uses runtime default if unset. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence for that container. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does. If unset or false, no such validation will be performed. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence. Optional.

The UID to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in SecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence for that container. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

seLinuxChangePolicy defines how the container's SELinux label is applied to all volumes used by the Pod. It has no effect on nodes that do not support SELinux or to volumes does not support SELinux. Valid values are "MountOption" and "Recursive". "Recursive" means relabeling of all files on all Pod volumes by the container runtime. This may be slow for large volumes, but allows mixing privileged and unprivileged Pods sharing the same volume on the same node. "MountOption" mounts all eligible Pod volumes with `-o context` mount option. This requires all Pods that share the same volume to use the same SELinux label. It is not possible to share the same volume among privileged and unprivileged Pods. Eligible volumes are in-tree FibreChannel and iSCSI volumes, and all CSI volumes whose CSI driver announces SELinux support by setting spec.seLinuxMount: true in their CSIDriver instance. Other volumes are always re-labelled recursively. If not specified, "MountOption" is used. This field affects only Pods that have SELinux label set, either in PodSecurityContext or in SecurityContext of all containers. All Pods that use the same volume should use the same seLinuxChangePolicy, otherwise some pods can get stuck in ContainerCreating state. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.
SELinuxOptions are the labels to be applied to the container Optional.
Level is SELinux level label that applies to the container. Optional.
Role is a SELinux role label that applies to the container. Optional.
Type is a SELinux type label that applies to the container. Optional.
User is a SELinux user label that applies to the container. Optional.
SeccompProfile defines a pod/container's seccomp profile settings. Only one profile source may be set. Optional.

localhostProfile indicates a profile defined in a file on the node should be used. The profile must be preconfigured on the node to work. Must be a descending path, relative to the kubelet's configured seccomp profile location. Must be set if type is "Localhost". Must NOT be set for any other type. Optional.

type indicates which kind of seccomp profile will be applied. Valid options are: Localhost - a profile defined in a file on the node should be used. RuntimeDefault - the container runtime default profile should be used. Unconfined - no profile should be applied. Required.

A list of groups applied to the first process run in each container, in addition to the container's primary GID and fsGroup (if specified). If the SupplementalGroupsPolicy feature is enabled, the supplementalGroupsPolicy field determines whether these are in addition to or instead of any group memberships defined in the container image. If unspecified, no additional groups are added, though group memberships defined in the container image may still be used, depending on the supplementalGroupsPolicy field. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

Defines how supplemental groups of the first container processes are calculated. Valid values are "Merge" and "Strict". If not specified, "Merge" is used. (Alpha) Using the field requires the SupplementalGroupsPolicy feature gate to be enabled and the container runtime must implement support for this feature. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.

Sysctls hold a list of namespaced sysctls used for the pod. Pods with unsupported sysctls (by the container runtime) might fail to launch. Note that this field cannot be set when spec.os.name is windows. Optional.
Name of the sysctl parameter to set in the pod's security context. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value to set for the sysctl parameter. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
WindowsSecurityContextOptions contain Windows-specific options and credentials. Optional.

GMSACredentialSpec is where the GMSA admission webhook (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-gmsa) inlines the contents of the GMSA credential spec named by the GMSACredentialSpecName field. Optional.
GMSACredentialSpecName is the name of the GMSA credential spec to use. Optional.

HostProcess determines if a container should be run as a 'Host Process' container. All of a Pod's containers must have the same effective HostProcess value (it is not allowed to have a mix of HostProcess containers and non-HostProcess containers). In addition, if HostProcess is true then HostNetwork must also be set to true. Optional.

The UserName in Windows to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to the user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence. Optional.
DeprecatedServiceAccount is a deprecated alias for ServiceAccountName. Deprecated: Use serviceAccountName instead. Optional.
ServiceAccountName is the name of the ServiceAccount to use to run this pod. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/ Optional.

If true the pod's hostname will be configured as the pod's FQDN, rather than the leaf name (the default). In Linux containers, this means setting the FQDN in the hostname field of the kernel (the nodename field of struct utsname). In Windows containers, this means setting the registry value of hostname for the registry key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\Tcpip\\Parameters to FQDN. If a pod does not have FQDN, this has no effect. Default to false. Optional.

Share a single process namespace between all of the containers in a pod. When this is set containers will be able to view and signal processes from other containers in the same pod, and the first process in each container will not be assigned PID 1. HostPID and ShareProcessNamespace cannot both be set. Optional: Default to false. Optional.
If specified, the fully qualified Pod hostname will be "<hostname>.<subdomain>.<pod namespace>.svc.<cluster domain>". If not specified, the pod will not have a domainname at all. Optional.

Optional duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully. May be decreased in delete request. Value must be non-negative integer. The value zero indicates stop immediately via the kill signal (no opportunity to shut down). If this value is nil, the default grace period will be used instead. The grace period is the duration in seconds after the processes running in the pod are sent a termination signal and the time when the processes are forcibly halted with a kill signal. Set this value longer than the expected cleanup time for your process. Defaults to 30 seconds. Optional.
If specified, the pod's tolerations. Optional.
Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. When omitted with the Exists operator, the toleration matches all taints. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator used to match the taint key. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. If 'Equal', the value must also match. Defaults to 'Equal' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The number of seconds a pod will tolerate a taint before being evicted, when the effect is NoExecute. If unset, the pod tolerates the taint indefinitely; zero or negative values evict immediately. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The value to match the toleration key. Used only when the operator is 'Equal'; ignored when operator is 'Exists'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

TopologySpreadConstraints describes how a group of pods ought to spread across topology domains. Scheduler will schedule pods in a way which abides by the constraints. All topologySpreadConstraints are ANDed. Optional.

A label selector used to identify the set of pods that this topology spread constraint applies to. The constraint is evaluated only against pods whose labels match this selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

match_expressions is a list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, or DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values, used to select pods based on their labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector operates on. Must be a valid Kubernetes label key, such as 'app' or 'tier'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the values in the match expression. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values for the label match expression. For the In and NotIn operators, this specifies the set of values the label key must or must not have. For Exists and DoesNotExist, the list must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of key-value pairs that must be matched by the pod's labels for this topology spread constraint label selector to apply. All specified labels must be present on the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of pod label keys to select the pods for spreading calculation. Values from the incoming pod's labels with these keys are ANDed with the labelSelector to determine the group of existing pods over which spreading is calculated for the incoming pod. Keys not present in the incoming pod labels are ignored. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The maximum degree of skew allowed when distributing pods across topology domains. This value must be greater than 0. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The minimum number of eligible domains (e.g., zones) required for the topology spread constraint to consider global minimum. If the number of eligible domains is less than this value, the skew calculation uses a global minimum of 0; otherwise it has no effect. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates how to treat a pod's node affinity when computing spread. Allowed values are 'Honor' (default), which considers node affinity, or 'Ignore', which ignores node affinity. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates how to treat tainted nodes when calculating pod topology spread skew. Valid values are 'Ignore' (default) and 'Honor'. With 'Honor', nodes whose taints are not tolerated by the pod are excluded from topology spread calculations. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The key of node labels. Nodes that have the same value for this label are considered to be in the same topology domain, and the scheduler spreads pods across these domains to achieve balanced distribution. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates how to deal with a pod if it doesn't satisfy the spread constraint. Allowed values are 'DoNotSchedule' (default) which prevents scheduling, and 'ScheduleAnyway' which allows scheduling and gives higher priority to nodes that minimize skew. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of volumes that can be mounted by containers belonging to the pod. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes Optional.

Represents an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume that can be mounted into the container. This configuration includes settings such as volume ID, filesystem type, partition, and read-only flag. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to mount for the AWS EBS volume (e.g., 'ext4'). Defaults to 'ext4' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Partition on the AWS EBS volume to mount. If omitted, the first partition is mounted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mounts the AWS EBS volume as read-only. If not set, defaults to false (read-write). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The unique ID of the AWS EBS volume to be mounted. This field is required. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures an Azure Disk volume source, allowing the pod to mount an Azure data disk. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The Azure Data Disk caching mode. Allowed values: None, ReadOnly, ReadWrite. Defaults to None if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Azure data disk to be mounted. This field is required when using the Azure Disk volume type. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URI of the Azure disk to mount. For unmanaged disks, this is the URI of the VHD blob; for managed disks, this is the resource ID. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to mount on the Azure disk. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host OS, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Defaults to 'ext4' if unspecified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the kind of Azure disk. Allowed values are 'Shared' (multiple blobs per disk), 'Dedicated' (single blob per disk), and 'Managed' (Azure managed disk). Defaults to 'Shared'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the Azure Disk volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the Azure File volume is mounted as read-only. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the Azure Storage account name and key used to access the Azure file share. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Azure File share to be mounted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
CephFS volume source configuration. This defines a Ceph Filesystem mount that can be used by the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of Ceph monitor endpoints (host:port) for the Ceph filesystem. Required when using CephFS volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path within CephFS to mount as the volume's root. Defaults to '/' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the CephFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Path to the Ceph secret file (e.g., /etc/ceph/user.secret) containing the keyring for the Ceph user. This file is used for authentication when accessing the CephFS volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Reference to a Kubernetes secret that provides the Ceph client keyring for CephFS authentication. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret used for CephFS authentication. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The CephFS user to authenticate as when mounting the volume. Defaults to 'admin' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents a Cinder volume source in Kubernetes, used to mount an OpenStack block storage volume into the pod. This configuration is part of the pod template's volume definitions. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g. "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". If unspecified, it is inferred to be "ext4". Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies whether the Cinder volume is mounted as read-only. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The secret_ref references a Kubernetes Secret that contains the authentication credentials (e.g., for OpenStack) required to access the Cinder volume. The referenced secret must be in the same namespace as the pod, and its name is provided in the object's 'name' field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Kubernetes secret that holds the authentication credentials for the Cinder volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The unique identifier of the Cinder volume in OpenStack that will be mounted into the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Represents a volume that is populated from a Kubernetes ConfigMap, making its data available as files in the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Permissions mode (as octal integer) applied to files in the mounted ConfigMap volume. If not specified, defaults to 0644. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of mappings from keys in the referenced ConfigMap to file paths within the volume. When specified, only the listed keys are projected as files at the given paths; when omitted, all keys are projected as files named after the keys. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key in the ConfigMap to project into the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mode is the optional Unix file permission bits (octal, e.g. 0400) for the config map item. Defaults to 0644 if omitted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The relative file path within the volume where the value of the corresponding ConfigMap key is mounted. The path must not contain '..' segments and must not start with '/'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference in this volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the volume will be empty if the ConfigMap or keys are not found. If false (default), the pod will fail if the ConfigMap or keys are missing. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

csi (object) configures a Container Storage Interface (CSI) volume source for this volume, allowing you to mount storage provided by a CSI driver. It includes fields such as driver, fsType, readOnly, nodePublishSecretRef, and volumeAttributes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the CSI driver that will handle the volume. This field is required and must match the name of a CSI driver installed on the cluster. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Examples include 'ext4', 'xfs', and 'ntfs'. If not specified, the default filesystem type of the volume is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A reference to a Secret object containing credentials for the CSI driver to use when publishing the volume on the node. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the secret in the pod's namespace that provides credentials for the CSI node publish operation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted read-only; otherwise it is mounted read-write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Represents additional attributes as key-value pairs to pass to the CSI driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures a downwardAPI volume, which exposes pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and other fields) to the container via files. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the default file permissions (mode bits) for files created in the downward API volume. This is an optional numeric value (octal, e.g., 0644) that defaults to 0644 if not set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Items is the list of downward API volume files. Each item defines a path and the field to project into that path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects a field from the pod's metadata or status to expose via the downward API. This object typically contains apiVersion and fieldPath to identify the specific pod field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The version of the schema that the field path refers to, defaults to 'v1' when not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Path to the pod field whose value should be exposed, such as metadata.name, metadata.labels, metadata.annotations, or spec.serviceAccountName. This selects the specific field from the pod's metadata or spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mode is the file permission bits (in octal) for the file, e.g., 0644. If not specified, the default is 0644. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path within the volume at which the downward API value is exposed as a file. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects a container resource field (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory, limits.ephemeral-storage) to expose as a file via the downward API. The object includes an optional containerName and a required resource string; only resource limits and requests are supported. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Name of the container for which the resource field is exposed via the downward API. Required when the field references a container resource (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory), and must match a container name in the pod spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The divisor for the resource value exposed via the downward API. This is a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1', '1Ki') that the resource value is divided by before being presented. Defaults to '1' if unspecified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The resource field name to select from the container's requests or limits, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures an emptyDir volume, a temporary directory that is created when the Pod is scheduled and exists as long as the Pod runs. This object can specify settings such as the medium (e.g., 'Memory' for tmpfs) and size limits. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The medium specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume. If unset, the volume uses the node's default filesystem (disk). Set to 'Memory' to back the volume with RAM instead of disk storage. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The size limit for the emptyDir volume, specified as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1Gi', '512M'). When set, the total storage used by the emptyDir volume is restricted to this amount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures an ephemeral volume source, which is handled by a generic storage driver and features a dynamic provisioner. This field is mutually exclusive with other volume source options. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The volume claim template that will be used to create a PersistentVolumeClaim for this ephemeral volume. The template's spec, such as storage class and size, determines the volume characteristics. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Standard Kubernetes object metadata (e.g., labels, annotations, name) for the dynamically created PersistentVolumeClaim from this ephemeral volume's claim template. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of string keys and values that stores arbitrary non-identifying metadata attached to the volume claim template. These annotations are applied to the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this template. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The creation timestamp of the object, in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Number of seconds allowed for this object to gracefully terminate before it is removed from the system. Only set when deletionTimestamp is also set, and may only be shortened. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The timestamp when the object is being deleted, in RFC3339 format. This is set by Kubernetes when a deletion is requested and is used for garbage collection. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of finalizer names. When non-empty, the object will not be deleted until all finalizers are removed. Kubernetes will only remove the object from etcd after all finalizers are cleared. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies a prefix to generate a unique name for the volume claim template when a name is not provided. The server will generate a unique name by appending a random suffix to this prefix. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The generation of the VolumeClaimTemplate metadata. This is a system-generated numeric value representing the object's generation, used for internal reconciliation and optimistic concurrency. It is read-only and cannot be set by the user. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Map of string keys and values that will be attached to the metadata of the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this volume claim template. These labels can be used for selection and organization of the generated resources. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of managed fields, as defined by Kubernetes. Each entry tracks a controller's management of the object's fields, including the manager name, operation, api version, and fields involved. This is used for field ownership and conflict detection. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The API version of the resource that this managed field entry applies to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The type of the managed fields entry, indicating the format of the FieldsV1 field. For example, "FieldsV1". Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
fields_v1 holds the JSON-serialized set of fields managed by this manager, represented as a FieldsV1 structure encoding field paths and values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the manager (e.g., a controller or client) that last modified the fields. It identifies the workflow managing these fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operation performed on the managed field, such as 'Apply' or 'Update'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The subresource of the object that the managed fields entry applies to, such as 'status' for status updates or empty string for the main resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The timestamp indicating when the managed field entry was last updated, in RFC3339 format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The namespace for the volume claim template's metadata. For ephemeral volumes, this is typically empty because the persistent volume claim is created in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of owner references that identify the owning objects of this resource. Each reference contains `api_version`, `kind`, `name`, `uid`, and optional `controller` and `block_owner_deletion` fields, establishing ownership and garbage collection behavior. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The API version of the referent object (e.g., 'v1', 'apps/v1'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

If true, the owner of this ownerReference cannot be deleted until this dependent object is removed. This flag is used by the Kubernetes garbage collector to honor the ownerReference as a blocking deletion dependency. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller of the owning object. When true, this owner reference points to the primary controller responsible for the object's lifecycle. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The kind of the referenced owner object, such as 'Pod' or 'ReplicaSet'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the owner object referenced by this owner reference. In Kubernetes, an OwnerReference contains the name of the owning resource. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The UID of the owner object referenced by this owner reference. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The version of the object used by Kubernetes for optimistic concurrency control. This field is set by the server and changes on every update, enabling clients to detect concurrent modifications. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A system-generated unique identifier for the object, set by the Kubernetes API server. It is read-only and used to distinguish the resource from all others in the cluster. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Spec of the PersistentVolumeClaim template, defining desired characteristics such as access modes, storage class, and resource requirements for the ephemeral volume's underlying PVC. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Defines a Fibre Channel (FC) volume source for a Kubernetes pod, allowing specification of FC-specific parameters such as target worldwide names (WWNs), logical unit number (LUN), filesystem type, and read-only mode. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to mount for the Fibre Channel volume, e.g., ext4 or xfs. Must be supported by the host operating system. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
lun is the logical unit number (LUN) of the Fibre Channel target device. This field is required and must be an integer between 0 and 255. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the Fibre Channel volume is mounted as read-only. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The list of Fibre Channel target WWNs (World Wide Names) for this volume. Each WWN is a unique identifier for a Fibre Channel target port. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of Fibre Channel world wide identifiers (WWIDs) that uniquely identify the target volume. Either this list or a combination of targetWWNs and lun must be provided, but not both. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configures a volume backed by FlexVolume, an out-of-tree volume plugin that uses a driver to mount storage. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Driver is the name of the flex volume driver to use for this volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to be mounted (e.g., ext4, xfs) for this flexVolume volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A map of key-value pairs that are passed to the FlexVolume driver. The driver interprets these options according to its own conventions. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
readOnly is a boolean flag that indicates whether the flexVolume is mounted read-only. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Optional reference to a secret in the pod's namespace that provides credentials or other sensitive data to the flexVolume driver. The secret must exist before the pod starts. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the Secret resource that provides additional configuration for the FlexVolume driver. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Flocker volume source. Configures a Flocker volume to be mounted into the pod, allowing the container to access a Flocker dataset. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the dataset (as stored in Flocker's metadata) to mount. One of dataset_name or dataset_uuid must be specified to identify the Flocker dataset. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to mount. This cannot be set if dataset_name is specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents a Google Compute Engine Persistent Disk (GCE PD) volume source. This configures the PD name, filesystem type, partition, and read-only mode for mounting into the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The filesystem type to mount on the GCE persistent disk. If not specified, the filesystem type of the underlying disk is used. Common values include ext4, xfs, and ext3. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk. If 0, the entire disk is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the GCE Persistent Disk (PD) to attach as a volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies whether the GCE persistent disk volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; when false (default), it is read-write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures a git repository as a volume source. This object specifies the repository URL, the revision to check out, and the target directory within the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Target directory name within the volume where the git repository will be placed. Must not contain or start with '..'. If set to '.', the volume root becomes the git repository; otherwise, the repository is cloned into the specified subdirectory. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The URL of the Git repository to clone into the volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The git revision (commit hash) to check out in the Git repository volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configuration for a GlusterFS volume source, used to mount a GlusterFS volume into the pod. This block defines the details of the GlusterFS mount. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the endpoints object that contains the IP addresses of the GlusterFS nodes. This is required for a GlusterFS volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Path is the Glusterfs volume path, identifying the specific volume to mount from the GlusterFS cluster. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
If true, the GlusterFS volume is mounted as read-only. If false or omitted, the volume is mounted as read-write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures a hostPath volume, which mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod. This allows the pod to access the host's filesystem. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The path on the host node to mount into the pod. Must be an absolute path. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Type of the host path. Must be one of: '', Directory, DirectoryOrCreate, File, FileOrCreate, Socket, CharDevice, BlockDevice. For more details, refer to the Kubernetes documentation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The 'image' block defines an image volume source, which mounts an OCI image as an ephemeral volume. This volume type includes configurations such as the image reference and pull policy. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the image pull policy for the image volume source. Allowed values: Always, Never, IfNotPresent. If unset, defaults to Always. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The image reference for the image volume, e.g., 'nginx:latest'. This is the container image to be mounted as a volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Configuration for an iSCSI volume source, used to mount an iSCSI target as a volume in the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Enables CHAP authentication for the iSCSI discovery session. When set to true, CHAP authentication is required for target discovery. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether CHAP authentication is enabled for the iSCSI session. When true, CHAP authentication is used for the session. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to mount for the iSCSI volume (e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'). If unspecified, it is inferred to be 'ext4'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The custom iSCSI initiator name. If not specified, the system default initiator name is used. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the target. This uniquely identifies the iSCSI target that the volume connects to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the iSCSI interface. Defaults to 'default' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The iSCSI target LUN (Logical Unit Number) to mount. This is a required field for iSCSI volumes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of additional iSCSI portals (IP addresses or hostnames) to connect to if the primary target portal is unreachable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Mounts the iSCSI volume as read-only. Defaults to false, meaning the volume is mounted read-write. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Reference to a Kubernetes Secret that provides CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target. The secret must contain the keys 'node.session.auth.username' and 'node.session.auth.password' (or similar) as required by the iSCSI configuration. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the secret that contains the CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The IP address or hostname of the iSCSI target portal (e.g., 192.168.0.1:3260). This field is required to connect to the iSCSI target. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

NFS (Network File System) volume source configuration. This block defines how an NFS export is mounted into the pod, including the server address, exported path, and read-only access settings. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The NFS export path on the server. It specifies the directory on the NFS server that is mounted into the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Indicates whether the NFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The hostname or IP address of the NFS server. This field is required when configuring an NFS volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Represents a Photon Controller persistent disk volume source, allowing a Photon persistent disk to be mounted into the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

ID that identifies the Photon Controller persistent disk. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Block specifying a Portworx volume to attach to the pod. It defines the volume source configuration for a Portworx persistent volume. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Filesystem type to mount the Portworx volume, e.g. "ext4" or "xfs". Defaults to "ext4" if unspecified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specify whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the volume does not fail when the ConfigMap or its keys are missing. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Optional mode bits for the projected file, as an octal permission value (e.g., 0644) or its decimal equivalent (0-511). Defaults to 0644 if not set. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the ScaleIO storage system. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. For example, ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Whether the StorageOS volume is mounted as read-only. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the StorageOS API credentials. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

If an address is specified manually, is in-range (as per system configuration), and is not in use, it will be allocated to the service; otherwise creation of the service will fail. This field may not be changed through updates unless the type field is also being changed to ExternalName (which requires this field to be empty) or the type field is being changed from ExternalName (in which case this field may optionally be specified, as describe above). Valid values are "None", empty string (""), or a valid IP address. Setting this to "None" makes a "headless service" (no virtual IP), which is useful when direct endpoint connections are preferred and proxying is not required. Only applies to types ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer. If this field is specified when creating a Service of type ExternalName, creation will fail. This field will be wiped when updating a Service to type ExternalName. If this field is not specified, it will be initialized from the clusterIP field. If this field is specified, clients must ensure that clusterIPs[0] and clusterIP have the same value. This field may hold a maximum of two entries (dual-stack IPs, in either order). These IPs must correspond to the values of the ipFamilies field. Both clusterIPs and ipFamilies are governed by the ipFamilyPolicy field. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#virtual-ips-and-service-proxies Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.external_ip.text: externalIPs is a list of IP addresses for which nodes in the cluster will also accept traffic for this service. These IPs are not managed by Kubernetes. The user is responsible for ensuring that traffic arrives at a node with this IP. A common example is external load-balancers that are not part of the Kubernetes system. Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.external_na.text: externalName is the external reference that discovery mechanisms will return as an alias for this service (e.g. a DNS CNAME record). No proxying will be involved. Must be a lowercase RFC-1123 hostname (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1123) and requires `type` to be "ExternalName". Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.external_tr.text: externalTrafficPolicy describes how nodes distribute service traffic they receive on one of the Service's "externally-facing" addresses (NodePorts, ExternalIPs, and LoadBalancer IPs). If set to "Local", the proxy will configure the service in a way that assumes that external load balancers will take care of balancing the service traffic between nodes, and so each node will deliver traffic only to the node-local endpoints of the service, without masquerading the client source IP. (Traffic mistakenly sent to a node with no endpoints will be dropped.) The default value, "Cluster", uses the standard behavior of routing to all endpoints evenly (possibly modified by topology and other features). Note that traffic sent to an External IP or LoadBalancer IP from within the cluster will always get "Cluster" semantics, but clients sending to a NodePort from within the cluster may need to take traffic policy into account when picking a node. Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.health_chec.text: healthCheckNodePort specifies the healthcheck nodePort for the service. This only applies when type is set to LoadBalancer and externalTrafficPolicy is set to Local. If a value is specified, is in-range, and is not in use, it will be used. If not specified, a value will be automatically allocated. External systems (e.g. load-balancers) can use this port to determine if a given node holds endpoints for this service or not. If this field is specified when creating a Service which does not need it, creation will fail. This field will be wiped when updating a Service to no longer need it (e.g. changing type). This field cannot be updated once set. Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.internal_tr.text: InternalTrafficPolicy describes how nodes distribute service traffic they receive on the ClusterIP. If set to "Local", the proxy will assume that pods only want to talk to endpoints of the service on the same node as the pod, dropping the traffic if there are no local endpoints. The default value, "Cluster", uses the standard behavior of routing to all endpoints evenly (possibly modified by topology and other features). Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.ip_families.text: IPFamilies is a list of IP families (e.g. IPv4, IPv6) assigned to this service. This field is usually assigned automatically based on cluster configuration and the ipFamilyPolicy field. If this field is specified manually, the requested family is available in the cluster, and ipFamilyPolicy allows it, it will be used; otherwise creation of the service will fail. This field is conditionally mutable: it allows for adding or removing a secondary IP family, but it does not allow changing the primary IP family of the Service. Valid values are "IPv4" and "IPv6". This field only applies to Services of types ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer, and does apply to "headless" services. This field will be wiped when updating a Service to type ExternalName. This field may hold a maximum of two entries (dual-stack families, in either order). These families must correspond to the values of the clusterIPs field, if specified. Both clusterIPs and ipFamilies are governed by the ipFamilyPolicy field. Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.ip_family_p.text: IPFamilyPolicy represents the dual-stack-ness requested or required by this Service. If there is no value provided, then this field will be set to SingleStack. Services can be "SingleStack" (a single IP family), "PreferDualStack" (two IP families on dual-stack configured clusters or a single IP family on single-stack clusters), or "RequireDualStack" (two IP families on dual-stack configured clusters, otherwise fail). The ipFamilies and clusterIPs fields depend on the value of this field. This field will be wiped when updating a service to type ExternalName. Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.load_balanc.text: loadBalancerClass is the class of the load balancer implementation this Service belongs to. If specified, the value of this field must be a label-style identifier, with an optional prefix, e.g. "internal-vip" or "example.com/internal-vip". Unprefixed names are reserved for end-users. This field can only be set when the Service type is 'LoadBalancer'. If not set, the default load balancer implementation is used, today this is typically done through the cloud provider integration, but should apply for any default implementation. If set, it is assumed that a load balancer implementation is watching for Services with a matching class. Any default load balancer implementation (e.g. cloud providers) should ignore Services that set this field. This field can only be set when creating or updating a Service to type 'LoadBalancer'. Once set, it can not be changed. This field will be wiped when a service is updated to a non 'LoadBalancer' type. Optional.

Only applies to Service Type: LoadBalancer. This feature depends on whether the underlying cloud-provider supports specifying the loadBalancerIP when a load balancer is created. This field will be ignored if the cloud-provider does not support the feature. Deprecated: This field was under-specified and its meaning varies across implementations. Using it is non-portable and it may not support dual-stack. Users are encouraged to use implementation-specific annotations when available. Optional.

This field will be ignored if the cloud-provider does not support the feature." More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-application-cluster/create-external-load-balancer/ Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.ports.text: The list of ports that are exposed by this service. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#virtual-ips-and-service-proxies Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.ports.app_p.text: The application protocol for this port (e.g., 'http', 'https', 'grpc'). Used as a hint for service discovery and may enable protocol-specific handling by service meshes or other systems. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.ports.name.text: The name of the port. This must be a DNS_LABEL and must be unique among all ports in the service. Optional, but required for multi-port services. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.ports.node_.text: The port on each node on which this service is exposed when type is NodePort or LoadBalancer. If not specified, a random port in the configured NodePort range is allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.ports.port.text: The port number on which this service will be exposed. Clients connect to this port to access the service. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.ports.proto.text: The IP protocol for this port. Valid values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP; defaults to TCP. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.ports.targe.text: The port on the pod that the service forwards traffic to. Can be an integer port number or a string referencing a named port on the pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.publish_not.text: publishNotReadyAddresses indicates that any agent which deals with endpoints for this Service should disregard any indications of ready/not-ready. The primary use case for setting this field is for a StatefulSet's Headless Service to propagate SRV DNS records for its Pods for the purpose of peer discovery. The Kubernetes controllers that generate Endpoints and EndpointSlice resources for Services interpret this to mean that all endpoints are considered "ready" even if the Pods themselves are not. Agents which consume only Kubernetes generated endpoints through the Endpoints or EndpointSlice resources can safely assume this behavior. Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.selector.text: Route service traffic to pods with label keys and values matching this selector. If empty or not present, the service is assumed to have an external process managing its endpoints, which Kubernetes will not modify. Only applies to types ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer. Ignored if type is ExternalName. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/ Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.session_aff.text: Supports "ClientIP" and "None". Used to maintain session affinity. Enable client IP based session affinity. Must be ClientIP or None. Defaults to None. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#virtual-ips-and-service-proxies Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.traffic_dis.text: TrafficDistribution offers a way to express preferences for how traffic is distributed to Service endpoints. Implementations can use this field as a hint, but are not required to guarantee strict adherence. If the field is not set, the implementation will apply its default routing strategy. If set to "PreferClose", implementations should prioritize endpoints that are in the same zone. Optional.

kubernetes_core_service.spec.type.text: type determines how the Service is exposed. Defaults to ClusterIP. Valid options are ExternalName, ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer. "ClusterIP" allocates a cluster-internal IP address for load-balancing to endpoints. Endpoints are determined by the selector or if that is not specified, by manual construction of an Endpoints object or EndpointSlice objects. If clusterIP is "None", no virtual IP is allocated and the endpoints are published as a set of endpoints rather than a virtual IP. "NodePort" builds on ClusterIP and allocates a port on every node which routes to the same endpoints as the clusterIP. "LoadBalancer" builds on NodePort and creates an external load-balancer (if supported in the current cloud) which routes to the same endpoints as the clusterIP. "ExternalName" aliases this service to the specified externalName. Several other fields do not apply to ExternalName services. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#publishing-services-service-types Optional.

`lendablePercent` prescribes the fraction of the level's NominalCL that can be borrowed by other priority levels. This value of this field must be between 0 and 100, inclusive, and it defaults to 0. The number of seats that other levels can borrow from this level, known as this level's LendableConcurrencyLimit (LendableCL), is defined as follows. LendableCL(i) = round( NominalCL(i) * lendablePercent(i)/100.0 ) Optional.

`nominalConcurrencyShares` (NCS) contributes to the computation of the NominalConcurrencyLimit (NominalCL) of this level. This is the number of execution seats nominally reserved for this priority level. This DOES NOT limit the dispatching from this priority level but affects the other priority levels through the borrowing mechanism. The server's concurrency limit (ServerCL) is divided among all the priority levels in proportion to their NCS values: NominalCL(i) = ceil( ServerCL * NCS(i) / sum_ncs ) sum_ncs = sum[priority level k] NCS(k) Bigger numbers mean a larger nominal concurrency limit, at the expense of every other priority level. This field has a default value of zero. Optional.

LimitedPriorityLevelConfiguration specifies how to handle requests that are subject to limits. It addresses two issues: - How are requests for this priority level limited? - What should be done with requests that exceed the limit? Optional.

`borrowingLimitPercent`, if present, configures a limit on how many seats this priority level can borrow from other priority levels. The limit is known as this level's BorrowingConcurrencyLimit (BorrowingCL) and is a limit on the total number of seats that this level may borrow at any one time. This field holds the ratio of that limit to the level's nominal concurrency limit. When this field is non-nil, it must hold a non-negative integer and the limit is calculated as follows. intent specifies the action that should be taken for the specified target. - Eviction means that the requester is interested in the eviction of the target. - Withdrawn means that the requester is no longer interested in the eviction of the target. kubernetes_networking_network_policy.spe.text: NetworkPolicySpec provides the specification of a NetworkPolicy Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

egress is a list of egress rules to be applied to the selected pods. Outgoing traffic is allowed if there are no NetworkPolicies selecting the pod (and cluster policy otherwise allows the traffic), OR if the traffic matches at least one egress rule across all of the NetworkPolicy objects whose podSelector matches the pod. If this field is empty then this NetworkPolicy limits all outgoing traffic (and serves solely to ensure that the pods it selects are isolated by default). This field is beta-level in 1.8 Optional.

Specifies the destination ports to which the egress traffic is allowed. Each port entry can include a protocol (TCP, UDP, or SCTP) and a port number or range. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The end of the port range (inclusive). Must be greater than or equal to `port` and is only valid when `port` is specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The port on the destination pod to allow traffic to. Can be a numeric port (1-65535) expressed as a string, or a named port defined in the pod's container ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The IP protocol for this port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. Defaults to TCP if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Optional list of peers (namespace selectors, pod selectors, or IP blocks) that egress traffic is allowed to. If omitted or empty, egress traffic is allowed to all destinations. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Defines the IP block (CIDR range) to which egress traffic is allowed, with optional subnets to exclude via the 'except' field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The IP block in CIDR notation (e.g., '192.168.1.0/24') that defines the destination addresses for this egress rule. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of CIDR ranges to exclude from the specified IP block. Traffic to these IPs will not be allowed even if they fall within the IP block's CIDR. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Selects namespaces from which Pods are allowed as destinations for egress traffic. This is a standard Kubernetes label selector over namespace labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements to match against namespaces. Each requirement includes a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector requirement applies to. This key must exist on the target namespace's labels for the matchExpression to be satisfied. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

values is a list of string values that applies to the matchExpression. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty; if the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A map of label keys to values that must match a namespace's labels for it to be selected by this selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Selects Pods in the same namespace to which egress traffic is allowed. This is a label selector (map of key-value pairs); if empty, it matches all Pods in the namespace. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements that constrain the pod selection. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector applies to. For example, 'app' or 'environment'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The values field contains a list of string values that are matched against the label key based on the operator. For operators 'In' and 'NotIn', this list must be non-empty; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of label keys to values that a pod's labels must match for the pod to be selected by this selector. Corresponds to the matchLabels field in a Kubernetes LabelSelector, used to define which pods the egress rule applies to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

ingress is a list of ingress rules to be applied to the selected pods. Traffic is allowed to a pod if there are no NetworkPolicies selecting the pod (and cluster policy otherwise allows the traffic), OR if the traffic source is the pod's local node, OR if the traffic matches at least one ingress rule across all of the NetworkPolicy objects whose podSelector matches the pod. If this field is empty then this NetworkPolicy does not allow any traffic (and serves solely to ensure that the pods it selects are isolated by default) Optional.

A list of sources (peers) from which traffic is allowed. Each element can specify an ipBlock, namespaceSelector, podSelector, or a combination. If omitted, the ingress rule allows traffic from all sources. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
IP block to select source IPs from. Used in NetworkPolicy ingress rules to allow traffic from a specific CIDR range, with optional exceptions. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The CIDR notation IP range (e.g., '192.168.1.0/24') that defines the IP block for the network policy rule. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specify a list of CIDR ranges to exclude from the allowed IP range defined by the parent `cidr` field. Traffic from these IPs is denied even if it matches the `cidr`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A label selector that selects namespaces to which the ingress rule applies. Traffic is allowed from pods in any namespace that matches the selector, using standard Kubernetes label selector semantics (matchLabels and matchExpressions). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements that filter namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a set of values. Only namespaces matching all expressions are selected. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector applies to. In a matchExpressions requirement, this key, along with operator and values, defines which namespaces match. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values used in a label selector requirement for selecting namespaces. Must be provided when the operator is `In` or `NotIn`, and must be empty for `Exists` or `DoesNotExist`. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels on a namespace for it to be selected by this rule. Only namespaces with all specified labels are allowed as sources of ingress traffic. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A label selector that identifies the source pods allowed to send ingress traffic to the policy's selected pods. It follows standard Kubernetes label selector semantics (matchLabels and matchExpressions) and applies to pods in the same namespace unless a namespaceSelector is also specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The pod selector matches pods that satisfy all listed requirements. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector requirement applies to. This key must exist on a pod's labels for the selector to match that pod. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values that correspond to the key and operator in the match expression. This field is required when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn' and must be non-empty; it must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist' operators. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of label keys and values that selects the source pods. The network policy ingress rule allows traffic only from pods that match all the specified label key-value pairs. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of destination ports and protocols for the ingress rule. Each entry defines a port (numeric or named) and protocol (TCP, UDP, or SCTP), with an optional endPort for a range. If ports are omitted, the rule applies to all ports. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The end of the port range, inclusive. When set, the port field must specify the start of the range, and traffic is allowed to any port in the range. This field is supported only for TCP and UDP protocols. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the port to which traffic is allowed. This can be a numeric port (e.g., '80') or a string name for a named port (e.g., 'https'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The IP protocol for this port. Allowed values are 'TCP', 'UDP', and 'SCTP'. Defaults to 'TCP' if not specified. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A label selector is a label query over a set of resources. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all objects. A null label selector matches no objects. Optional.
matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed. Optional.
The label key that the selector applies to. This is part of the matchExpressions requirement within the pod selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Operator defines the relationship between the key and the set of values. Valid values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of string values that the label key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. For Exists or DoesNotExist operators, values must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed. Optional.

policyTypes is a list of rule types that the NetworkPolicy relates to. Valid options are ["Ingress"], ["Egress"], or ["Ingress", "Egress"]. If this field is not specified, it will default based on the existence of ingress or egress rules; policies that contain an egress section are assumed to affect egress, and all policies (whether or not they contain an ingress section) are assumed to affect ingress. If you want to write an egress-only policy, you must explicitly specify policyTypes [ "Egress" ]. Likewise, if you want to write a policy that specifies that no egress is allowed, you must specify a policyTypes value that include "Egress" (since such a policy would not include an egress section and would otherwise default to just [ "Ingress" ]). This field is beta-level in 1.8 Optional.

unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy defines the criteria for when unhealthy pods should be considered for eviction. Current implementation considers healthy pods, as pods that have status.conditions item with type="Ready",status="True". Valid policies are IfHealthyBudget and AlwaysAllow. If no policy is specified, the default behavior will be used, which corresponds to the IfHealthyBudget policy. IfHealthyBudget policy means that running pods (status.phase="Running"), but not yet healthy can be evicted only if the guarded application is not disrupted (status.currentHealthy is at least equal to status.desiredHealthy). Healthy pods will be subject to the PDB for eviction. AlwaysAllow policy means that all running pods (status.phase="Running"), but not yet healthy are considered disrupted and can be evicted regardless of whether the criteria in a PDB is met. This means perspective running pods of a disrupted application might not get a chance to become healthy. Healthy pods will be subject to the PDB for eviction. Additional policies may be added in the future. Clients making eviction decisions should disallow eviction of unhealthy pods if they encounter an unrecognized policy in this field. Optional.

Therefore no disruptions are allowed and the status of the condition will be False. - InsufficientPods: The number of pods are either at or below the number required by the PodDisruptionBudget. No disruptions are allowed and the status of the condition will be False. - SufficientPods: There are more pods than required by the PodDisruptionBudget. This field holds configuration for multiple potential drivers which could satisfy requests in this claim. It is ignored while allocating the claim. Optional.

Opaque carries driver-specific configuration parameters in a raw object, allowing the device driver to interpret the settings without Kubernetes understanding them. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the name of the driver that interprets the opaque device configuration parameters. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Arbitrary JSON object containing driver-specific parameters. The cluster does not interpret these parameters; they are passed as-is to the device driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
These constraints must be satisfied by the set of devices that get allocated for the claim. Optional.

The name of a device attribute that all devices selected for the request must have different values for, ensuring the devices are distinct with respect to that attribute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the device attribute this constraint applies to. A device is selected only if it has this attribute with a value matching the constraint's 'value' field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of request names that this constraint applies to. If empty, the constraint applies to all requests in the claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Requests represent individual requests for distinct devices which must all be satisfied. If empty, nothing needs to be allocated. Optional.

Indicates that this request requires administrative access to the device(s). Claims with admin access are expected to be used for monitoring or management purposes. Defaults to false. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of resource names (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') to their requested quantities (e.g., '500m', '1Gi') that must be matched exactly by the device's capacity in this request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The exact number of devices to allocate, as required by the device request's 'exactly' specification. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A CEL (Common Expression Language) expression that evaluates to a boolean. It is used to match devices by their derived attributes; the expression is true for devices that satisfy the condition. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the device attribute that must be matched exactly. It identifies a specific derived attribute in the request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the DeviceClass that this request is for. The DeviceClass defines the kinds of devices that can be allocated to satisfy this resource claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Configures a CEL (Common Expression Language) selector for matching devices. The object contains a CEL expression that is evaluated against device attributes to determine if a device satisfies the request. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The CEL (Common Expression Language) expression used to select devices in the resource claim. It defines the matching criteria that devices must satisfy. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of tolerations for the device request. Each toleration allows the request to match devices that have specified conditions, using key, operator, value, and effect fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects. When specified, allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule and NoExecute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. If empty, it matches all keys when the operator is Exists. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator used for matching the toleration key and value. Valid values are 'Exists' (matches on key presence) and 'Equal' (matches on key and value). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The number of seconds the toleration remains effective. If omitted, the toleration applies indefinitely. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The value that the toleration matches against the taint's value. This field is optional and is used when the operator is 'Equal'; it must be empty if the operator is 'Exists'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
An ordered list of DeviceRequest alternatives; the first one that can be satisfied will be allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The allocation mode for the device request. In the Kubernetes DRA API, this can be 'All' (allocate all matching devices) or 'Exact' (allocate the specified number of matching devices). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Number of devices to allocate from the first available devices that match the request's class and selectors. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The Common Expression Language (CEL) expression used to compute the derived attribute value from the device's attributes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the DeviceClass that the requested device must belong to when using the firstAvailable selector. Only devices from the named class are eligible for allocation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of device selectors used to filter devices from the requested device class. Each selector is a CEL expression evaluated against device attributes; multiple selectors are combined with AND logic. If empty, all devices of the class are considered for allocation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

CEL (Common Expression Language) selector for device allocation. The expression is evaluated against device attributes to determine which devices match the request; a device is selected if the expression evaluates to true. This is an alternative to the serial selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The CEL expression used to select devices that satisfy this request. It is evaluated against each device's attributes and must return true for the device to be matched. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of tolerations that apply to this device request in a Kubernetes ResourceClaim. Tolerations allow scheduling onto nodes with matching taints, similar to pod tolerations. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The effect of the taint to match. Valid values are 'NoSchedule', 'PreferNoSchedule', and 'NoExecute'. An empty value matches all taint effects. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. When the operator is 'Exists', the value must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator used to match the taint key. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. Defaults to 'Equal'. When 'Exists' is set, the value must be empty and the toleration matches all taints with the specified key. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The duration in seconds for which the toleration tolerates the taint when the effect is NoExecute. If omitted, the toleration lasts forever. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The value associated with the key of the toleration. This is used with the operator to determine a match, e.g., when operator is Equal, the value must match the taint's value; when operator is Exists, this field is ignored. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Name of the device request. Must be unique within the requests list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
