AllocationResult contains attributes of an allocated resource. Optional.
Time is a wrapper around time.Time which supports correct marshaling to YAML and JSON. Wrappers are provided for many of the factory methods that the time package offers. Optional.
DeviceAllocationResult is the result of allocating devices. Optional.

This field is a combination of all the claim and class configuration parameters. Drivers can distinguish between those based on a flag. This includes configuration parameters for drivers which have no allocated devices in the result because it is up to the drivers which configuration parameters they support. They can silently ignore unknown configuration parameters. Optional.
Opaque provides driver-specific configuration parameters for the device allocation. It is used when the configuration source is 'FromData'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Driver is used to determine which kubelet plugin needs to be passed these configuration parameters. The driver must be a valid subdomain name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Opaque parameters for this device configuration, passed as a raw extension object. The structure is driver-defined and not interpreted by Kubernetes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Source indicates the origin of the device allocation configuration. Valid values are 'claim' (configuration from the ResourceClaim) and 'driver' (configuration from the driver). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Results lists all allocated devices. Optional.
Indicates whether the device was allocated with administrative access. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of conditions that describe why the binding of the resource to the claim failed. In the Kubernetes ResourceClaim status, this field is populated with error reasons when the scheduler cannot allocate the requested devices. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the device that was allocated from the pool for this resource claim, as reported by the resource driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the device driver that provides the allocated device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource pool from which the device was allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the device request that this allocation result corresponds to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
ShareID is a string that uniquely identifies a shared device across multiple resource claims. If the device is not shared, this field is omitted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of node operations that the driver has indicated should be skipped for this allocated device. These operations are normally performed by the kubelet during device preparation, but are skipped for devices that do not require them. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The effect of the taint that this toleration matches, such as NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, or NoExecute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The taint key that this toleration applies to. If empty, the toleration matches all taints (requiring operator 'Exists'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator represents a key's relationship to the value. Valid operators are Exists and Equal. If Exists, the value must be empty; if Equal, the value must match the specified value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The duration in seconds for which the toleration is effective. In Kubernetes, this is used with the NoExecute effect to specify how long a pod can remain on a node after a taint is added. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The value associated with the toleration key. When the operator is 'Equal', this matches the value of the key on the node; it is ignored or empty when the operator is 'Exists' or when the key is empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A node selector represents the union of the results of one or more label queries over a set of nodes; that is, it represents the OR of the selectors represented by the node selector terms. Optional.
Required. A list of node selector terms. The terms are ORed. Required.
A list of node selector requirements by node's labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector expression applies to. It must be a valid Kubernetes label key (e.g., 'disktype' or 'kubernetes.io/os'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
values is the list of strings that correspond to the key. For example, if operator is In or NotIn, the key's value must be in (or not in) this list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

match_fields is a list of node selector requirements that specify the node fields (e.g., metadata.name) that must match for a node to be selected by this node selector term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that this node selector match field targets, such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator to apply to the key and values in this match field requirement. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values that the field must match, as part of a node selector term's match field expression. The operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist) determines how these values are interpreted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Devices contains the status of each device allocated for this claim, as reported by the driver. This can include driver-specific information. Entries are owned by their respective drivers. Optional.

The list of conditions representing the latest observed state of the device. Each condition includes the type, status, reason, and message to indicate the device's health status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This timestamp is typically represented in RFC3339 format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A human-readable message providing details about the current condition of the device in the resource claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

observedGeneration is the .metadata.generation of the ResourceClaim that this condition was observed against, indicating the freshness of the condition relative to the latest generation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Reason is a machine-readable, CamelCase reason for the condition's last transition, providing a stable identifier for the cause of the condition. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The status of the condition, typically 'True', 'False', or 'Unknown'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Arbitrary driver-specific data about the device allocation, as provided by the resource driver. Kubernetes does not interpret this field and it may be used to pass device-specific configuration or status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the device that has been allocated for this resource claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the device driver that manages this allocated device, matching the driver specified in the corresponding DeviceClass. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Network information for the allocated device, including its interface name, IP addresses, and MAC address. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The MAC address of the network interface allocated for this resource claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the network interface on the node where this device is allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of IP addresses assigned to the network device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource pool (ResourceSlice) from which this device was allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

ReservedFor indicates which entities are currently allowed to use the claim. A Pod which references a ResourceClaim which is not reserved for that Pod will not be started. A claim that is in use or might be in use because it has been reserved must not get deallocated. In a cluster with multiple scheduler instances, two pods might get scheduled concurrently by different schedulers. When they reference the same ResourceClaim which already has reached its maximum number of consumers, only one pod can be scheduled. Both schedulers try to add their pod to the claim.status.reservedFor field, but only the update that reaches the API server first gets stored. The other one fails with an error and the scheduler which issued it knows that it must put the pod back into the queue, waiting for the ResourceClaim to become usable again. There can be at most 256 such reservations. This may get increased in the future, but not reduced. Optional.
The API group of the resource that reserved this claim. For core resources, this is the empty string; otherwise it is the fully-qualified API group name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the pod that this resource claim is reserved for. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource (e.g., a Pod) that holds a reservation for this resource claim, as recorded in the status.reservedFor list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The UID of the consumer (e.g., a Pod) that this ResourceClaim is reserved for. This is part of the ResourceClaimConsumerReference in the reservedFor list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The number of devices in the resource pool that are currently unavailable. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

kubernetes_resource_resource_slice.spec.text: ResourceSliceSpec contains the information published by the driver in one ResourceSlice. Required.

kubernetes_resource_resource_slice.spec..text: AllNodes indicates that all nodes have access to the resources in the pool. Exactly one of NodeName, NodeSelector, AllNodes, and PerDeviceNodeSelection must be set. Optional.

Devices lists some or all of the devices in this pool. Must not have more than 128 entries. If any device uses taints or consumes counters the limit is 64. Only one of Devices and SharedCounters can be set in a ResourceSlice. Optional.

When true, the device may be allocated to multiple ResourceClaims simultaneously; when false or omitted, the device is allocated exclusively to a single claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Attributes is a map of device attributes. Each key is the attribute name, and the value is a DeviceAttribute object holding a typed value: one of IntValue (int64), BoolValue (bool), StringValue (string), or VersionValue (string). These attributes describe device properties and are used for device selection in resource claims. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
When set, this device attribute has a boolean value. Only one of bool, int, string, or version may be specified for an attribute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The integer value of this device attribute. This field is set when the attribute is an integer; exactly one of 'int', 'bool', 'string', or 'version' must be present. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The string value of a device attribute. This field is set when the attribute's value is specified as a string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of conditions that indicate why this device cannot be bound to a resource claim. If any condition is met, the device is considered unavailable for allocation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A map of resource names to resource quantities (e.g., memory, cpu) that describes the capacity provided by this device. Each key is a resource name, and the corresponding value is a quantity string like '1Gi' or '500m'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the allowed range of values for a device capacity request. Requests must fall within this range to be considered valid. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The maximum value (inclusive) in the valid range for the device request policy. This sets the upper limit for the number of devices that can be requested, expressed as a string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The minimum value allowed in the valid range, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '1', '500m'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The step size between allowed values in the valid range, specified as a Kubernetes quantity string. Values within the range must be of the form min + N*step, where N is an integer, up to max. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The quantity of the device capacity, expressed as a Kubernetes resource quantity string (e.g., "1Gi", "500m", "2"). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of counters that this device consumes. Each item represents a counter with a name and a value, indicating the amount of that counter required by the device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the counter set from which the device consumes counters. This refers to a named set of counters defined by a DRA resource driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The value of the consumed counter entry, represented as a string (typically a numeric value). Specifies the amount of the counter that this device consumes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the device, unique within the resource slice. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key in the node allocatable resources mapping that identifies a particular resource capacity. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The per-pod overhead resource quantity for this device, expressed as a Kubernetes resource quantity string (e.g., '1', '500m', '1Gi'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the Kubernetes node that this device is associated with. This field may be empty if the device is not node-specific. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The node selector that restricts this ResourceSlice to nodes with matching labels. It uses standard Kubernetes label selector semantics to identify eligible nodes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of node selector terms. The terms are ORed, so a node matches the node selector if any one term matches. Each term contains a list of match expressions and optionally a list of match fields. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of label selector requirements that constrain which nodes are selected. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a list of values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that this match expression applies to. In Kubernetes node selectors, this is the key of the label that is matched against node labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values in a Kubernetes node selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values for the node selector match expression. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist. Each value must be a valid label value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of node selector requirements that match nodes by their fields (e.g., metadata.name). Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and optionally a list of values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key of the node field to match. In a matchFields expression, this is a field path such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.unschedulable'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator defines the relationship between the key and the set of values for the node selector match field. Allowed operators are: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the list of values that the node selector key must match, depending on the operator. For example, with operator 'In', the node must have the key set to one of these values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Taints is a list of taints associated with the device. Each taint restricts which nodes can allocate the device, defined by key, value, and effect. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The effect of the taint, indicating how pods that do not tolerate the taint are handled. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The key of the taint, identifying the specific attribute or condition being tainted on the device. It follows the standard Kubernetes taint key format, which may include a DNS subdomain prefix and a name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The time at which the taint was added, in RFC3339 timestamp format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'). This corresponds to the Kubernetes taint's TimeAdded field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The value associated with the taint key. This is an optional string that provides additional context for the taint, such as a specific condition or constraint. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Driver identifies the DRA driver providing the capacity information. A field selector can be used to list only ResourceSlice objects with a certain driver name. Must be a DNS subdomain and should end with a DNS domain owned by the vendor of the driver. It should use only lower case characters. This field is immutable. Required.

NodeName identifies the node which provides the resources in this pool. A field selector can be used to list only ResourceSlice objects belonging to a certain node. This field can be used to limit access from nodes to ResourceSlices with the same node name. It also indicates to autoscalers that adding new nodes of the same type as some old node might also make new resources available. Exactly one of NodeName, NodeSelector, AllNodes, and PerDeviceNodeSelection must be set. This field is immutable. Optional.
A node selector represents the union of the results of one or more label queries over a set of nodes; that is, it represents the OR of the selectors represented by the node selector terms. Optional.
Required. A list of node selector terms. The terms are ORed. Required.

A list of label selector requirements for the node. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The node must satisfy all match expressions to match the selector term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The label key that this match expression applies to. In a Kubernetes node selector, it identifies the node label that the operator and values are evaluated against. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the operator for the match expression, defining how the key and values are compared. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values that the key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. Must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist operators, matching Kubernetes NodeSelectorRequirement semantics. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name), rather than node labels. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values that a node's field must satisfy to be selected. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The node field key, such as metadata.name or metadata.uid, that the match field requirement applies to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator specifies the relationship between the key and value(s) in the match field. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values for the match field requirement. The operator determines how these values are used: for In and NotIn, the list must be non-empty; for Exists and DoesNotExist, the list must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

PartitionTypeAttribute names a string device attribute (by fully qualified name, e.g. "gpu.example.com/profile") whose value labels each device with its partition type, such as "Full" or "Half" for a MIG-style GPU. When set, every partitionable device in the slice must carry the attribute and devices sharing a value must share the same ConsumesCounters cost. Optional.

PerDeviceNodeSelection defines whether the access from nodes to resources in the pool is set on the ResourceSlice level or on each device. If it is set to true, every device defined the ResourceSlice must specify this individually. Exactly one of NodeName, NodeSelector, AllNodes, and PerDeviceNodeSelection must be set. Optional.
ResourcePool describes the pool that ResourceSlices belong to. Required.

Generation tracks the change in a pool over time. Whenever a driver changes something about one or more of the resources in a pool, it must change the generation in all ResourceSlices which are part of that pool. Consumers of ResourceSlices should only consider resources from the pool with the highest generation number. The generation may be reset by drivers, which should be fine for consumers, assuming that all ResourceSlices in a pool are updated to match or deleted. Combined with ResourceSliceCount, this mechanism enables consumers to detect pools which are comprised of multiple ResourceSlices and are in an incomplete state. Required.

Name is used to identify the pool. For node-local devices, this is often the node name, but this is not required. A field selector can be used to list only ResourceSlice objects belonging to a certain pool. It must not be longer than 253 characters and must consist of one or more DNS sub-domains separated by slashes. This field is immutable. Required.

ResourceSliceCount is the total number of ResourceSlices in the pool at this generation number. Must be greater than zero. Consumers can use this to check whether they have seen all ResourceSlices belonging to the same pool. Required.

SharedCounters defines a list of counter sets, each of which has a name and a list of counters available. The names of the counter sets must be unique in the ResourcePool. Only one of Devices and SharedCounters can be set in a ResourceSlice. The maximum number of counter sets is 8. Optional.

SkipNodeOperations lists node-local resource operations (gRPC calls) that will be skipped for the devices in this slice when determining whether operations are necessary on the node. If all allocated devices for a driver in a claim skip an operation, that gRPC call will be skipped. Valid values are: - "NodePrepareResources": NodePrepareResources gRPC calls are skipped. This value cannot be specified unless "NodeUnprepareResources" is also listed (or "*" is specified). - "NodeUnprepareResources": NodeUnprepareResources gRPC calls are skipped. - "*": All node-local resource operations are skipped. Other values may be added in the future. The kubelet must ignore unknown values. Optional.

DeviceTaintRuleSpec specifies the selector and one taint.
DeviceTaintSelector defines which device(s) a DeviceTaintRule applies to. The empty selector matches all devices. Without a selector, no devices are matched.

If device is set, only devices with that name are selected. This field corresponds to slice.spec.devices[].name.

Setting also driver and pool may be required to avoid ambiguity, but is not required.
If driver is set, only devices from that driver are selected. This fields corresponds to slice.spec.driver.

If pool is set, only devices in that pool are selected.

Also setting the driver name may be useful to avoid ambiguity when different drivers use the same pool name, but this is not required because selecting pools from different drivers may also be useful, for example when drivers with node-local devices use the node name as their pool name.
The device this taint is attached to has the "effect" on any claim which does not tolerate the taint and, through the claim, to pods using the claim.

The effect of the taint on claims that do not tolerate the taint and through such claims on the pods using them.

Valid effects are None, NoSchedule and NoExecute. PreferNoSchedule as used for nodes is not valid here. More effects may get added in the future. Consumers must treat unknown effects like None.
The taint key to be applied to a device. Must be a label name.
Time is a wrapper around time.Time which supports correct marshaling to YAML and JSON.  Wrappers are provided for many of the factory methods that the time package offers.
The taint value corresponding to the taint key. Must be a label value.
DeviceTaintRuleStatus provides information about an on-going pod eviction.

Conditions provide information about the state of the DeviceTaintRule and the cluster at some point in time, in a machine-readable and human-readable format.

The following condition is currently defined as part of this API, more may get added: - Type: EvictionInProgress - Status: True if there are currently pods which need to be evicted, False otherwise
  (includes the effects which don't cause eviction).
- Reason: not specified, may change - Message: includes information about number of pending pods and already evicted pods
  in a human-readable format, updated periodically, may change

For `effect: None`, the condition above gets set once for each change to the spec, with the message containing information about what would happen if the effect was `NoExecute`. This feedback can be used to decide whether changing the effect to `NoExecute` will work as intended. It only gets set once to avoid having to constantly update the status.

Must have 8 or fewer entries.

The last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should reflect when the underlying condition changed, typically represented as a timestamp string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A human-readable message that provides additional details about the current condition, including information about the last transition. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The generation of the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that was last processed by the controller, used to determine whether the status reflects the latest spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A machine-readable, CamelCase reason for the condition's last transition. This provides a stable identifier for the condition state, complementing the human-readable message. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The status of the condition, indicating whether the condition is True, False, or Unknown. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Type is a string that identifies the condition and distinguishes it from other conditions in the status.conditions list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

DeviceClassSpec is used in a [DeviceClass] to define what can be allocated and how to configure it.

Config defines configuration parameters that apply to each device that is claimed via this class. Some classses may potentially be satisfied by multiple drivers, so each instance of a vendor configuration applies to exactly one driver.

They are passed to the driver, but are not considered while allocating the claim.
Provides driver-specific settings for a device class that are opaque to the Kubernetes scheduler. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the name of the driver that owns this opaque device configuration. This driver is responsible for interpreting the corresponding parameters and allocating resources accordingly. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Parameters is an arbitrary JSON object containing driver-specific configuration for this opaque device class configuration. The structure is not defined by Kubernetes and must be interpreted by the device driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

ExtendedResourceName is the extended resource name for the devices of this class. The devices of this class can be used to satisfy a pod's extended resource requests. It has the same format as the name of a pod's extended resource. It should be unique among all the device classes in a cluster. If two device classes have the same name, then the class created later is picked to satisfy a pod's extended resource requests. If two classes are created at the same time, then the name of the class lexicographically sorted first is picked.
Each selector must be satisfied by a device which is claimed via this class.

The CEL selector object, containing a Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that is evaluated against device attributes to determine whether a device matches this selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The CEL expression used to select devices based on their attributes. The expression is evaluated against device attributes, and devices for which it evaluates to true are selected. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

DeviceClaim defines how to request devices with a ResourceClaim.
This field holds configuration for multiple potential drivers which could satisfy requests in this claim. It is ignored while allocating the claim.

Opaque carries driver-specific configuration parameters in a raw object, allowing the device driver to interpret the settings without Kubernetes understanding them. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Specifies the name of the driver that interprets the opaque device configuration parameters. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Arbitrary JSON object containing driver-specific parameters. The cluster does not interpret these parameters; they are passed as-is to the device driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Which of this claim's own device requests this configuration applies to -- every request, when left empty.
These constraints must be satisfied by the set of devices that get allocated for the claim.

The name of a device attribute that all devices selected for the request must have different values for, ensuring the devices are distinct with respect to that attribute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the device attribute this constraint applies to. A device is selected only if it has this attribute with a value matching the constraint's 'value' field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A list of request names that this constraint applies to. If empty, the constraint applies to all requests in the claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Requests represent individual requests for distinct devices which must all be satisfied. If empty, nothing needs to be allocated.
Whether this device request grants the claim admin-level access to the device, bypassing the device's own normal usage restrictions -- only usable in a namespace explicitly labeled to allow it.
How many devices this request needs -- `ExactCount` for a specific `count`, or `All` for every device matching its selectors.
Real, minimum capacity requirements (per named capacity) this request's own matched device(s) must satisfy.
The real, minimum quantity requested for each named device capacity.
How many devices to allocate, when `allocation_mode` is `ExactCount`.
Real, computed attributes (a CEL expression evaluated per allocated device) exposed on the resulting allocation, not present on the device itself.
The real CEL expression computing this derived attribute's own value from the allocated device.
The real name this derived attribute is exposed under on the resulting allocation.
The real DeviceClass this request selects candidate devices from.
An ordered list of DeviceRequest alternatives; the first one that can be satisfied will be allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Real, minimum capacity requirements (per named capacity) this prioritized sub-request's own matched device must satisfy.
The real, minimum quantity requested for each named device capacity.
Number of devices to allocate from the first available devices that match the request's class and selectors. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The real name this derived attribute is exposed under on the resulting allocation.

This is an alternative to the serial selector. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The CEL expression used to select devices that satisfy this request. It is evaluated against each device's attributes and must return true for the device to be matched. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The effect of the taint to match. Valid values are 'NoSchedule', 'PreferNoSchedule', and 'NoExecute'. An empty value matches all taint effects. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. When the operator is 'Exists', the value must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator used to match the taint key. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. Defaults to 'Equal'. When 'Exists' is set, the value must be empty and the toleration matches all taints with the specified key. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The real taint key this toleration matches against.
Whether this toleration matches by exact key/value (`Equal`) or by key presence alone (`Exists`).

DeviceAllocationResult is the result of allocating devices.

This field is a combination of all the claim and class configuration parameters. Drivers can distinguish between those based on a flag.

This includes configuration parameters for drivers which have no allocated devices in the result because it is up to the drivers which configuration parameters they support. They can silently ignore unknown configuration parameters.
Opaque provides driver-specific configuration parameters for the device allocation. It is used when the configuration source is 'FromData'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Driver is used to determine which kubelet plugin needs to be passed these configuration parameters. The driver must be a valid subdomain name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Opaque parameters for this device configuration, passed as a raw extension object. The structure is driver-defined and not interpreted by Kubernetes. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Which of this claim's own device requests this configuration applies to -- every request, when left empty.

Source indicates the origin of the device allocation configuration. Valid values are 'claim' (configuration from the ResourceClaim) and 'driver' (configuration from the driver). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Results lists all allocated devices.
Indicates whether the device was allocated with administrative access. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Real cluster conditions (matching a device's own `binding_conditions`) that must hold before this allocated device is actually usable by the pod.

A list of conditions that describe why the binding of the resource to the claim failed. In the Kubernetes ResourceClaim status, this field is populated with error reasons when the scheduler cannot allocate the requested devices. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The real, actual capacity quantities this allocation consumed from the device's own advertised capacity.
The name of the device that was allocated from the pool for this resource claim, as reported by the resource driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the device driver that provides the allocated device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource pool from which the device was allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the device request that this allocation result corresponds to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
ShareID is a string that uniquely identifies a shared device across multiple resource claims. If the device is not shared, this field is omitted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of node operations that the driver has indicated should be skipped for this allocated device. These operations are normally performed by the kubelet during device preparation, but are skipped for devices that do not require them. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The real tolerations this allocation result was granted under, letting it keep using a device that later gained a matching taint.
The effect of the taint that this toleration matches, such as NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, or NoExecute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The taint key that this toleration applies to. If empty, the toleration matches all taints (requiring operator 'Exists'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator represents a key's relationship to the value. Valid operators are Exists and Equal. If Exists, the value must be empty; if Equal, the value must match the specified value. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The duration in seconds for which the toleration is effective. In Kubernetes, this is used with the NoExecute effect to specify how long a pod can remain on a node after a taint is added. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The value associated with the toleration key. When the operator is 'Equal', this matches the value of the key on the node; it is ignored or empty when the operator is 'Exists' or when the key is empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A node selector represents the union of the results of one or more label queries over a set of nodes; that is, it represents the OR of the selectors represented by the node selector terms.
Required. A list of node selector terms. The terms are ORed.
A list of node selector requirements by node's labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The label key that the selector expression applies to. It must be a valid Kubernetes label key (e.g., 'disktype' or 'kubernetes.io/os'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
values is the list of strings that correspond to the key. For example, if operator is In or NotIn, the key's value must be in (or not in) this list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

match_fields is a list of node selector requirements that specify the node fields (e.g., metadata.name) that must match for a node to be selected by this node selector term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator to apply to the key and values in this match field requirement. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values that the field must match, as part of a node selector term's match field expression. The operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist) determines how these values are interpreted. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Devices contains the status of each device allocated for this claim, as reported by the driver. This can include driver-specific information. Entries are owned by their respective drivers.

The list of conditions representing the latest observed state of the device. Each condition includes the type, status, reason, and message to indicate the device's health status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This timestamp is typically represented in RFC3339 format. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A human-readable message providing details about the current condition of the device in the resource claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

observedGeneration is the .metadata.generation of the ResourceClaim that this condition was observed against, indicating the freshness of the condition relative to the latest generation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Reason is a machine-readable, CamelCase reason for the condition's last transition, providing a stable identifier for the cause of the condition. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The status of the condition, typically 'True', 'False', or 'Unknown'. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The real, named condition type (e.g. whether the device is still healthy and reachable) this status condition reports on.

Arbitrary driver-specific data about the device allocation, as provided by the resource driver. Kubernetes does not interpret this field and it may be used to pass device-specific configuration or status. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The name of the device driver that manages this allocated device, matching the driver specified in the corresponding DeviceClass. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Network information for the allocated device, including its interface name, IP addresses, and MAC address. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The MAC address of the network interface allocated for this resource claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the network interface on the node where this device is allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
List of IP addresses assigned to the network device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource pool (ResourceSlice) from which this device was allocated. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A real, unique identifier for this specific share of a device that supports being allocated to more than one claim at once.

ReservedFor indicates which entities are currently allowed to use the claim. A Pod which references a ResourceClaim which is not reserved for that Pod will not be started. A claim that is in use or might be in use because it has been reserved must not get deallocated.

In a cluster with multiple scheduler instances, two pods might get scheduled concurrently by different schedulers. When they reference the same ResourceClaim which already has reached its maximum number of consumers, only one pod can be scheduled.

Both schedulers try to add their pod to the claim.status.reservedFor field, but only the update that reaches the API server first gets stored. The other one fails with an error and the scheduler which issued it knows that it must put the pod back into the queue, waiting for the ResourceClaim to become usable again.

There can be at most 256 such reservations. This may get increased in the future, but not reduced.
The API group of the resource that reserved this claim. For core resources, this is the empty string; otherwise it is the fully-qualified API group name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the pod that this resource claim is reserved for. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The name of the resource (e.g., a Pod) that holds a reservation for this resource claim, as recorded in the status.reservedFor list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The UID of the consumer (e.g., a Pod) that this ResourceClaim is reserved for. This is part of the ResourceClaimConsumerReference in the reservedFor list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

DeviceTaintRuleSpec specifies the selector and one taint.
DeviceTaintSelector defines which device(s) a DeviceTaintRule applies to. The empty selector matches all devices. Without a selector, no devices are matched.

If device is set, only devices with that name are selected. This field corresponds to slice.spec.devices[].name.

Setting also driver and pool may be required to avoid ambiguity, but is not required.
If driver is set, only devices from that driver are selected. This fields corresponds to slice.spec.driver.

If pool is set, only devices in that pool are selected.

Also setting the driver name may be useful to avoid ambiguity when different drivers use the same pool name, but this is not required because selecting pools from different drivers may also be useful, for example when drivers with node-local devices use the node name as their pool name.
The device this taint is attached to has the "effect" on any claim which does not tolerate the taint and, through the claim, to pods using the claim.

The effect of the taint on claims that do not tolerate the taint and through such claims on the pods using them.

Valid effects are None, NoSchedule and NoExecute. PreferNoSchedule as used for nodes is not valid here. More effects may get added in the future. Consumers must treat unknown effects like None.

DeviceTaintRuleStatus provides information about an on-going pod eviction.

Conditions provide information about the state of the DeviceTaintRule and the cluster at some point in time, in a machine-readable and human-readable format.

The following condition is currently defined as part of this API, more may get added: - Type: EvictionInProgress - Status: True if there are currently pods which need to be evicted, False otherwise
  (includes the effects which don't cause eviction).
- Reason: not specified, may change - Message: includes information about number of pending pods and already evicted pods
  in a human-readable format, updated periodically, may change

For `effect: None`, the condition above gets set once for each change to the spec, with the message containing information about what would happen if the effect was `NoExecute`. This feedback can be used to decide whether changing the effect to `NoExecute` will work as intended. It only gets set once to avoid having to constantly update the status.

Must have 8 or fewer entries.

The last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should reflect when the underlying condition changed, typically represented as a timestamp string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
A human-readable message that provides additional details about the current condition, including information about the last transition. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The generation of the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that was last processed by the controller, used to determine whether the status reflects the latest spec. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A machine-readable, CamelCase reason for the condition's last transition. This provides a stable identifier for the condition state, complementing the human-readable message. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The status of the condition, indicating whether the condition is True, False, or Unknown. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Type is a string that identifies the condition and distinguishes it from other conditions in the status.conditions list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

ReservedFor indicates which entities are currently allowed to use the claim. A Pod which references a ResourceClaim which is not reserved for that Pod will not be started. A claim that is in use or might be in use because it has been reserved must not get deallocated.

In a cluster with multiple scheduler instances, two pods might get scheduled concurrently by different schedulers. When they reference the same ResourceClaim which already has reached its maximum number of consumers, only one pod can be scheduled.

Both schedulers try to add their pod to the claim.status.reservedFor field, but only the update that reaches the API server first gets stored. The other one fails with an error and the scheduler which issued it knows that it must put the pod back into the queue, waiting for the ResourceClaim to become usable again.

There can be at most 256 such reservations. This may get increased in the future, but not reduced.

The UID of the consumer (e.g., a Pod) that this ResourceClaim is reserved for. This is part of the ResourceClaimConsumerReference in the reservedFor list. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

ResourceSliceSpec contains the information published by the driver in one ResourceSlice.

AllNodes indicates that all nodes have access to the resources in the pool.

Exactly one of NodeName, NodeSelector, AllNodes, and PerDeviceNodeSelection must be set.

Devices lists some or all of the devices in this pool.

Must not have more than 128 entries. If any device uses taints or consumes counters the limit is 64.

Only one of Devices and SharedCounters can be set in a ResourceSlice.
Whether this device is available identically on every node in the cluster, rather than being tied to the one node this ResourceSlice is scoped to.

When true, the device may be allocated to multiple ResourceClaims simultaneously; when false or omitted, the device is allocated exclusively to a single claim. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Attributes is a map of device attributes. Each key is the attribute name, and the value is a DeviceAttribute object holding a typed value: one of IntValue (int64), BoolValue (bool), StringValue (string), or VersionValue (string). These attributes describe device properties and are used for device selection in resource claims. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
When set, this device attribute has a boolean value. Only one of bool, int, string, or version may be specified for an attribute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

This device attribute's own real value, when it's a list of semantic versions.

Whether allocating this device also binds the claiming pod to the specific node this ResourceSlice is scoped to.

Real rules constraining how much of this capacity a single request may actually consume, beyond just its own raw quantity.
The real default amount of this capacity a request consumes when it doesn't specify its own explicit amount.
Specifies the allowed range of values for a device capacity request. Requests must fall within this range to be considered valid. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The maximum value (inclusive) in the valid range for the device request policy. This sets the upper limit for the number of devices that can be requested, expressed as a string. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The minimum value allowed in the valid range, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '1', '500m'). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The step size between allowed values in the valid range, specified as a Kubernetes quantity string. Values within the range must be of the form min + N*step, where N is an integer, up to max. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The real, fixed set of amounts a request's own consumption of this capacity is allowed to be, instead of a continuous range.
The quantity of the device capacity, expressed as a Kubernetes resource quantity string (e.g., "1Gi", "500m", "2"). Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

List of counters that this device consumes. Each item represents a counter with a name and a value, indicating the amount of that counter required by the device. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Groups of counter-consuming devices treated as sharing the same real pool -- devices in the same group can't independently double-consume the same counter.
The name of the counter set from which the device consumes counters. This refers to a named set of counters defined by a DRA resource driver. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The real, named counters within the referenced CounterSet, and how much of each this device consumes.

The name of the device, unique within the resource slice. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The label key that this match expression applies to. In Kubernetes node selectors, this is the key of the label that is matched against node labels. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of node selector requirements that match nodes by their fields (e.g., metadata.name). Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and optionally a list of values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The operator defines the relationship between the key and the set of values for the node selector match field. Allowed operators are: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the list of values that the node selector key must match, depending on the operator. For example, with operator 'In', the node must have the key set to one of these values. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
Taints is a list of taints associated with the device. Each taint restricts which nodes can allocate the device, defined by key, value, and effect. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The effect of the taint, indicating how pods that do not tolerate the taint are handled. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The key of the taint, identifying the specific attribute or condition being tainted on the device. It follows the standard Kubernetes taint key format, which may include a DNS subdomain prefix and a name. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The time at which the taint was added, in RFC3339 timestamp format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'). This corresponds to the Kubernetes taint's TimeAdded field. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The value associated with the taint key. This is an optional string that provides additional context for the taint, such as a specific condition or constraint. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Driver identifies the DRA driver providing the capacity information. A field selector can be used to list only ResourceSlice objects with a certain driver name.

Must be a DNS subdomain and should end with a DNS domain owned by the vendor of the driver. It should use only lower case characters. This field is immutable.

NodeName identifies the node which provides the resources in this pool. A field selector can be used to list only ResourceSlice objects belonging to a certain node.

This field can be used to limit access from nodes to ResourceSlices with the same node name. It also indicates to autoscalers that adding new nodes of the same type as some old node might also make new resources available.

Exactly one of NodeName, NodeSelector, AllNodes, and PerDeviceNodeSelection must be set. This field is immutable.
A node selector represents the union of the results of one or more label queries over a set of nodes; that is, it represents the OR of the selectors represented by the node selector terms.
Required. A list of node selector terms. The terms are ORed.

A list of label selector requirements for the node. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The node must satisfy all match expressions to match the selector term. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The label key that this match expression applies to. In a Kubernetes node selector, it identifies the node label that the operator and values are evaluated against. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

Specifies the operator for the match expression, defining how the key and values are compared. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

The list of values that the key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. Must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist operators, matching Kubernetes NodeSelectorRequirement semantics. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name), rather than node labels. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values that a node's field must satisfy to be selected. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The node field key, such as metadata.name or metadata.uid, that the match field requirement applies to. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.
The operator specifies the relationship between the key and value(s) in the match field. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

A list of string values for the match field requirement. The operator determines how these values are used: for In and NotIn, the list must be non-empty; for Exists and DoesNotExist, the list must be empty. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

PartitionTypeAttribute names a string device attribute (by fully qualified name, e.g. "gpu.example.com/profile") whose value labels each device with its partition type, such as "Full" or "Half" for a MIG-style GPU.

When set, every partitionable device in the slice must carry the attribute and devices sharing a value must share the same ConsumesCounters cost.

PerDeviceNodeSelection defines whether the access from nodes to resources in the pool is set on the ResourceSlice level or on each device. If it is set to true, every device defined the ResourceSlice must specify this individually.

Exactly one of NodeName, NodeSelector, AllNodes, and PerDeviceNodeSelection must be set.
ResourcePool describes the pool that ResourceSlices belong to.

Generation tracks the change in a pool over time. Whenever a driver changes something about one or more of the resources in a pool, it must change the generation in all ResourceSlices which are part of that pool. Consumers of ResourceSlices should only consider resources from the pool with the highest generation number. The generation may be reset by drivers, which should be fine for consumers, assuming that all ResourceSlices in a pool are updated to match or deleted.

Combined with ResourceSliceCount, this mechanism enables consumers to detect pools which are comprised of multiple ResourceSlices and are in an incomplete state.

Name is used to identify the pool. For node-local devices, this is often the node name, but this is not required. A field selector can be used to list only ResourceSlice objects belonging to a certain pool.

kubernetes_storage_csidriver.spec.preven.text: preventPodSchedulingIfMissing indicates that the CSI driver wants to prevent pod scheduling if the CSI driver on the node is missing. They must create simulated CSINode objects in addition to Node objects during scheduling simulation, otherwise if PreventPodSchedulingIfMissing is enabled globally for CSIDriver object, any newly created node may be rejected by the scheduler because of missing CSI driver information from the node. This is typical for storage backends that provide volumes as filesystems on block devices or as independent shared volumes. kubernetes_storage_csistorage_capacity.c.text: Quantity is a fixed-point representation of a number. It provides convenient marshaling/unmarshaling in JSON and YAML, in addition to String() and AsInt64() accessors. The serialization format is: ``` <quantity> ::= <signedNumber><suffix> (Note that <suffix> may be empty, from the "" case in <decimalSI>.) <digit> ::= 0 | 1 | ... | 9 <digits> ::= <digit> | <digit><digits> <number> ::= <digits> | <digits>.<digits> | <digits>. | .<digits> <sign> ::= "+" | "-" <signedNumber> ::= <number> | <sign><number> <suffix> ::= <binarySI> | <decimalExponent> | <decimalSI> <binarySI> ::= Ki | Mi | Gi | Ti | Pi | Ei (International System of units; See: http://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Units/binary.html) <decimalSI> ::= m | "" | k | M | G | T | P | E (Note that 1024 = 1Ki but 1000 = 1k; I didn't choose the capitalization.) <decimalExponent> ::= "e" <signedNumber> | "E" <signedNumber> ``` No matter which of the three exponent forms is used, no quantity may represent a number greater than 2^63-1 in magnitude, nor may it have more than 3 decimal places. Numbers larger or more precise will be capped or rounded up. (E.g.: 0.1m will rounded up to 1m.) This may be extended in the future if we require larger or smaller quantities. When a Quantity is parsed from a string, it will remember the type of suffix it had, and will use the same type again when it is serialized. Before serializing, Quantity will be put in "canonical form". This means that Exponent/suffix will be adjusted up or down (with a corresponding increase or decrease in Mantissa) such that: - No precision is lost - No fractional digits will be emitted - The exponent (or suffix) is as large as possible. The sign will be omitted unless the number is negative. Examples: - 1.5 will be serialized as "1500m" - 1.5Gi will be serialized as "1536Mi" Note that the quantity will NEVER be internally represented by a floating point number. That is the whole point of this exercise. Non-canonical values will still parse as long as they are well formed, but will be re-emitted in their canonical form. (So always use canonical form, or don't diff.) This format is intended to make it difficult to use these numbers without writing some sort of special handling code in the hopes that that will cause implementors to also use a fixed point implementation. Optional; if omitted, computed by Kubernetes.

parameters hold volume attributes defined by the CSI driver. These values are opaque to the Kubernetes and are passed directly to the CSI driver. The underlying storage provider supports changing these attributes on an existing volume, however the parameters field itself is immutable. To invoke a volume update, a new VolumeAttributesClass should be created with new parameters, and the PersistentVolumeClaim should be updated to reference the new VolumeAttributesClass. This field is required and must contain at least one key/value pair. The keys cannot be empty, and the maximum number of parameters is 512, with a cumulative max size of 256K. If the deletionTimestamp of the object is non-nil, entries in this list can only be removed. Finalizers may be processed and removed in any order.  Order is NOT enforced because it introduces significant risk of stuck finalizers. finalizers is a shared field, any actor with permission can reorder it.
